knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp uniqueness boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A=(1\ \ 0)\) and \(b=1\), \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^2}\|Ax-b\|_2^2=\{(1,t):t\in\mathbb R\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A design null space produces multiple coefficient vectors with the same fitted value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The least-squares coefficient vector is not unique.
knowledge_statements.title: Rank Deficiency Causes Coefficient Nonuniqueness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric structure of least-squares solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x^\star\) is a least-squares minimizer, then \(b-Ax^\star\perp\operatorname{range}A\), and for every \(x\), \[\|Ax-b\|_2^2=\|Ax^\star-b\|_2^2+\|A(x-x^\star)\|_2^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimal residual is orthogonal to every fitted direction, giving an exact excess-error decomposition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimal residual is orthogonal to \(\operatorname{range}A\), and the displayed identity holds.
knowledge_statements.title: Orthogonality and Pythagorean Error Identity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Complete rank-deficient solution geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(A,b\), \[\operatorname*{argmin}_x\|Ax-b\|_2^2=A^\dagger b+\ker A.\] Every minimizer satisfies \(Ax^\star=AA^\dagger b=P_{\operatorname{range}A}b\), and \(A^\dagger b\) is the unique minimum-Euclidean-norm solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All least-squares solutions share the projection of b onto the column space; the pseudoinverse selects the minimum-norm coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_x\|Ax-b\|_2^2=A^\dagger b+\ker A\) and \(Ax^\star=P_{\operatorname{range}A}b\).
knowledge_statements.title: Pseudoinverse and Projection Representation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional unconstrained linear least squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \[\min_x\tfrac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2\] has a nonempty minimizer set equal to \(\{x:A^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)=0\}\). If \(A\) has full column rank, the unique solution is \((A^{\mathsf T}A)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Least-squares solutions satisfy the normal equations; full column rank gives the unique inverse formula.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_x\|Ax-b\|_2^2=\{x:A^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)=0\}\), with the stated full-rank formula.
knowledge_statements.title: Least-Squares Approximation and Normal Equations

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\|Ax-b\|_2^2\), equivalently \(A^{\mathsf T}Ax^\star=A^{\mathsf T}b\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard finite-dimensional linear least-squares formulation and normal-equation optimality condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional unconstrained linear least squares, including its first-order characterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), least-squares approximation is the convex problem \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\frac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2.\] Its minimizer set is nonempty and equals \[\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:A^{\mathsf T}(Ax-b)=0\}.\] If \(A\) has full column rank, the minimizer is unique and is \(x^\star=(A^{\mathsf T}A)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Least squares minimizes the squared Euclidean residual. Its solutions satisfy the normal equations, and full column rank makes the solution unique.
knowledge_statements.title: Least-Squares Approximation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional least-squares representation, normal equations, existence claim, and full-column-rank formula are mathematically correct, but no inspectable citation is supplied.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed-range least-squares existence and normal-equation characterization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear least-squares approximation for a bounded closed-range operator between real Hilbert spaces.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal H\) and \(\mathcal K\) be real Hilbert spaces, let \(T\in\mathcal B(\mathcal H,\mathcal K)\) have closed range, and let \(y\in\mathcal K\). Then \(\min_{z\in\mathcal H}\|Tz-y\|\) has a solution. For every \(x\in\mathcal H\), the following are equivalent: \(x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\mathcal H}\|Tz-y\|\); \(Tx=P_{\operatorname{ran}T}y\); and \(T^*Tx=T^*y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a bounded operator with closed range between real Hilbert spaces, every right-hand side admits a least-squares solution. A point is a least-squares solution exactly when its image is the metric projection of the right-hand side onto the operator range, equivalently when it satisfies the normal equation.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal H,\mathcal K\text{ are real Hilbert spaces}\)
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{z\in\mathcal H}\|Tz-y\|\neq\varnothing\), and for every \(x\in\mathcal H\), \(x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z}\|Tz-y\|\iff Tx=P_{\operatorname{ran}T}y\iff T^*Tx=T^*y\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes Euclidean residual minimization, existence of normal-equation solutions, and uniqueness under full column rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For A\in\mathbf{R}^{m\times n} and b\in\mathbf{R}^m, minimizing \|Ax-b\|_2 is equivalent to minimizing \|Ax-b\|_2^2. A vector x is optimal if and only if A^TAx=A^Tb. The normal equations always have at least one solution. If \operatorname{rank}(A)=n, the optimizer is unique and equals (A^TA)^{-1}A^Tb.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Least-squares approximation has the same minimizers whether the Euclidean residual norm or its square is minimized. Its minimizers are exactly the solutions of the normal equations, which always have a solution. Full column rank gives the unique usual inverse-form solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_x\|Ax-b\|_2=\operatorname*{argmin}_x\|Ax-b\|_2^2=\{x:A^TAx=A^Tb\}\ne\varnothing;\quad \operatorname{rank}(A)=n\implies \operatorname*{argmin}_x\|Ax-b\|_2^2=\{(A^TA)^{-1}A^Tb\}.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient optimality test for unconstrained LAD fitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A point \(x^\star\) minimizes \(\|Ax-b\|_1\) if and only if there exists \(s\in\mathbb R^m\) with \(A^{\mathsf T}s=0\), where \(s_i=\operatorname{sign}((Ax^\star-b)_i)\) for nonzero residuals and \(s_i\in[-1,1]\) for zero residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An LAD fit is optimal exactly when compatible residual signs balance the design columns.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\|Ax-b\|_1\iff\exists s\in\partial\|Ax^\star-b\|_1\text{ with }A^{\mathsf T}s=0\).

knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even a nonzero one-column design can have an interval of LAD minimizers.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional LAD dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \[\min_x\|Ax-b\|_1=\max_y\{-b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\ \|y\|_\infty\le1\}.\] Both optima are attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The LAD dual uses bounded residual weights orthogonal to every design column.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed primal and dual values are equal and attained.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual of Unconstrained LAD Fitting

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional linear LAD fitting and its exact LP form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) with rows \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\) and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \[\min_x\|Ax-b\|_1=\min_{x,t}\{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}t:-t\le Ax-b\le t,\ t\ge0\}.\] All inequalities are componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: LAD minimizes the sum of absolute residuals and has an exact linear-program formulation.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), its i-th row is \(a_i^{\mathsf T}\), and \(b\in\mathbb R^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_x\|Ax-b\|_1=\min_{x,t}\{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}t:-t\le Ax-b\le t,\ t\ge0\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: Least-Absolute-Deviation Approximation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical scalar LAD specialization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(b_{(1)}\le\cdots\le b_{(m)}\), then the minimizers of \(\sum_i|x-b_i|\) are the middle order statistic for odd \(m\), and the interval \([b_{(m/2)},b_{(m/2+1)}]\) for even \(m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An intercept-only LAD fit is a sample median.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_x\sum_i|x-b_i|\) is the stated median set.
knowledge_statements.title: Median Characterization of Intercept-Only LAD

children.title: Chebyshev Approximation
children.top_down_role: Approximation templates conventionally identified with the Chebyshev formulation.

assumptions_latex: \(K\) is compact, \(f\in C(K)\), and \(V\subset C(K)\) is a finite-dimensional linear subspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{v\in V}\max_{t\in K}|f(t)-v(t)|\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical best uniform approximation of a continuous function from a finite-dimensional subspace.

source_refs.locator: 1.2.1 Best uniform approximation p. 2

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) be compact, let \(f\in C(K)\), and let \(V\subset C(K)\) be a finite-dimensional linear subspace. A Chebyshev approximation to \(f\) from \(V\) is any \(v^\star\in V\) satisfying \[\|f-v^\star\|_\infty=\min_{v\in V}\|f-v\|_\infty,\qquad \|g\|_\infty:=\max_{t\in K}|g(t)|.\] Compactness and finite dimensionality ensure that at least one such best approximation exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A Chebyshev approximation is a member of the approximating subspace that minimizes the largest absolute pointwise error over a compact domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Chebyshev Approximation

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2.1 Best uniform approximation p. 2

assumptions_latex: Every nonzero \(v\in V\) has at most \(m-1\) distinct zeros on \([a,b]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(f\in C([a,b])\) has a unique best uniform approximation from \(V\).

notation.meaning: An m-dimensional Haar or Chebyshev subspace.

review_flags: corrected_builder_counterexample: for f(x)=1 and V=span{x}, the norm is 1+|a|, so the builder's claimed nonuniqueness was false
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness of best uniform approximation from a Haar subspace on an interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the Haar zero-count condition, every continuous target has exactly one best uniform approximant in \(V\). Finite dimensionality alone does not imply uniqueness: on \([-1,1]\), let \(V=\operatorname{span}\{x\}\) and \(f(x)=1-|x|\). For every \(a\in[-1,1]\), \[\|f-a x\|_\infty=1,\] and no smaller error is possible because every \(a x\) vanishes at \(x=0\) while \(f(0)=1\). Hence all \(a x\), \(|a|\le1\), are best approximants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Haar subspaces give unique Chebyshev approximants, whereas a general finite-dimensional subspace can have many best approximants.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Haar Uniqueness and Its Failure Boundary
knowledge_statements.title: Haar Uniqueness and Its Failure Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifies affine uniform-norm fitting as a minimax model and gives its equivalent epigraph linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For A\in\mathbf{R}^{m\times n} and b\in\mathbf{R}^m, the Chebyshev approximation problem is \min_{x\in\mathbf{R}^n}\|Ax-b\|_\infty=\min_x\max_{1\le i\le m}|(Ax-b)_i|. It is equivalent to the linear program \min_{x\in\mathbf{R}^n,\,t\in\mathbf{R}}t subject to -t\mathbf{1}\preccurlyeq Ax-b\preccurlyeq t\mathbf{1}.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Chebyshev approximation minimizes the largest absolute affine residual and is therefore a minimax approximation model. A scalar residual bound gives an equivalent linear program with two-sided componentwise inequalities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_x\|Ax-b\|_\infty=\min_{x,t}\{t:-t\mathbf{1}\preccurlyeq Ax-b\preccurlyeq t\mathbf{1}\}.

children.title: Uniform-Norm Approximation
children.top_down_role: Templates organized around worst-case residual magnitude.

assumptions_latex: \(K\) is compact and each residual map \(r_x:K\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous.
\(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is a nonempty convex feasible set, and \(x\mapsto r_x(t)\) is affine for every \(t\in K\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in X}\|r_x\|_\infty=\min_{x\in X,\,\tau\in\mathbb{R}}\{\tau:-\tau\le r_x(t)\le\tau\ \forall t\in K\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex epigraph form of continuous uniform-residual minimization.

source_refs.locator: 1.4.1 Uniform approximation p. 30

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and convex, let \(K\) be compact, and suppose \(r_x\in C(K)\) with \(x\mapsto r_x(t)\) affine for every \(t\in K\). Then uniform-norm approximation \[\min_{x\in X}\max_{t\in K}|r_x(t)|\] has the equivalent convex semi-infinite epigraph form \[\min_{x\in X,\,\tau\in\mathbb{R}}\tau\quad\text{subject to}\quad -\tau\le r_x(t)\le\tau\quad\text{for every }t\in K.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform-norm fitting minimizes the worst absolute residual and is equivalently expressed by one scalar bound imposed at every point of the domain.
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform-Norm Approximation

source_witnesses.locator: 1.4.1 Uniform approximation p. 30

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of attainment despite convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=(0,\infty)\), \(K=\{0\}\), and \(r_x(0)=x\). Then \(\inf_{x\in X}\|r_x\|_\infty=0\), but the infimum is not attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convexity alone does not guarantee a best uniform fit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in X}\|r_x\|_\infty=0\) and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\|r_x\|_\infty=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Nonattainment Without Closedness or Coercivity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite sampled specialization of uniform fitting with affine residuals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(r_i(x)=a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i\), \(i=1,\ldots,m\), and polyhedral \(X\), \[\min_{x\in X}\max_i|r_i(x)|=\min_{x\in X,\tau}\{\tau:-\tau\le a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i\le\tau\ \forall i\},\] which is a linear program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Finite affine uniform approximation with polyhedral side constraints is a linear program.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The finite uniform-fitting problem has the displayed linear-program representation.

notation.meaning: Common bound on all absolute residuals.

knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Domain Linear-Program Form

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment under joint continuity and compactness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(X\) and \(K\) are nonempty compact spaces and \((x,t)\mapsto r_x(t)\) is continuous on \(X\times K\), then \(F(x)=\max_{t\in K}|r_x(t)|\) is continuous and attains its minimum on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint continuity and compactness guarantee existence of a best uniform fit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\max_{t\in K}|r_x(t)|\neq\varnothing\).

children.title: Equioscillation Interface
children.top_down_role: Structural optimality patterns used to interpret uniform approximation solutions.

assumptions_latex: A basis of an \(m\)-dimensional Haar space on \([a,b]\) and an ordered reference set of \(m+1\) distinct points are available.
A global maximizer of the current absolute residual can be computed at each exchange step.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Equality between the global residual maximum and the reference amplitude terminates with an exact best approximation.
review_flags: No universal iteration-complexity claim is made without a specified exchange rule, extremum oracle, and regularity assumptions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Remez exchange interface and exact termination certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A Remez exchange iteration solves \[f(t_i)-v(t_i)=\sigma(-1)^iE_R\quad(i=0,\ldots,m)\] for \(v\in V\) and \(E_R\), finds \(s\in\operatorname*{argmax}_{t\in[a,b]}|f(t)-v(t)|\), and exchanges a reference point while retaining the ordered alternating pattern. If \(|f(s)-v(s)|=|E_R|\), the reference points are global alternating extrema and the alternation theorem certifies that \(v\) is best. Alternation only on the reference set is insufficient when \(|f(s)-v(s)|>|E_R|\). For polynomial spaces the reference system has size \(n+2\), but no universal iteration bound follows without further assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Remez exchange repeatedly repairs an alternating reference set and terminates exactly when no larger residual exists outside that set.
knowledge_statements.title: Remez Exchange and Stopping Certificate

assumptions_latex: \(V\subset C([a,b])\) is an \(m\)-dimensional Haar subspace, \(a<b\), and \(f\in C([a,b])\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(v^\star\) is best if and only if its residual reaches its uniform norm with alternating signs at \(m+1\) ordered points.

notation.meaning: Dimension of the Haar approximation space.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Alternation theorem for finite-dimensional Haar subspaces on a nondegenerate compact interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A function \(v^\star\in V\) is the unique best uniform approximation to \(f\) if and only if there exist \(a\le t_0<\cdots<t_m\le b\) and \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\) such that \[f(t_i)-v^\star(t_i)=\sigma(-1)^iE,\qquad i=0,\ldots,m.\] For \(V=\mathcal P_n\), \(m=n+1\), giving the classical \(n+2\)-point polynomial alternation certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: In an m-dimensional Haar space, best uniform approximation is exactly certified by m+1 ordered alternating extrema.
knowledge_statements.title: Haar-Space Alternation Theorem

assumptions_latex: \(f\in C([a,b])\), and \(\mathcal P_n\) is the space of real polynomials of degree at most \(n\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p^\star\) is best in \(\|\cdot\|_\infty\) if and only if its error alternates with equal magnitude at at least \(n+2\) ordered points.

notation.meaning: Polynomial approximating space of degree at most n.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical polynomial Chebyshev alternation theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical alternation certificate for polynomial approximation on a compact interval.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f\in C([a,b])\) and \(p^\star\in\mathcal P_n\), where \(\mathcal P_n\) denotes the real polynomials of degree at most \(n\). Set \(e=f-p^\star\) and \(E=\|e\|_\infty\). Then \(p^\star\) is a best uniform approximation to \(f\) from \(\mathcal P_n\) if and only if there exist \(a\le t_0<t_1<\cdots<t_{n+1}\le b\) and \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\) such that \[e(t_i)=\sigma(-1)^iE\quad\text{for }i=0,\ldots,n+1.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A degree-n polynomial is uniformly best exactly when its maximum error is attained with alternating signs at at least n+2 ordered points.
knowledge_statements.title: Equioscillation Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is appropriately a certificate, but the exact alternation theorem lacks a source. Its hypotheses should also explicitly require a nondegenerate interval a<b and n to be a nonnegative integer.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the unique solution and associated dual multiplier for the squared Euclidean least-norm problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbf R^{m\times n}\) satisfy \(\operatorname{rank}A=m<n\), and let \(b\in\mathbf R^m\). The problems \[\min_{Ax=b}\|x\|_2\qquad\text{and}\qquad\min_{Ax=b}\|x\|_2^2\] have the same unique solution. For the squared formulation, the optimality conditions \[2x^\star+A^T\nu^\star=0,\qquad Ax^\star=b\] yield \[\nu^\star=-2(AA^T)^{-1}b,\qquad x^\star=A^T(AA^T)^{-1}b,\] where \(AA^T\) is invertible because \(A\) has full row rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a full-row-rank underdetermined system, minimizing the Euclidean norm, equivalently its square, gives a unique solution. The primal-dual optimality equations yield x star equal to A transpose times the inverse of A A transpose times b, with dual multiplier minus twice that inverse times b.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^\star=A^T(AA^T)^{-1}b\text{ is unique},\qquad \nu^\star=-2(AA^T)^{-1}b.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines minimum-norm solutions of consistent linear equations and records the square and underdetermined full-row-rank regimes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a norm \(\|\cdot\|\) on \(\mathbf R^n\), \(A\in\mathbf R^{m\times n}\), and \(b\in\mathbf R^m\), the least-norm problem is \[\min_{x\in\mathbf R^n}\ \|x\|\quad\text{subject to }Ax=b.\] This is a convex optimization problem. If \(\{x:Ax=b\}\neq\varnothing\), a minimizer exists and is called a least-norm solution of \(Ax=b\). For a consistent system, redundant equations may be removed to obtain an equivalent representation with \(\operatorname{rank}A=m\le n\). If \(m=n\), then \(A\) is invertible and the sole feasible point is \(A^{-1}b\); the nontrivial full-row-rank case is \(m<n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A least-norm solution minimizes a chosen norm of x among all solutions of Ax=b. A minimizer exists whenever the equations are consistent. Redundant equations in a consistent system can be removed to give a full-row-rank representation. In the square full-rank case the sole feasible point is A inverse b; the nontrivial case is underdetermined.
assumptions_latex: \{x\in\mathbf R^n:Ax=b\}\neq\varnothing\text{ for the existence and rank-reduction assertions}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{Ax=b}\|x\|\neq\varnothing;\qquad \operatorname{rank}A=m=n\Longrightarrow x^\star=A^{-1}b.

children.title: Least-Norm Approximation
children.top_down_role: Approximation templates minimizing a selected residual norm.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General convex first-order certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty closed convex \(X\), a feasible \(x^\star\) minimizes \(\|Ax-b\|\) if and only if \[0\in A^{\mathsf T}\partial\|Ax^\star-b\|+N_X(x^\star).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A least-norm fit is optimal exactly when a norm subgradient balances a feasible-set normal.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\|Ax-b\|\iff0\in A^{\mathsf T}\partial\|Ax^\star-b\|+N_X(x^\star)\).

notation.meaning: Convex normal cone to X at the candidate.

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Least-Norm Optimality Condition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard sufficient conditions for existence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(X\) is nonempty and closed, then \(\inf_{x\in X}\|Ax-b\|\) is attained whenever \(X\) is compact or the objective has compact sublevel sets on \(X\); coercivity on \(X\) is a sufficient condition for the latter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Compactness or coercivity on a closed feasible set guarantees a least-norm solution.
assumptions_latex: Either \(X\) is compact or \(x\mapsto\|Ax-b\|\) has compact sublevel sets on \(X\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\|Ax-b\|\neq\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Attainment Conditions for Least-Norm Fitting

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Closed Convex Feasibility Does Not Ensure Attainment
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp existence boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=\{(u,v)\in\mathbb R^2:v\ge e^u\}\), \(A=(0\ \ 1)\), and \(b=0\). Then \(X\) is closed and convex and \(\inf_{(u,v)\in X}|v|=0\), but no feasible point attains the infimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A closed convex feasible set alone need not guarantee a least-norm solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in X}\|Ax-b\|=0\) and \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}\|Ax-b\|=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.title: Closed Convex Feasibility Does Not Ensure Attainment

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional convex approximation under an arbitrary residual norm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and convex, \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\|\cdot\|\) a norm on \(\mathbb R^m\). Least-norm approximation minimizes \(\|Ax-b\|\) over \(X\). The objective is convex; the term “solution” additionally requires attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Least-norm approximation minimizes the size of an affine residual in a selected norm.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\|\cdot\|\) is a norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\inf_{x\in X}\|Ax-b\|\) is a convex optimization problem, and any attaining point is a least-norm approximation.
knowledge_statements.title: Least-Norm Approximation

children.title: Minimax Approximation
children.top_down_role: Approximation templates controlling the largest indexed loss.

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\) are nonempty compact convex sets.
\(\phi:X\times U\to\mathbb{R}\) is continuous, convex in \(x\), and concave in \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in X}\max_{u\in U}\phi(x,u)=\max_{u\in U}\min_{x\in X}\phi(x,u)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compact finite-dimensional convex-concave minimax formulation with zero duality gap.

source_refs.locator: 5.5.1. Minimax Duality Theorems p. 200

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) and \(U\subseteq\mathbb{R}^q\) be nonempty compact convex sets, and let \(\phi:X\times U\to\mathbb{R}\) be continuous, convex in \(x\), and concave in \(u\). The minimax approximation value is \[v=\min_{x\in X}\max_{u\in U}\phi(x,u).\] Under these hypotheses, minimax duality gives \[\min_{x\in X}\max_{u\in U}\phi(x,u)=\max_{u\in U}\min_{x\in X}\phi(x,u),\] and both extrema are attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a continuous convex-concave payoff on compact convex sets, minimizing the worst case equals maximizing the best guaranteed value.
knowledge_statements.title: Minimax Approximation

source_witnesses.locator: 5.5.1. Minimax Duality Theorems p. 200

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality certificate under the seed's compact convex-concave hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the accepted minimax theorem's hypotheses, \((x^\star,u^\star)\) is a saddle point exactly when \[\phi(x^\star,u)\le\phi(x^\star,u^\star)\le\phi(x,u^\star)\quad\forall x\in X,\ u\in U.\] Such a pair simultaneously solves the min-max and max-min problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Mutual best responses certify primal and dual minimax optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(X,U\), and \(\phi\) satisfy the compact continuous convex-concave hypotheses of the accepted seed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed saddle inequalities are equivalent to joint min-max and max-min optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Saddle-Point Characterization

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimax Gap on Nonconvex Strategy Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of minimax equality without convexification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X=U=\{-1,1\}\) and \(\phi(x,u)=xu\). Then \[\min_{x\in X}\max_{u\in U}\phi(x,u)=1>-1=\max_{u\in U}\min_{x\in X}\phi(x,u).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonconvex pure-strategy sets can produce a strict minimax gap even for a bilinear payoff.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_x\max_u\phi=1>-1=\max_u\min_x\phi\).
knowledge_statements.title: Minimax Gap on Nonconvex Strategy Sets

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconditional relation and boundary of minimax equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every real-valued \(\phi:X\times U\to\mathbb R\) on nonempty sets, \[\sup_{u\in U}\inf_{x\in X}\phi(x,u)\le\inf_{x\in X}\sup_{u\in U}\phi(x,u).\] Equality and attainment require additional hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The max-min value never exceeds the min-max value, but equality is not automatic.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and \(U\) are nonempty and \(\phi\) is real-valued.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_u\inf_x\phi(x,u)\le\inf_x\sup_u\phi(x,u)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Weak Minimax Inequality

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-index worst-loss formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\phi_i:X\to\mathbb R\), \[\inf_{x\in X}\max_{1\le i\le m}\phi_i(x)=\inf_{x\in X,t}\{t:\phi_i(x)\le t\ \forall i\}.\] If \(X\) and all \(\phi_i\) are convex, this is a convex problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite worst-case objective uses one epigraph bound for every indexed loss.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The finite minimax objective has the displayed epigraph representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Minimax Epigraph Form

children.title: Norm-Duality Interface
children.top_down_role: Connections between norm selection, worst-case interpretations, and certificate structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Norm-Duality Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional support-function representation linking least-norm and minimax formulations without assuming attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\|\cdot\|\) be a norm on \(\mathbb{R}^m\), and define its dual norm by \[\|y\|_*:=\sup_{\|z\|\le 1}\langle y,z\rangle.\] Then every \(r\in\mathbb{R}^m\) satisfies \[\|r\|=\max_{\|y\|_*\le 1}\langle y,r\rangle.\] Consequently, for any \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and nonempty \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\), \[\inf_{x\in X}\|Ax-b\|=\inf_{x\in X}\max_{\|y\|_*\le 1}\langle y,Ax-b\rangle.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A norm is the support function of its dual unit ball. Thus any least-norm residual objective has an equivalent pointwise minimax representation, whether or not an optimizer is attained.
assumptions_latex: \(\|\cdot\|\) is a norm on \(\mathbb{R}^m\), with dual norm \(\|\cdot\|_*\).
\(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty for the fitting representation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|r\|=\max_{\|y\|_*\le 1}\langle y,r\rangle\) for every \(r\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and hence \(\inf_{x\in X}\|Ax-b\|=\inf_{x\in X}\max_{\|y\|_*\le 1}\langle y,Ax-b\rangle\).

notation.meaning: Primal norm on the residual space.
Residual, primal test vector, and dual vector, respectively.
Linear fitting map, observation vector, and nonempty parameter set.

source_refs.locator: 5.3. Convex Programming Duality p. 167

source_witnesses.locator: 5.3. Convex Programming Duality p. 167

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Dual Certificate for an Unconstrained Least-Norm Fit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equality conditions for primal-dual optimality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A pair \((x^\star,y^\star)\) is primal-dual optimal exactly when \[A^{\mathsf T}y^\star=0,\qquad \|y^\star\|_*\le1,\qquad \langle y^\star,Ax^\star-b\rangle=\|Ax^\star-b\|.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimality is certified by a dual-unit vector that annihilates the design range and supports the norm at the residual.
assumptions_latex: \(A,b\), and the norm are as in unconstrained least-norm fitting.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed feasibility and support-equality conditions are necessary and sufficient for primal-dual optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual Certificate for an Unconstrained Least-Norm Fit

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimization dual induced by the accepted support-function interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and any norm \(\|\cdot\|\), \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\|Ax-b\|=\max_y\{-b^{\mathsf T}y:A^{\mathsf T}y=0,\ \|y\|_*\le1\}.\] Both optima are attained.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distance to the range of A equals the largest dual-unit separation by a vector annihilating that range.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\|\cdot\|\) is a norm.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed primal and dual values are equal and attained.
knowledge_statements.title: Dual of Unconstrained Least-Norm Approximation

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Support Representation Does Not Imply Minimax Interchange
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between pointwise norm representation and zero-gap interchange.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The accepted identity \(\inf_{x\in X}\|Ax-b\|=\inf_{x\in X}\max_{\|y\|_*\le1}\langle y,Ax-b\rangle\) is pointwise. Replacing its right side by \(\max_{\|y\|_*\le1}\inf_{x\in X}\langle y,Ax-b\rangle\) requires separate minimax or convex-duality hypotheses and can fail for nonconvex \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Writing a norm as a maximum is automatic; interchanging that maximum with minimization is a separate theorem.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\), with no convexity or compactness assumed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The pointwise support identity does not alone justify exchanging \(\inf\) and \(\max\).
knowledge_statements.title: Support Representation Does Not Imply Minimax Interchange

children.title: Regularized-Robust Fitting Regime Family
children.top_down_role: Application views of fitting templates whose penalty and robust-counterpart constructions have primary homes elsewhere in A08.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Semidefinite Quadratic Penalties Need Not Ensure Uniqueness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between scalar ridge and general Tikhonov regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\tfrac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|Lx\|_2^2\), positive \(\lambda\) does not imply strong convexity when \(L\) is rank deficient. If \(\ker A\cap\ker L\ne\{0\}\), the Hessian is singular and minimizers are not unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Quadratic regularization cannot identify directions invisible to both the data and the penalty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\ker A\cap\ker L\ne\{0\}\Rightarrow A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda L^{\mathsf T}L\text{ is singular and uniqueness fails}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Semidefinite Quadratic Penalties Need Not Ensure Uniqueness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Singular-value action of scalar ridge.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\), then \[x_\lambda=V\operatorname{diag}\!\left(\frac{\sigma_i}{\sigma_i^2+\lambda}\right)U^{\mathsf T}b.\] Thus ridge filters each singular direction and shifts the normal-matrix eigenvalues by \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ridge suppresses poorly determined singular directions and shifts every curvature eigenvalue upward.
assumptions_latex: \(A=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\) is an SVD and \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The ridge solution has the displayed spectral-filter representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Ridge Spectral Shrinkage

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained scalar ridge fitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\lambda>0\), \[\min_x\tfrac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\tfrac\lambda2\|x\|_2^2\] is strongly convex and has the unique solution \[x^\star=(A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda I)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}b.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive squared coefficient penalty makes least squares strongly convex and uniquely solvable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star=(A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda I)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}b\) is the unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Ridge-Regularized Least Squares

knowledge_statements.statement_title: General Tikhonov and Augmented Least-Squares Forms
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-valued quadratic regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(L\in\mathbb R^{p\times n}\) and \(\lambda>0\), \[\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\lambda\|Lx\|_2^2=\left\|\begin{bmatrix}A\\ \sqrt\lambda L\end{bmatrix}x-\begin{bmatrix}b\\0\end{bmatrix}\right\|_2^2.\] Its minimizers satisfy \((A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda L^{\mathsf T}L)x=A^{\mathsf T}b\), and the minimizer is unique exactly when \(\ker A\cap\ker L=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tikhonov regularization is ordinary least squares on an augmented design; uniqueness excludes common data and penalty null directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented representation and stated normal equation hold, with uniqueness iff \(\ker A\cap\ker L=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.title: General Tikhonov and Augmented Least-Squares Forms

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint behavior of the scalar ridge path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x_\lambda=(A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda I)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}b\), \[\lim_{\lambda\downarrow0}x_\lambda=A^\dagger b,\qquad\lim_{\lambda\to\infty}x_\lambda=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Vanishing ridge selects the minimum-norm least-squares solution, while dominant ridge shrinks coefficients to zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x_\lambda\to A^\dagger b\) as \(\lambda\downarrow0\), and \(x_\lambda\to0\) as \(\lambda\to\infty\).
knowledge_statements.title: Ridge Regularization Limits

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star=(A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda I)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}b\) is the unique minimizer.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard ridge or Tikhonov-regularized least-squares formula
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unconstrained ridge-regularized linear least squares with positive scalar regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(\lambda>0\), quadratically regularized fitting solves \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\frac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\frac{\lambda}{2}\|x\|_2^2.\] The objective is strongly convex, so it has the unique minimizer determined by \[(A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda I)x^\star=A^{\mathsf T}b,\] namely \(x^\star=(A^{\mathsf T}A+\lambda I)^{-1}A^{\mathsf T}b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Ridge fitting adds a positive squared parameter penalty to least squares, producing a strongly convex problem with a unique closed-form solution.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratically Regularized Fitting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ridge objective, strong-convexity claim, normal equation, and unique closed-form minimizer are correct for lambda>0, but no inspectable citation is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact all-zero certificate for unconstrained lasso.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F_\lambda(x)=\tfrac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\lambda\|x\|_1\), \[0\in\operatorname*{argmin}F_\lambda\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\|A^{\mathsf T}b\|_\infty\le\lambda.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The zero vector is optimal exactly when every feature-response correlation is bounded by the penalty weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=0\) is optimal if and only if \(\lambda\ge\|A^{\mathsf T}b\|_\infty\).

notation.meaning: Threshold \(\|A^{\mathsf T}b\|_\infty\) for the zero solution.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Solution Threshold

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel dual of unconstrained least-squares lasso.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\min_x\tfrac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\lambda\|x\|_1=\max_{\|A^{\mathsf T}u\|_\infty\le\lambda}\left(-\tfrac12\|u\|_2^2-b^{\mathsf T}u\right).\] Both optima are attained, and optimal pairs satisfy \(u^\star=Ax^\star-b\) and \(-A^{\mathsf T}u^\star\in\lambda\partial\|x^\star\|_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lasso dual maximizes a quadratic over residual vectors with bounded design correlations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed primal and dual have equal attained values and satisfy the stated primal-dual relations.
knowledge_statements.title: Lasso Residual Dual

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment, a standard sufficient uniqueness condition, and a rank-deficient nonuniqueness family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every \(\lambda>0\), the lasso objective is coercive and therefore attains a minimum. If \(A\) has full column rank, its quadratic term is strictly convex and the minimizer is unique. Rank deficiency does not force nonuniqueness, but it permits it: for \(A=[1\;1]\), \(b>\lambda>0\), every \((x_1,x_2)\ge0\) with \(x_1+x_2=b-\lambda\) is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lasso always attains a solution; full column rank guarantees uniqueness, while rank-deficient designs can have a continuum of solutions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A minimizer always exists; full column rank is sufficient for uniqueness, and the displayed rank-deficient family is nonunique.
knowledge_statements.title: Existence and Uniqueness Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Closed-form lasso solution for orthonormal design columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A^{\mathsf T}A=I_n\), the unique lasso minimizer is \[x^\star=S_\lambda(A^{\mathsf T}b),\qquad S_\lambda(t)=\operatorname{sign}(t)(|t|-\lambda)_+\] componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With orthonormal columns, lasso is componentwise soft thresholding of the least-squares correlations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star=S_\lambda(A^{\mathsf T}b)\) is the unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Orthonormal-Design Soft Thresholding

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\) minimizes \(\frac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\lambda\|x\|_1\) if and only if \(0\in A^{\mathsf T}(Ax^\star-b)+\lambda\partial\|x^\star\|_1\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard lasso objective and subgradient optimality condition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Lasso-type linear fitting and its exact convex optimality condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb{R}^m\), and \(\lambda>0\), sparsity-regularized fitting solves \[\min_{x\in\mathbb{R}^n}\frac12\|Ax-b\|_2^2+\lambda\|x\|_1.\] A vector \(x^\star\) is optimal if and only if \[0\in A^{\mathsf T}(Ax^\star-b)+\lambda\partial\|x^\star\|_1.\] Componentwise, this means \(a_j^{\mathsf T}(Ax^\star-b)=-\lambda\operatorname{sign}(x_j^\star)\) when \(x_j^\star\ne0\), and \(|a_j^{\mathsf T}(Ax^\star-b)|\le\lambda\) when \(x_j^\star=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lasso balances squared residual error against an l1 penalty; its subgradient condition identifies both active and zero coefficients.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparsity-Regularized Fitting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The lasso optimality condition and componentwise characterization are correct, but no citation is supplied and a_j should be explicitly identified as the j-th column of A.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable finite convex residual losses over a closed convex parameter set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F(x)=\sum_{i=1}^m\ell_i(a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i)\), where every \(\ell_i:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is convex. For nonempty closed convex \(X\), \(x^\star\in X\) minimizes \(F\) over \(X\) if and only if there are \(g_i\in\partial\ell_i(a_i^{\mathsf T}x^\star-b_i)\) such that \[0\in A^{\mathsf T}g+N_X(x^\star).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimality holds exactly when residual scores balance through the design matrix and the feasible-set normal cone.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
Each \(\ell_i:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\) is finite and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\) is optimal if and only if \(0\in A^{\mathsf T}g+N_X(x^\star)\) for suitable residual subgradients \(g_i\).
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Score Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical convex loss with a bounded residual score.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\delta>0\), \[h_\delta(t)=\begin{cases}\tfrac12t^2,&|t|\le\delta,\\ \delta|t|-\tfrac12\delta^2,&|t|>\delta.\end{cases}\] It is convex and continuously differentiable, with \(h_\delta'(t)=t\) for \(|t|\le\delta\) and \(h_\delta'(t)=\delta\operatorname{sign}(t)\) otherwise; hence \(|h_\delta'(t)|\le\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Huber loss is quadratic near zero and linear for large residuals, with a bounded derivative.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h_\delta\) is convex, continuously differentiable, and has derivative bounded by \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.title: Huber Residual Loss

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel dual of unconstrained finite convex residual fitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finite convex \(f(r)=\sum_i\ell_i(r_i)\), \[\inf_x f(Ax-b)=\sup_{A^{\mathsf T}u=0}\{-b^{\mathsf T}u-f^*(u)\}.\] If a primal minimizer \(x^\star\) exists, a dual maximizer can be chosen with \(u^\star\in\partial f(Ax^\star-b)\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}u^\star=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The dual chooses balanced residual scores and penalizes them through the loss conjugate.
assumptions_latex: \(f:\mathbb R^m\to\mathbb R\) is finite and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed primal and dual values agree; attained primal solutions admit balanced optimal residual scores.

notation.meaning: Convex conjugate of the aggregate residual loss.

knowledge_statements.title: Separable Residual-Fitting Dual

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Basic existence and limits of rank- and score-based robustness claims.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If every \(\ell_i\) is lower semicontinuous and coercive and \(A\) has full column rank, then \(x\mapsto\sum_i\ell_i(a_i^{\mathsf T}x-b_i)\) is coercive and attains its minimum. If \(0\ne d\in\ker A\), the objective is constant on each line \(x+\mathbb Rd\), so an attained minimizer is not unique. Moreover, bounded scalar residual scores alone do not imply bounded influence under arbitrary perturbations of the design rows; leverage must be controlled separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full rank and coercive losses ensure existence, a design nullspace prevents uniqueness, and bounded residual scores do not by themselves control high-leverage observations.
assumptions_latex: Each \(\ell_i\) is lower semicontinuous and coercive for the existence assertion.
\(A\) has full column rank for the coercivity assertion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated conditions ensure attainment; nullspace directions obstruct uniqueness, and bounded residual score is not a leverage-robustness guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: Existence, Nullspace, and Leverage Boundaries

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear-program representation of finite-dimensional least-absolute-deviation fitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \[\min_x\|Ax-b\|_1=\min_{x,t}\left\{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}t:-t\le Ax-b\le t\right\}.\] The inequalities imply \(t_i\ge |(Ax-b)_i|\), and equality may be imposed at an optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Least-absolute-deviation fitting is a linear program using one absolute-residual bound per observation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The least-absolute-deviation problem equals the displayed linear program.
knowledge_statements.title: Least-Absolute-Deviation LP

assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) is nonempty and convex, and \(r:X\to\mathbb{R}^m\) is affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in X}\rho(r(x))\) is a convex fitting problem; bounded influence requires bounded subgradients of the scalar residual loss.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard convex robust M-estimation template
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic convex robust-loss template; no single residual loss is imposed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb{R}^n\) be nonempty and convex, let \(r:X\to\mathbb{R}^m\) be affine, and let \(\rho:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) be proper, closed, and convex. Robust residual fitting uses the convex template \[\min_{x\in X}\rho(r(x)).\] For a separable loss \(\rho(z)=\sum_{i=1}^m\ell(z_i)\), resistance to arbitrarily large individual residuals is expressed by bounded subgradients: there exists \(M<\infty\) such that \(|g|\le M\) for every \(s\in\mathbb{R}\) and \(g\in\partial\ell(s)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robust fitting minimizes a convex residual loss. For separable losses, uniformly bounded subgradients limit the effect of any single extreme residual.
knowledge_statements.title: Robust Residual Fitting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The convex-composition template is correct, but the asserted connection between bounded scalar subgradients and resistance or influence requires a precise robustness notion and authoritative support.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: First-Order Certificate for a Supported Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualified convex optimality condition for weighted fitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be closed and convex and let \(f,g\) be proper convex functions. If the subdifferential sum rule holds, then \(x^\star\in X\) minimizes \(f+\lambda g\), \(\lambda>0\), exactly when \[0\in\partial f(x^\star)+\lambda\partial g(x^\star)+N_X(x^\star).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A supported tradeoff is certified when weighted objective subgradients balance a feasible-set normal.
assumptions_latex: \(f,g\) are proper convex and a subdifferential sum-rule qualification holds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inclusion is necessary and sufficient for weighted-sum optimality.
knowledge_statements.title: First-Order Certificate for a Supported Tradeoff

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Weighted Sums Can Miss Nonsupported Pareto Points
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure outside convex attainable objective geometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y=\{(0,2),(1,3/2),(2,0)\}\). All three vectors are Pareto optimal for componentwise minimization, but \((1,3/2)\) minimizes no positive weighted sum \(w_1y_1+w_2y_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonconvex attainable objective set can contain Pareto points invisible to every positive weighted sum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((1,3/2)\) is Pareto optimal but unsupported by positive weights.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Sums Can Miss Nonsupported Pareto Points

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pareto consequence and supported-point converse.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be nonempty and let \(f,g:X\to\mathbb R\). Every minimizer of \(f+\lambda g\) with \(\lambda>0\) is Pareto optimal for componentwise minimization of \((f,g)\). Conversely, any attainable Pareto point whose upper image admits a supporting hyperplane with a strictly positive normal solves a positive weighted-sum problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive weighted sums produce Pareto-optimal tradeoffs, and strictly supported Pareto points arise from suitable weights.
assumptions_latex: For the converse, the attainable upper image has a strictly positive supporting normal at the Pareto point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\in\operatorname*{argmin}_X(f+\lambda g)\Rightarrow x^\star\text{ is Pareto optimal}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Positive Weighted-Sum Tradeoffs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Comparative statics for exact weighted-sum minimizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(0\le\lambda_1<\lambda_2\), and choose \(x_i\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X}[f(x)+\lambda_i g(x)]\). Then \[g(x_2)\le g(x_1),\qquad f(x_1)\le f(x_2).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing the penalty weight cannot worsen the selected penalty value or improve the selected fitting loss.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity Along Weighted Tradeoffs

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical alternative scalarization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a budget \(\gamma\), the epsilon-constraint scalarization is \[\min_{x\in X}f(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad g(x)\le\gamma.\] Every Pareto-optimal \(\bar x\) solves this problem for \(\gamma=g(\bar x)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraining one criterion and minimizing the other recovers each Pareto point at its achieved budget.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar x\text{ Pareto optimal}\Rightarrow\bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{f(x):x\in X,\ g(x)\le g(\bar x)\}.\)
knowledge_statements.title: Epsilon-Constraint Tradeoff Form

assumptions_latex: \(X\) is nonempty and convex, and \(f,g:X\to\mathbb{R}\) are convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^\star\) is weakly Pareto optimal for the objective pair \((f,g)\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard weighted-sum scalarization property in convex multiobjective optimization
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weighted-sum scalarization of two convex fitting objectives and its Pareto implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\) be nonempty and convex, and let \(f,g:X\to\mathbb{R}\) be convex objectives representing fit and regularization or robustness. For \(\lambda>0\), every solution of \[\min_{x\in X} f(x)+\lambda g(x)\] is weakly Pareto optimal: there is no \(y\in X\) satisfying \(f(y)<f(x^\star)\) and \(g(y)<g(x^\star)\). If \(X\), \(f\), and \(g\) are convex and an attainable Pareto point admits a supporting hyperplane with strictly positive normal, that point solves such a weighted problem for some \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive weighted sum of fit and regularization yields a weakly Pareto-optimal tradeoff; supported Pareto points arise from suitable weights.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiobjective Fitting Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Positive weighted-sum solutions are indeed weakly Pareto optimal, and the qualified supported-point converse is plausible under the stated supporting-hyperplane condition, but neither claim has an inspectable citation.

assumptions_latex: \(L:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) and \(R:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) are proper closed convex functions, and the subdifferential sum and affine-chain rules hold at the point considered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\beta^\star\) is optimal if and only if \(0\in\Phi^\top\partial L(\Phi\beta^\star-y)+\partial R(\beta^\star)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite design-matrix form and optimality conditions for convex basis fitting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The basis fit is \(\min_\beta L(\Phi\beta-y)+R(\beta)\), and \(\beta^\star\) is optimal exactly when \[0\in\Phi^\top\partial L(\Phi\beta^\star-y)+\partial R(\beta^\star).\] A minimizer exists when the objective is proper and level-bounded. It is unique when the full objective is strictly convex, for example when \(R\) is strongly convex. When \(R=0\) and \(\ker\Phi\ne\{0\}\), coefficients need not be unique because \(\beta\) and \(\beta+h\) produce identical fitted values for every \(h\in\ker\Phi\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The design matrix converts basis fitting to a convex composite problem whose subgradient inclusion certifies optimality; level-boundedness, curvature, and rank govern existence and identifiability.
knowledge_statements.title: Design-Matrix Optimality and Identifiability

assumptions_latex: The observations satisfy \(x_i\in\mathcal X\) and \(y_i\in\mathbb R\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\).
The basis functions \(\phi_j:\mathcal X\to\mathbb R\) are fixed, and \(L_i:\mathbb R\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) and \(R:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) are proper convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \[\min_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}\ \sum_{i=1}^n L_i\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^p\beta_j\phi_j(x_i)-y_i\right)+R(\beta)\] is a convex optimization problem in \(\beta\).

notation.meaning: Coefficient vector for the fitted basis expansion.
Convex regularizer or extended-valued coefficient constraint.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this fitting template; an authoritative approximation or convex-optimization source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional fitting with fixed basis functions and convex loss and regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given fixed basis functions \(\phi_1,\ldots,\phi_p\), represent the fitted function by \(f_\beta(x)=\sum_{j=1}^p\beta_j\phi_j(x)\). For data \((x_i,y_i)_{i=1}^n\), convex residual losses \(L_i\), and a convex extended-valued regularizer \(R\), basis-function fitting has the finite-dimensional representation \[\underset{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad \sum_{i=1}^n L_i\bigl(f_\beta(x_i)-y_i\bigr)+R(\beta).\] Because each \(f_\beta(x_i)-y_i\) is affine in \(\beta\), the displayed objective is convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed basis turns function fitting into convex optimization over coefficients whenever the residual losses and coefficient regularizer are convex.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Function Fitting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-dimensional convex fitting representation is mathematically sound and the content kind fits the leaf, but no inspectable citation or locator supports it.

assumptions_latex: The sites \(x_1,\ldots,x_n\in\mathbb R^d\), values \(y_1,\ldots,y_n\in\mathbb R\), and vectors \(g_i\) satisfy \(y_j\ge y_i+g_i^\top(x_j-x_i)\) for all \(i,j\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_0(x)=\max_i\{y_i+g_i^\top(x-x_i)\}\) is the pointwise least convex function having \(f_0(x_i)=y_i\) and the assigned \(g_i\) as subgradients.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimality and consistency properties of the supporting-plane interpolant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For feasible supporting slopes, \[f_0(x)=\max_i\{y_i+g_i^\top(x-x_i)\}\] is finite, polyhedral, and convex, with \(f_0(x_i)=y_i\) and \(g_i\in\partial f_0(x_i)\). If another convex function \(h\) has the same values and satisfies \(g_i\in\partial h(x_i)\) for every \(i\), then \(h(x)\ge f_0(x)\) for every \(x\). If \(x_i=x_j\) but \(y_i\ne y_j\), no function can interpolate the data; equal-valued duplicate sites may be merged for value-only interpolation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasible supporting planes generate the least convex interpolant consistent with those assigned planes, while unequal values at a duplicate site make interpolation impossible.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimal Polyhedral Interpolant and Duplicate-Site Boundary
knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Polyhedral Interpolant and Duplicate-Site Boundary

assumptions_latex: The interpolation sites \(x_1,,x_n\) lie in a convex set \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^d\), and prescribed values are \(y_1,,y_n\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A finite convex interpolant exists exactly when the displayed vectors \(g_i\) exist; then \(f(x)=\max_i\{y_i+g_i^\top(x-x_i)\}\) is one such interpolant.

notation.meaning: Interpolation sites and prescribed function values.
Candidate subgradient at the interpolation site \(x_i\).
Polyhedral convex interpolant constructed from supporting affine functions.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the finite convex interpolation criterion; a precise convex-analysis source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact interpolation by a finite-valued polyhedral convex function on a convex domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The data \((x_i,y_i)_{i=1}^n\) admit a finite-valued convex interpolant on \(D\) if and only if there exist vectors \(g_i\in\mathbb R^d\) satisfying \[y_j\ge y_i+g_i^\top(x_j-x_i)\qquad\text{for every }i,j.\] When these inequalities hold, \[f(x)=\max_{1\le i\le n}\bigl\{y_i+g_i^\top(x-x_i)\bigr\}\] is convex on \(D\) and satisfies \(f(x_i)=y_i\) for every \(i\). The feasibility inequalities are linear in the unknown subgradients \((g_i)_{i=1}^n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convex interpolation is feasible exactly when every datum admits a supporting affine function lying below all other data values.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Interpolation Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The interpolation criterion requires a precise convex-analysis source. The assumptions also contain malformed ranges (“x_1,,x_n” and “y_1,,y_n”), which should be corrected when sourced.

assumptions_latex: Observations are ordered \(x_1\le\cdots\le x_n\), weights satisfy \(w_i>0\), and responses are \(y_i\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Weighted least-squares monotone fitting is projection onto the order cone and is solved exactly by PAVA.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Total-order weighted least-squares isotonic regression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Isotonic regression solves \[\min_{\theta_1\le\cdots\le\theta_n}\frac12\sum_{i=1}^n w_i(\theta_i-y_i)^2.\] Its feasible set is a closed convex cone and the positive weights make the optimizer unique. The pool-adjacent-violators algorithm starts with singleton blocks, repeatedly merges adjacent blocks whose weighted means violate monotonicity, and assigns each final block its weighted mean. A stack implementation returns the exact optimizer in \(O(n)\) time.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted isotonic regression is projection onto an order cone, and PAVA computes its unique solution in linear time.
knowledge_statements.title: Isotonic Regression and PAVA

assumptions_latex: A basis model \(f_\beta(x)=\sum_j\beta_j\phi_j(x)\) is defined on a continuum domain \(D\).
A desired shape restriction is expressed by affine or affine-semidefinite inequalities in \(\beta\) indexed by every \(x\in D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact feasible set is convex but is generally semi-infinite; finitely sampled shape inequalities need not certify the domain-wide restriction.

notation.meaning: Coefficient vector of the fitted basis expansion.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tractability boundary for domain-wide coefficient-based shape restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Constraints such as \(\nabla f_\beta(x)\ge0\) or \(\nabla^2f_\beta(x)\succeq0\) for every \(x\in D\) define a convex set of coefficients because their left sides depend affinely on \(\beta\). They are nevertheless generally semi-infinite. Enforcing them only at finitely many sampled points does not in general imply the restriction between sample points. An exact finite convex formulation therefore requires additional structure, such as a basis and domain admitting a finite conic certificate; otherwise discretization is an approximation rather than an exact shape certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Domain-wide shape constraints remain convex in basis coefficients but may be semi-infinite, and finite sampling alone generally does not certify the shape everywhere.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuum Shape-Constraint Boundary

assumptions_latex: Sites \(x_i\in\mathbb R^d\), responses \(y_i\in\mathbb R\), and a proper convex loss \(L:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite-sample convex regression is a convex program in fitted values and supporting slopes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noisy finite-sample fitting under a global convexity restriction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Convex regression on sampled sites has the finite formulation \[\min_{\theta_i,g_i}L(\theta-y)\quad\text{subject to}\quad \theta_j\ge\theta_i+g_i^\top(x_j-x_i)\quad\forall i,j.\] Every feasible solution extends to \(f(x)=\max_i\{\theta_i+g_i^\top(x-x_i)\}\). Fixed monotonicity, convexity, or derivative-sign restrictions define convex feasible sets. By contrast, requiring a sequence to be unimodal while optimizing over an unknown mode gives a finite union of order cones and is generally nonconvex unless the mode is fixed or explicitly enumerated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noisy convex regression uses fitted values and supporting slopes in a finite convex program; fixed shape regimes are convex, while an unknown regime change generally is not.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite Convex Regression and Regime Boundary
knowledge_statements.title: Finite Convex Regression and Regime Boundary

assumptions_latex: The fitted model is \(f_\beta(x)=\sum_{j=1}^p\beta_j\phi_j(x)\) with fixed twice differentiable basis functions on a convex domain \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^d\).
The data-fit loss \(\mathcal L:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) and regularizer \(R:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) are proper convex functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The shape-restricted estimator is obtained by minimizing \(\mathcal L(\beta)+R(\beta)\) over the convex feasible set \(\{\beta:A\beta\le b,\ \sum_j\beta_j\nabla^2\phi_j(x)\succeq0\ \forall x\in D\}\).

notation.meaning: Linear coefficient restrictions encoding finite shape constraints such as sampled monotonicity.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this general shape-restricted fitting formulation; specialized sourcing is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex fitting with affine and semidefinite shape constraints on basis coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A shape-restricted basis fit can be written as \[\underset{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad \mathcal L(\beta)+R(\beta)\qquad\text{subject to}\qquad A\beta\le b,\quad \sum_{j=1}^p\beta_j\nabla^2\phi_j(x)\succeq0\quad\text{for all }x\in D.\] The affine inequalities may encode finite monotonicity, sign, or bound restrictions, while the semidefinite inequalities impose convexity of \(f_\beta\). Their intersection is convex in \(\beta\), so the estimator remains a convex optimization problem, although the domain-wide constraint may be semi-infinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shape restrictions preserve convexity when they become affine or semidefinite constraints on the coefficients of a fixed basis expansion.
knowledge_statements.title: Shape-Restricted Fitting

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and content kind fit shape-restricted basis fitting, but the domain-wide Hessian constraint and claimed convex formulation lack an inspectable specialized source.

children.top_down_role: Application interpretation and selection boundary; the reusable Lasso formulation is primary in Regularized Learning Formulation Templates.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Limit-point optimality of block-coordinate minimization for separable composite convex objectives
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convergence theorem for block-coordinate minimization of a convex differentiable term plus convex block-separable terms, including qualifying nonsmooth regularizers.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^{(0)}\in\mathcal X\), and let \(S_0=\{x:f_0(x)\leq f_0(x^{(0)})\}\). Assume that \(S_0\) is compact and \(S_0\subseteq\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}f_0)\). If \(f_0(x)=\phi(x)+\sum_{i=1}^{\nu}\psi_i(x_i)\), where \(\phi\) is convex and differentiable on \(S_0\) and each \(\psi_i\) is convex, then every limit point of the sequence generated by BCM is an optimal solution of problem (12.90). The result applies to \(\ell_1\)-regularized problems such as LASSO when these hypotheses hold.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the initial sublevel set is compact and lies in the interior of the objective's domain, and the objective is a convex differentiable function plus convex block-separable terms, every limit point of the block-coordinate minimization sequence is optimal. Qualifying l1-regularized problems, including LASSO, satisfy this result.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{Every limit point of the BCM sequence is an optimal solution of problem (12.90).}

source_evidence.locator: Introduction to algorithms / 12. Introduction to algorithms / Theorem 12.5

source_refs.locator: Introduction to algorithms / 12. Introduction to algorithms / Theorem 12.5
