children.title: Penalized Lasso Interface
children.top_down_role: Lasso applications exposed through a loss-plus-penalty representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient optimality conditions for normalized penalized Lasso.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda>0\), \(\widehat\beta\) minimizes \(F_\lambda(\beta)=(2n)^{-1}\|y-X\beta\|_2^2+\lambda\|\beta\|_1\) if and only if there is \(z\in\mathbb R^p\) such that \[\frac1nX^T(X\widehat\beta-y)+\lambda z=0,\qquad z_j=\operatorname{sign}(\widehat\beta_j)\ \text{if }\widehat\beta_j\ne0,\quad |z_j|\le1\ \text{if }\widehat\beta_j=0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coefficient vector is Lasso-optimal exactly when its residual correlations balance an l1 subgradient coordinatewise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in n^{-1}X^T(X\widehat\beta-y)+\lambda\partial\|\widehat\beta\|_1.

notation.meaning: l1-norm subgradient at the candidate coefficient vector

knowledge_statements.title: Penalized-Lasso KKT Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel dual of normalized squared-loss Lasso.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda>0\), the dual is \[\max_{\theta\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{y^T\theta-\frac n2\|\theta\|_2^2:\ \|X^T\theta\|_\infty\le\lambda\right\}.\] Strong duality holds. For every primal point \(\beta\) and dual-feasible \(\theta\), the primal-dual gap upper-bounds primal suboptimality. At optimality, \(\theta=(y-X\beta)/n\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lasso dual constrains residual correlations, and every feasible primal-dual gap certifies objective accuracy.
assumptions_latex: The primal loss is normalized by \(1/(2n)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F_\lambda(\beta)-\left(y^T\theta-\frac n2\|\theta\|_2^2\right)\ge F_\lambda(\beta)-F_\lambda^\star\ge0.
knowledge_statements.title: Residual-Correlation Dual and Gap Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Attainment distinction between positive and zero penalty levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\lambda>0\), then \(F_\lambda(\beta)\ge\lambda\|\beta\|_1\), so \(F_\lambda\) is coercive and has a nonempty compact minimizer set. If \(\lambda=0\), ordinary least squares still attains its minimum because \(\operatorname{range}(X)\) is closed, but its minimizer set is unbounded whenever \(\ker X\ne\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive l1 regularization makes the objective coercive; unregularized least squares still attains its minimum but can have an unbounded solution set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda>0\Rightarrow\operatorname*{argmin}F_\lambda\text{ is nonempty and compact};\quad\lambda=0\Rightarrow\operatorname*{argmin}F_0\ne\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Existence and Coercivity Regimes

assumptions_latex: The response is \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), the design matrix is \(X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\), and \(\lambda\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The penalized Lasso estimator set is \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}\{(2n)^{-1}\|y-X\beta\|_2^2+\lambda\|\beta\|_1\}\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the Lasso definition and normalization convention; a statistical-learning source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Squared-loss Lasso with the explicit \(1/(2n)\) normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), \(X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\), and \(\lambda\ge0\), the penalized Lasso solution set is \[\widehat B_\lambda=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}\left\{\frac{1}{2n}\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2^2+\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\right\}.\] Any \(\widehat\beta_\lambda\in\widehat B_\lambda\) is a penalized Lasso estimator. The objective is convex and coercive only in directions not simultaneously invisible to both \(X\) and the \(\ell_1\)-norm; nevertheless, in finite dimensions its nonempty compact sublevel structure ensures that a minimizer exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalized Lasso minimizes normalized squared residual error plus a nonnegative multiple of the coefficient l1 norm.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalized Lasso Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The defining optimization problem is standard, but it has no citation. The added existence explanation is also inaccurate: for lambda>0 the l1 penalty is coercive, whereas for lambda=0 nullspace directions can make sublevel sets noncompact even though least-squares minimizers still exist.

children.title: Constrained Lasso Interface
children.top_down_role: Lasso applications exposed through an explicit sparsity-budget representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact optimality certificate for squared-loss Lasso with an l1 budget, including the zero-radius endpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A feasible \(\widehat\beta\) solves \(\min_{\|\beta\|_1\le t}(2n)^{-1}\|y-X\beta\|_2^2\) if and only if there exist \(\lambda\ge0\) and \(z\in\partial\|\widehat\beta\|_1\) such that \(n^{-1}X^\top(X\widehat\beta-y)+\lambda z=0\) and \(\lambda(\|\widehat\beta\|_1-t)=0\). For \(t>0\) this follows from Slater regularity; for \(t=0\), feasibility forces \(\widehat\beta=0\), and a sufficiently large \(\lambda\) supplies the same certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Feasibility, l1-subgradient stationarity, a nonnegative multiplier, and complementary slackness exactly certify constrained-Lasso optimality for every nonnegative radius.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac1nX^\top(X\widehat\beta-y)+\lambda z=0,\qquad \lambda(\|\widehat\beta\|_1-t)=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Constrained-Lasso KKT Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution-set property distinguishing prediction uniqueness from coefficient uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: All constrained-Lasso minimizers have the same fitted value \(X\widehat\beta\), even when their coefficient vectors differ. If \(X\) has full column rank, the squared loss is strictly convex in \(\beta\), so the coefficient vector is unique. Rank deficiency can permit nonuniqueness: with \(X=(1,1)\), \(y=1\), and \(t\ge1\), every nonnegative \(\beta\) satisfying \(\beta_1+\beta_2=1\) is optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constrained-Lasso predictions are always unique; full column rank makes coefficients unique, while duplicated columns can produce a continuum of coefficient solutions.
assumptions_latex: The constrained-Lasso solution set is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat\beta_1,\widehat\beta_2\in\widehat B_t^{\mathrm c}\Longrightarrow X\widehat\beta_1=X\widehat\beta_2.
knowledge_statements.title: Fitted-Value and Coefficient Uniqueness

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-dimensional QP representation of constrained Lasso.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The constraint \(\|\beta\|_1\le t\) is equivalent to the existence of \(u\in\mathbb R_+^p\) satisfying \(-u\le\beta\le u\) and \(\mathbf1^\top u\le t\). Hence constrained Lasso is the convex quadratic program minimizing \((2n)^{-1}\|y-X\beta\|_2^2\) subject to these linear inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonnegative absolute-value auxiliaries convert constrained Lasso exactly into a convex quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|\beta\|_1\le t\iff\exists u\ge0:\ -u\le\beta\le u,\ \mathbf1^\top u\le t.
knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Program Epigraph Form

assumptions_latex: The response is \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), the design matrix is \(X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\), and the radius is \(t\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constrained Lasso estimator set is \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{\|\beta\|_1\le t}(2n)^{-1}\|y-X\beta\|_2^2\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the constrained Lasso definition and normalization convention; a statistical-learning source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Squared-loss Lasso expressed through an explicit \(\ell_1\)-budget constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), \(X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\), and \(t\ge0\), the constrained Lasso solution set is \[\widehat B^{\mathrm c}_t=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}\left\{\frac{1}{2n}\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2^2:\lVert\beta\rVert_1\le t\right\}.\] Any \(\widehat\beta_t\in\widehat B^{\mathrm c}_t\) is a constrained Lasso estimator. The feasible set is nonempty, compact, and convex, and the squared-loss objective is continuous and convex, so the solution set is nonempty and convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constrained Lasso minimizes normalized squared residual error over coefficients whose l1 norm does not exceed a prescribed budget.
knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Lasso Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constrained Lasso definition and existence statement are correct and appropriately classified, but no source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Lasso Parameter-Correspondence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes governing correspondence between penalty levels and constraint budgets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Endpoint regime of the penalized squared-loss Lasso path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(\beta)=(2n)^{-1}\|y-X\beta\|_2^2\), the zero vector solves \(\min_\beta f(\beta)+\lambda\|\beta\|_1\) if and only if \(\lambda\ge\lambda_{\max}:=n^{-1}\|X^\top y\|_\infty\). Thus every \(\lambda\ge\lambda_{\max}\) corresponds to the constrained endpoint \(t=0\), so the parameter map is not generally injective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every penalty at or above the maximal score norm yields the zero solution and corresponds to the same zero budget.
assumptions_latex: Any intercept is absent, fixed, or separately profiled out.
The squared loss is normalized by \(1/(2n)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in\operatorname*{argmin}_\beta\{f(\beta)+\lambda\|\beta\|_1\}\iff\lambda\ge\frac1n\|X^\top y\|_\infty.

notation.meaning: Smallest penalty for which zero is optimal

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Solution Penalty Threshold

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Constrained Value Function and Multiplier Slopes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value-function description of Lasso penalty-budget correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(v(t)=\inf\{f(\beta):\|\beta\|_1\le t\}\). Then \(v\) is nonincreasing and convex on \([0,\infty)\). At a budget \(t>0\), every optimal multiplier \(\lambda^\star\ge0\) satisfies \(-\lambda^\star\in\partial v(t)\). Conversely, a supporting slope \(-\lambda\in\partial v(t)\) yields a common solution of the constrained problem at \(t\) and the penalized problem \(\min_\beta f(\beta)+\lambda\|\beta\|_1\). Corners and affine portions of \(v\) produce set-valued parameter correspondence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The constrained value is decreasing and convex, and negative optimal multipliers are its subgradients; nonsmooth or affine regions create nonunique parameter mappings.
assumptions_latex: \(t>0\), so the l1-budget problem satisfies Slater regularity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: -\lambda^\star\in\partial v(t).

notation.meaning: Optimal loss at l1 budget t

knowledge_statements.title: Constrained Value Function and Multiplier Slopes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary where constrained solutions correspond only to the unpenalized endpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If a constrained optimum \(\widehat\beta\) satisfies \(\|\widehat\beta\|_1<t\), complementary slackness forces every associated optimal multiplier to equal zero. Hence an inactive budget corresponds to unpenalized least squares, not to a strictly positive penalty. Conversely, every penalized optimum with \(\lambda>0\) matches the active budget \(t=\|\widehat\beta\|_1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slack l1 budgets have only the zero multiplier and correspond to unpenalized least squares; positive penalties match active budgets.
assumptions_latex: The KKT conditions hold for the constrained problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|\widehat\beta\|_1<t\Longrightarrow\lambda^\star=0.
knowledge_statements.title: Inactive-Budget and Zero-Multiplier Regime

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every penalized solution at \(\lambda\) solves the constrained problem at its own radius; conversely, an active constrained solution corresponds to any nonnegative optimal multiplier.
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the exact set-valued correspondence and multiplier qualifications; a convex-duality or Lasso source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued penalty-constraint correspondence, including nonunique parameters and solutions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\widehat\beta\) minimizes \(f(\beta)+\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\) for \(\lambda>0\), then with \(t=\lVert\widehat\beta\rVert_1\), the same \(\widehat\beta\) minimizes \(f\) subject to \(\lVert\beta\rVert_1\le t\). Conversely, if \(\widehat\beta\) solves the constrained problem, its constraint is active, and \(\lambda\ge0\) is an optimal Lagrange multiplier, then \(\widehat\beta\) minimizes \(f(\beta)+\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\). The correspondence between \(t\) and \(\lambda\) need not be one-to-one when minimizers or multipliers are nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Penalized and constrained Lasso share solutions when the radius equals the solution norm and the penalty is a valid constraint multiplier.
knowledge_statements.title: Lasso Parameter-Correspondence Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set-valued penalty–constraint correspondence is plausible and appropriately classified as duality, but its multiplier qualifications and nonuniqueness caveat require an authoritative, specifically located source.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-knot path geometry under a nondegenerate uniqueness regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume the Lasso solution is unique for every \(\lambda>0\), every encountered active matrix \(X_A\) has full column rank, and only one predictor enters or leaves at each knot. Between knots, \[\widehat\beta_A(\lambda)=(X_A^TX_A)^{-1}(X_A^Ty-n\lambda s_A),\qquad \widehat\beta_{A^c}(\lambda)=0.\] Thus the coefficient and fitted-value paths are continuous and piecewise affine. A LARS/Lasso homotopy method follows each affine segment from \(\lambda_{\max}\) to the next entry or deletion event.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under standard nondegeneracy, the Lasso path is continuous and piecewise affine and can be traversed by homotopy.
assumptions_latex: The minimizer is unique for every \(\lambda>0\).
Every encountered \(X_A\) has full column rank.
Only one entry or deletion occurs at each knot.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda\mapsto\widehat\beta(\lambda)\text{ is continuous and piecewise affine and is traversed knot by knot.}

notation.meaning: active predictor set on a path segment

knowledge_statements.title: Piecewise-Affine Homotopy Path

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case output complexity of exact Lasso homotopy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(p\) predictors, each nondegenerate affine path segment is associated with a signed active pattern in \(\{-1,0,1\}^p\), giving the finite bound \(N_{\rm seg}\le3^p\). There are design and response families with unique Lasso paths whose numbers of segments grow exponentially in \(p\). Consequently, exact knot-by-knot homotopy has finite output-sensitive complexity but no polynomial worst-case bound in the number of predictors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The exact Lasso path is finite, but it can contain exponentially many affine segments.
assumptions_latex: The path is in the nondegenerate unique-solution regime.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\rm seg}\le3^p,\qquad \sup_{X,y}N_{\rm seg}=2^{\Omega(p)}.

notation.meaning: number of affine segments in the regularization path

knowledge_statements.title: Exponential Path-Complexity Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Zero-model endpoint and monotonic objective-component behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lambda_{\max}=\|X^Ty\|_\infty/n\). Then \(0\in\widehat B_\lambda\) for \(\lambda\ge\lambda_{\max}\), and zero is the unique minimizer for \(\lambda>\lambda_{\max}\). If \(0\le\lambda_1<\lambda_2\) and \(\widehat\beta_k\in\widehat B_{\lambda_k}\), then \[\|\widehat\beta_2\|_1\le\|\widehat\beta_1\|_1,\qquad \|y-X\widehat\beta_1\|_2^2\le\|y-X\widehat\beta_2\|_2^2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Above the maximal correlation knot the zero model is optimal; increasing the penalty cannot increase the selected l1 norm or improve training loss.
assumptions_latex: A minimizer is chosen at each penalty level.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lambda\ge\lambda_{\max}\Rightarrow0\in\widehat B_\lambda;\quad\lambda\uparrow\Rightarrow\|\widehat\beta\|_1\downarrow,\ \|y-X\widehat\beta\|_2^2\uparrow.

notation.meaning: smallest penalty for which zero is Lasso-optimal

knowledge_statements.title: Path Endpoint and Monotonic Tradeoff

assumptions_latex: The response and design are fixed as \(y\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The regularization path is the set-valued map \(\lambda\mapsto\widehat B_\lambda\), with \(\widehat B_\lambda=\operatorname*{argmin}_\beta\{(2n)^{-1}\|y-X\beta\|_2^2+\lambda\|\beta\|_1\}\).

notation.meaning: Penalized Lasso solution set at penalty level lambda.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the path definition and uniqueness distinctions; a Lasso-path source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-valued coefficient path, distinguished from the uniquely determined fitted-value path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Lasso regularization-path interface is the set-valued map \[\mathcal P:[0,\infty)\rightrightarrows\mathbb R^p,\qquad \mathcal P(\lambda)=\widehat B_\lambda=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}\left\{\frac{1}{2n}\lVert y-X\beta\rVert_2^2+\lambda\lVert\beta\rVert_1\right\}.\] A single-valued coefficient path requires a specified selection rule whenever \(\widehat B_\lambda\) is not a singleton. Although coefficients can be nonunique, all members of \(\widehat B_\lambda\) have the same fitted value \(X\widehat\beta\), so \(\lambda\mapsto X\widehat B_\lambda\) is single-valued.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lasso path maps each penalty to its solution set; coefficients may be nonunique even though fitted values are unique.
knowledge_statements.title: Lasso Regularization-Path Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The set-valued path definition and uniqueness distinction are mathematically appropriate, but the claim that fitted values are unique for every penalty level requires a specifically located Lasso source.

children.title: Lasso Variable-Support Selection
children.top_down_role: Application-facing support-selection behavior across sparse regression regimes.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient certificate for a proposed Lasso signed support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix \(S\subseteq[p]\) and \(s\in\{-1,1\}^{S}\). A vector \(\widehat\beta\) has support \(S\), signs \(s\), and is Lasso-optimal if and only if \[\widehat\beta_{S^c}=0,\quad \operatorname{sign}(\widehat\beta_S)=s,\quad \frac1nX_S^T(y-X_S\widehat\beta_S)=\lambda s,\quad \left\|\frac1nX_{S^c}^T(y-X_S\widehat\beta_S)\right\|_\infty\le\lambda.\] Strict inactive inequality together with full column rank of \(X_S\) makes this signed-support solution unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact signed support is certified by active correlation equalities, inactive inequalities, requested signs, and zero coefficients off support.
assumptions_latex: A candidate support \(S\) and sign vector \(s\) are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{supp}(\widehat\beta)=S\text{ and }\operatorname{sign}(\widehat\beta_S)=s\text{ exactly under the displayed KKT system.}
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Signed-Support KKT Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact deterministic signed-support regime in the noiseless model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(y=X\beta^\star\), \(S=\operatorname{supp}(\beta^\star)\), \(s=\operatorname{sign}(\beta_S^\star)\), and \(C=X^TX/n\), with \(C_{SS}\) nonsingular. Put \(d=C_{SS}^{-1}s\). If \[\|C_{S^cS}d\|_\infty<1\quad\text{and}\quad \operatorname{sign}(\beta_S^\star-\lambda d)=s,\] then the unique Lasso solution is \(\widehat\beta_S=\beta_S^\star-\lambda d\), \(\widehat\beta_{S^c}=0\). Conversely, if \(\|C_{S^cS}d\|_\infty>1\), no positive \(\lambda\) preserving active signs \(s\) can recover that signed support.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict irrepresentability and beta-min sign preservation give noiseless signed recovery; violation beyond one makes that sign pattern impossible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|C_{S^cS}C_{SS}^{-1}s\|_\infty<1\text{ and sign preservation}\Rightarrow\operatorname{sign}(\widehat\beta)=\operatorname{sign}(\beta^\star).
knowledge_statements.title: Noiseless Irrepresentable Signed-Recovery Regime

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic noise conditions and their stochastic consistency consequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: In \(y=X\beta^\star+\varepsilon\), retain \(S,s,C,d\) from the noiseless regime and let \(P_S=X_S(X_S^TX_S)^{-1}X_S^T\). Suppose \(\|C_{S^cS}d\|_\infty\le1-\eta\) for some \(\eta>0\). If \[\left\|\frac1nX_{S^c}^T(I-P_S)\varepsilon\right\|_\infty<\lambda\eta\] and \[\min_{j\in S}|\beta_j^\star|>\left\|C_{SS}^{-1}\frac{X_S^T\varepsilon}{n}\right\|_\infty+\lambda\|d\|_\infty,\] then the unique Lasso solution has signed support \((S,s)\). Along a stochastic sequence, if these two displayed events have probability tending to one, signed-support selection is consistent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under strict irrepresentability, projected-noise control and a beta-min bound yield noisy signed recovery and a direct selection-consistency criterion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Pr(\operatorname{sign}(\widehat\beta)=\operatorname{sign}(\beta^\star))\to1\text{ whenever the displayed noise and beta-min events hold with probability }1-o(1).

notation.meaning: orthogonal projector onto the span of active predictors

knowledge_statements.title: Noisy Signed-Selection Consistency Regime

assumptions_latex: The linear model is \(y=X\beta^\star+\varepsilon\), with true support \(S=\{j:\beta_j^\star\ne0\}\).
A Lasso estimator \(\widehat\beta_\lambda\) is computed with \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact signed-support selection is the event \(\operatorname{sign}(\widehat\beta_\lambda)=\operatorname{sign}(\beta^\star)\); exact support selection is \(\operatorname{supp}(\widehat\beta_\lambda)=S\).

notation.meaning: Support of the true coefficient vector.
Indices selected by the Lasso estimator.
Componentwise sign vector, with zero mapped to zero.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this selection criterion or its distinction from prediction; a variable-selection source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample definitions of exact support and signed-support recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(S=\operatorname{supp}(\beta^\star)\) and \(\widehat S_\lambda=\operatorname{supp}(\widehat\beta_\lambda)\), exact variable-support selection occurs when \[\widehat S_\lambda=S.\] Exact signed-support selection, the stronger condition, occurs when \[\operatorname{sign}(\widehat\beta_\lambda)=\operatorname{sign}(\beta^\star).\] In a stochastic model these become recovery events, and selection consistency means that the probability of the relevant event tends to one along a specified sequence of sample sizes, designs, noise distributions, signals, and penalty levels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lasso exactly selects variables when its nonzero coefficient indices equal the true support; signed recovery additionally requires every recovered sign to match.
knowledge_statements.title: Lasso Variable-Support Selection

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-sample support and signed-support recovery conditions fit the node, but no variable-selection source with an inspectable locator is provided.

children.title: Lasso Coefficient Identifiability
children.top_down_role: Design regimes affecting uniqueness or interpretability of fitted coefficients.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact characterization of all coefficient solutions from the common fitted value.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\lambda>0\), let \(\widehat y=X\widehat\beta\) be the fitted value common to all minimizers, define \(z=X^T(y-\widehat y)/(n\lambda)\), and let \(E=\{j:|z_j|=1\}\). Then \[\widehat B_\lambda=\{\beta:\beta_{E^c}=0,\ X_E\beta_E=\widehat y,\ z_E\odot\beta_E\ge0\}.\] Hence the coefficients are identifiable exactly when this polyhedron is a singleton. Full column rank of \(X_E\) is sufficient for uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All Lasso solutions form one sign-restricted affine system over the equicorrelation set; uniqueness is exactly singletonness of that system.
assumptions_latex: The penalized Lasso uses normalized squared loss.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat B_\lambda=\{\beta:\beta_{E^c}=0,\ X_E\beta_E=\widehat y,\ z_E\odot\beta_E\ge0\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Equicorrelation-Set Uniqueness Characterization

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coefficient vector is identifiable precisely when \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}F_\lambda(\beta)\) is a singleton; full column rank of \(X\) is sufficient.

notation.meaning: Fitted response associated with a minimizer.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the exact Lasso uniqueness criterion; a source treating coefficient uniqueness is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample identifiability as uniqueness of the penalized Lasso coefficient vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Lasso coefficients are identifiable at \(\lambda\) when \[\widehat B_\lambda=\operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}F_\lambda(\beta)\] contains exactly one vector. Full column rank of \(X\) is sufficient because then the squared-loss term is strictly convex. Rank deficiency does not by itself imply nonuniqueness: uniqueness depends on the design, response, and active-set geometry. Regardless of coefficient uniqueness, any two minimizers \(\beta^{(1)},\beta^{(2)}\in\widehat B_\lambda\) satisfy \(X\beta^{(1)}=X\beta^{(2)}\), so fitted values remain identifiable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lasso coefficients are identifiable when the minimizer is unique; full column rank suffices, while fitted values remain unique even if coefficients do not.
knowledge_statements.title: Lasso Coefficient Identifiability

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The uniqueness-based identifiability condition, full-rank sufficient condition, and fitted-value uniqueness claim are coherent, but they require a specifically located source on Lasso uniqueness.

children.title: Correlated-Design Failure Boundary
children.top_down_role: Selection and identification failures associated with strongly related predictors.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Corrected counterexample family covering identical and antipodal predictors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x_2=\sigma x_1=\sigma x\ne0\), where \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}\). The fit depends on \(s=\beta_1+\sigma\beta_2\). If the reduced scalar Lasso problem has an optimum \(s^\star>0\), then for every \(a\in[0,s^\star]\), \[\beta(a)=(a,\sigma(s^\star-a))\] has fitted value \(xs^\star\) and penalty \(\|\beta(a)\|_1=s^\star\), so every \(\beta(a)\) is optimal. Endpoints select one predictor and interior points select both.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Perfectly correlated or anticorrelated predictors can split one fitted effect continuously among coefficient vectors with different supports.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{(a,\sigma(s^\star-a)):0\le a\le s^\star\}\subseteq\widehat B_\lambda.

notation.meaning: effective coefficient multiplying the common design direction
positive optimum of the reduced scalar problem

knowledge_statements.title: Perfect-Correlation Solution Continuum

assumptions_latex: Let \(X=[x_1\ x_2]\in\mathbb R^{n\times2}\) have identical nonzero columns \(x_1=x_2=x\).
Choose \(y\) and \(\lambda>0\) so the scalar problem has a positive optimum \(s^\star>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \((\beta_1,\beta_2)=(a,s^\star-a)\) with \(0\le a\le s^\star\) is optimal, so coefficients and selected support are not identifiable.

notation.meaning: Sum of the two coefficients multiplying identical columns.
Positive optimizer of the reduced scalar Lasso problem.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports this correlated-design counterexample; a Lasso uniqueness or selection source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Perfectly correlated columns give a concrete nonidentifiability and support-instability boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(x_1=x_2=x\), the two-variable Lasso objective depends on the fit only through \(s=eta_1+eta_2\). If its reduced scalar optimum satisfies \(s^\star>0\), then for every \(a\in[0,s^\star]\), \[\beta(a)=(a,s^\star-a)\] has the same fitted value \(x s^\star\) and the same penalty \(\lVert\beta(a)\rVert_1=s^\star\). Hence every \(\beta(a)\) is optimal. The endpoints select one variable, while interior points select both, demonstrating failure of coefficient identifiability and stable support selection under perfect collinearity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identical design columns can split one optimal effect arbitrarily, producing equal-objective solutions with different coefficients and supports.
knowledge_statements.title: Correlated-Design Failure Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The perfect-collinearity failure example is valid in substance and the failure_boundary kind fits, but no source is supplied. The statement and notation incorrectly write “eta_1+eta_2” and “beta_1+eta_2” where beta_1+beta_2 is intended.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous coordinatewise and groupwise sparsity for a fixed disjoint grouping.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a partition \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\) of \(\{1,\ldots,p\}\), sparse-group regression minimizes \[L(X\beta-y)+\lambda\left(\alpha\|\beta\|_1+(1-\alpha)\sum_{g=1}^m w_g\|\beta_{G_g}\|_2\right),\] where \(\lambda\ge0\), \(\alpha\in[0,1]\), and \(w_g>0\). The penalty permits complete group removal and zeros within retained groups; \(\alpha=0\) gives group Lasso and \(\alpha=1\) gives ordinary Lasso.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse-group regression combines coordinate and group penalties and interpolates between group Lasso and Lasso.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \Omega_{\mathrm{sg}}(\beta)=\alpha\|\beta\|_1+(1-\alpha)\sum_gw_g\|\beta_{G_g}\|_2\ \text{is convex}.

notation.meaning: Tradeoff between coordinatewise and groupwise sparsity.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Group Regression

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structured sparsity imposed on prescribed coefficient contrasts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(D\in\mathbb R^{q\times p}\), generalized-Lasso regression minimizes \[L(X\beta-y)+\lambda\|D\beta\|_1.\] This objective is convex for proper convex \(L\). When the rows of \(D\) are weighted signed incidence vectors of a graph, the penalty becomes \(\sum_{(j,k)\in E}w_{jk}|\beta_j-\beta_k|\), which promotes equal coefficients across selected edges. A nontrivial nullspace of \(D\) means the penalty need not be a norm and does not by itself ensure uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generalized Lasso sparsifies linear contrasts; graph incidence operators yield fused Lasso and may leave an unpenalized nullspace.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \beta\mapsto L(X\beta-y)+\lambda\|D\beta\|_1\ \text{is convex}.

notation.meaning: Linear operator encoding contrasts or graph differences.
Edge set of the fusion graph.

knowledge_statements.title: Generalized and Fused Lasso Regression

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex group selection for prescribed groups that may overlap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For groups \(G_1,\ldots,G_m\), define \[\Omega_{\mathrm{lat}}(\beta)=\inf\left\{\sum_{g=1}^m w_g\|v^{(g)}\|_2:\ \sum_gv^{(g)}=\beta,\ \operatorname{supp}(v^{(g)})\subseteq G_g\right\}.\] Then \(L(X\beta-y)+\lambda\Omega_{\mathrm{lat}}(\beta)\) is convex. If every coordinate lies in at least one group and every \(w_g>0\), \(\Omega_{\mathrm{lat}}\) is a norm; an uncovered nonzero coordinate makes the value infinite.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A latent decomposition gives a convex overlapping-group penalty and exposes its coordinate-coverage boundary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigcup_gG_g=\{1,\ldots,p\}\Longrightarrow\Omega_{\mathrm{lat}}\text{ is a norm}.

notation.meaning: Latent coefficient component supported on group g.

knowledge_statements.title: Latent Overlapping-Group Regression

assumptions_latex: The coefficient indices are partitioned into groups \(G_1,,G_m\), with weights \(w_g>0\).
The loss \(L:\mathbb R^n\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) is proper convex, and \(X\in\mathbb R^{n\times p}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Minimizing \(L(X\beta-y)+\lambda\sum_{g=1}^m w_g\|\beta_{G_g}\|_2\) is a convex structured sparse-regression problem promoting groupwise zero blocks.

notation.meaning: Coefficient subvector indexed by group G_g.

review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the group-structured sparse-regression template; a structured-sparsity source is required.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Disjoint-group Lasso as a canonical convex structured-sparsity application.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a partition \(G_1,,G_m\) of \(\{1,,p\}\), the group-structured sparse-regression template is \[\underset{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad L(X\beta-y)+\lambda\sum_{g=1}^m w_g\lVert\beta_{G_g}\rVert_2,\qquad \lambda\ge0.\] The objective is convex because it is the sum of a convex loss composed with an affine map and a nonnegative weighted sum of norms. The nonsmooth group penalty permits entire subvectors \(\beta_{G_g}\) to be zero, encoding blockwise rather than coordinatewise sparsity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Group Lasso combines a convex regression loss with a sum of group norms, allowing entire predefined coefficient blocks to be excluded.
knowledge_statements.title: Structured Sparse-Regression Applications

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The disjoint-group Lasso representation is standard and fits the application leaf, but it has no citation. The ranges “G_1,,G_m” and “{1,,p}” are malformed and should be replaced by explicit ellipses.

children.title: Robust Regression Applications
children.top_down_role: Regression templates designed to limit sensitivity to atypical residuals.

assumptions_latex: The data satisfy \(x_i\in\mathbb R^p\) and \(y_i\in\mathbb R\) for \(i=1,,n\).
The threshold \(\delta>0\) and regularizer \(R:\mathbb R^p\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\) are fixed, with \(R\) proper convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The Huber regression estimator minimizes \(\sum_i h_\delta(y_i-x_i^\top\beta)+R(\beta)\), a convex objective with bounded residual derivative.

notation.meaning: Huber loss with quadratic center and linear tails.

review_flags: The supplied nonsmooth-objective locator is only indirect support for this specific Huber regression application.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Huber-loss regression as a convex robust alternative to least squares.

source_refs.locator: 3.3.1 Nonsmooth Models of the Objective Function p. 225

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define the Huber loss by \[h_\delta(r)=\begin{cases}\frac12 r^2,&|r|\le\delta,\\ \delta|r|-\frac12\delta^2,&|r|>\delta.\end{cases}\] Huber regression solves \[\underset{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}{\operatorname{minimize}}\quad \sum_{i=1}^n h_\delta\bigl(y_i-x_i^\top\beta\bigr)+R(\beta).\] This is a convex optimization problem. Moreover, \(|h_\delta'(r)|\le\delta\), so the marginal contribution of a residual is bounded, unlike squared loss whose derivative grows without bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Huber regression uses quadratic loss for moderate residuals and linear loss for large residuals, retaining convexity while limiting outlier influence.
knowledge_statements.title: Robust Regression Applications

source_witnesses.locator: 3.3.1 Nonsmooth Models of the Objective Function p. 225

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes bounded residual influence from protection against extreme covariates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(\beta)=\sum_i h_\delta(y_i-x_i^\top\beta)+R(\beta)\), observation \(i\) contributes \(-x_i\psi_\delta(r_i)\) to a data-fit subgradient, where \(r_i=y_i-x_i^\top\beta\) and \(|\psi_\delta(r_i)|\le\delta\). Hence \[\|x_i\psi_\delta(r_i)\|_2\le\delta\|x_i\|_2,\] but no bound independent of \(x_i\) exists. Huberization limits large residual contributions at fixed design but does not itself protect against arbitrarily high-leverage covariates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Huber loss clips residual derivatives, but an extreme feature vector can still give one observation an arbitrarily large regression gradient.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|-x_i\psi_\delta(r_i)\|_2\le\delta\|x_i\|_2,\quad\text{with no design-independent bound}.
knowledge_statements.title: Huber Regression Leverage Limitation

children.title: Quantile-Regression Applications
children.top_down_role: Regression templates targeting conditional quantiles.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample optimality test for linear quantile regression, with an optional convex penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(Q(\beta)=\sum_{i=1}^n\rho_\tau(y_i-x_i^\top\beta)+\lambda R(\beta)\), a point \(\widehat\beta\in\operatorname{dom}R\) minimizes \(Q\) if and only if there are \(a_i\in[\tau-1,\tau]\) with \(a_i=\tau\) when \(y_i-x_i^\top\widehat\beta>0\), \(a_i=\tau-1\) when \(y_i-x_i^\top\widehat\beta<0\), and \(0\in-X^\top a+\lambda\partial R(\widehat\beta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Residual-sign subgradients balancing a penalty subgradient give an exact quantile-regression optimality certificate.
assumptions_latex: R\text{ is proper convex when present}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in-X^\top a+\lambda\partial R(\widehat\beta).
knowledge_statements.title: Quantile-Regression Subgradient Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Population check-loss minimizers for a scalar response distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a real random variable \(Y\) with \(\mathbb E|Y|<\infty\) and distribution function \(F\), \[q\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{s\in\mathbb R}\mathbb E\rho_\tau(Y-s)\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F(q^-)\le\tau\le F(q).\] Thus convexity does not imply a unique target: uniqueness holds exactly when this quantile set is a singleton.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Expected check loss identifies the set-valued quantile, which can be nonunique at atoms or across flat distribution regions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_s\mathbb E\rho_\tau(Y-s)=\{q:F(q^-)\le\tau\le F(q)\}.

notation.meaning: Left limit of the distribution function at q.

knowledge_statements.title: Quantile Identification and Nonuniqueness Boundary

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Linear-Programming Form of Linear Quantile Regression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unregularized linear quantile regression and variants with polyhedral convex penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Writing \(y_i-x_i^\top\beta=u_i-v_i\) with \(u_i,v_i\ge0\), linear quantile regression is equivalent to \[\min_{\beta,u,v}\sum_{i=1}^n\bigl(\tau u_i+(1-\tau)v_i\bigr)\quad\text{s.t.}\quad X\beta+u-v=y,\quad u,v\ge0.\] A polyhedral convex penalty on \(\beta\), including a weighted \(\ell_1\) penalty, preserves LP representability after an epigraph lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive and negative residual parts convert linear quantile regression and polyhedrally penalized variants into linear programs.
assumptions_latex: R\text{ is omitted or polyhedral convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_{\beta}\sum_i\rho_\tau(y_i-x_i^\top\beta)=\operatorname{proj}_{\beta}\operatorname*{argmin}_{X\beta+u-v=y,\ u,v\ge0}\sum_i\bigl(\tau u_i+(1-\tau)v_i\bigr).
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Programming Form of Linear Quantile Regression
Quantile-Regression Applications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-sample linear quantile regression with optional convex regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define \(\rho_\tau(u)=\tau u_+ +(1-\tau)(-u)_+\). For \(\lambda>0\), a regularized linear quantile-regression estimator is any element of
\[
\mathop{\rm argmin}_{\beta\in\mathbb R^p}\left\{\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\rho_\tau\bigl(y_i-x_i^\top\beta\bigr)+\lambda R(\beta)\right\}.
\]
For \(\lambda=0\), the penalty term is omitted. The resulting objective is convex. At the population level, every minimizer of \(q\mapsto\mathbb E[\rho_\tau(Y-q)\mid X=x]\), when the conditional expectation is finite and a minimizer exists, is a conditional \(\tau\)-quantile under the usual set-valued quantile convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Linear quantile regression minimizes asymmetric check loss, optionally together with a convex penalty; the corresponding population loss targets a conditional quantile.
assumptions_latex: Observations satisfy \((x_i,y_i)\in\mathbb R^p\times\mathbb R\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\), where \(n\ge1\).
The quantile level satisfies \(\tau\in(0,1)\), the penalty weight satisfies \(\lambda\ge0\), and \(R:\mathbb R^p\to(-\infty,+\infty]\) is proper and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any displayed minimizer is a convex empirical check-loss estimator, with the penalty omitted when \(\lambda=0\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: empirical check-loss minimization is the standard convex template for linear quantile regression

children.title: Asymmetric-Loss Regimes
children.top_down_role: Application regimes distinguished by unequal treatment of positive versus negative residuals.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interior slopes and the sharp one-sided endpoint boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\tau\in[0,1]\), \[\partial\rho_\tau(u)=\begin{cases}\{\tau-1\},&u<0,\\[\tau-1,\tau],&u=0,\\\{\tau\},&u>0.\end{cases}\] The loss is \(L_\tau\)-Lipschitz with \(L_\tau=\max\{\tau,1-\tau\}\), and it is coercive exactly when \(0<\tau<1\). At \(\tau=0\), \(\rho_0(u)=(-u)_+\) vanishes for \(u\ge0\); at \(\tau=1\), \(\rho_1(u)=u_+\) vanishes for \(u\le0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Interior check losses grow in both directions; endpoint losses remain convex but ignore an entire residual half-line.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho_\tau\text{ is coercive}\iff0<\tau<1.
knowledge_statements.title: Subgradient and Endpoint-Coercivity Regimes

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent convex representations of check loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\tau\in[0,1]\), \[\rho_\tau(u)=\max\{\tau u,(\tau-1)u\}=\sup_{a\in[\tau-1,\tau]}au.\] Hence \(\rho_\tau^*=\delta_{[\tau-1,\tau]}\), and its epigraph is \[t\ge\tau u,\qquad t\ge(\tau-1)u.\] Consequently, a finite-sample linear quantile-regression objective has an exact linear-programming epigraph formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Check loss is the support function of an asymmetric interval, has an interval-indicator conjugate, and admits a two-inequality linear epigraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \rho_\tau=\sigma_{[\tau-1,\tau]},\qquad\rho_\tau^*=\delta_{[\tau-1,\tau]}.
knowledge_statements.title: Support-Function, Conjugate, and Epigraph Forms

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Changing \(\tau\) changes the relative costs of underprediction and overprediction while preserving convexity.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the check loss gives the canonical convex asymmetric-loss regime
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymmetry induced by the quantile check loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every residual \(u\in\mathbb R\), the check loss satisfies
\[
\rho_\tau(u)=\begin{cases}\tau u,&u\ge 0,\\(1-\tau)(-u),&u<0.\end{cases}
\]
It is convex and nonnegative. If \(u=y-\widehat y\), then underprediction \(u>0\) has marginal cost \(\tau\), whereas overprediction \(u<0\) has marginal cost \(1-\tau\). Thus \(\tau>1/2\) penalizes underprediction more heavily, \(\tau<1/2\) penalizes overprediction more heavily, and \(\tau=1/2\) gives one half of absolute loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The quantile parameter selects a convex asymmetric loss: larger values penalize underprediction more, while smaller values penalize overprediction more.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymmetric-Loss Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The asymmetric check-loss formula, convexity, marginal costs, and interpretation of tau are mathematically consistent and fit the property container, but no inspectable citation is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical algorithm and block representation for monotone least-squares regression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w_i>0\), weighted isotonic regression solves \[\min_{\theta_1\le\cdots\le\theta_n}\frac12\sum_{i=1}^n w_i(y_i-\theta_i)^2.\] Its unique solution is constant on consecutive blocks, with each final block \(B\) taking value \(\sum_{i\in B}w_i y_i/\sum_{i\in B}w_i\). The pool-adjacent-violators algorithm repeatedly merges adjacent blocks whose weighted means violate monotonicity and runs in \(O(n)\) time with a stack implementation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: PAVA pools adjacent mean-violating blocks and computes the unique weighted isotonic fit in linear time.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat\theta_i=\frac{\sum_{j\in B}w_jy_j}{\sum_{j\in B}w_j}\ \text{for }i\in B,\qquad T(n)=O(n).

notation.meaning: A consecutive constant block in the isotonic fit.

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Isotonic Regression and PAVA
Shape-Constrained Regression Applications
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional least-squares fitting under convex shape constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A shape-constrained least-squares fit is the Euclidean projection
\[
\widehat\theta=\mathop{\rm argmin}_{\theta\in K}\frac12\|y-\theta\|_2^2.
\]
For example, monotonicity is encoded by the isotonic cone \(K=\{\theta\in\mathbb R^n:\theta_1\le\cdots\le\theta_n\}\). For ordered scalar design points \(t_1<\cdots<t_n\), discrete convexity is encoded by
\[
K=\left\{\theta\in\mathbb R^n:\frac{\theta_{i+1}-\theta_i}{t_{i+1}-t_i}\le\frac{\theta_{i+2}-\theta_{i+1}}{t_{i+2}-t_{i+1}},\ i=1,\ldots,n-2\right\}.
\]
Because \(K\) is nonempty, closed, and convex, the fitted-value vector exists and is unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Shape-constrained least squares uniquely projects the response vector onto a nonempty closed convex set encoding constraints such as monotonicity or discrete convexity.
assumptions_latex: The response vector satisfies \(y\in\mathbb R^n\), where \(n\ge3\), and the scalar design points satisfy \(t_1<\cdots<t_n\).
The feasible shape set \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) is nonempty, closed, and convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The vector \(\widehat\theta\) is the unique Euclidean projection of \(y\) onto \(K\).

notation.meaning: Vector of fitted values at the design points.
Closed convex set encoding the prescribed shape.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: least-squares projection onto a convex constraint set is the standard finite-dimensional shape-constrained template

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Projection Certificate for a Shape-Constrained Fit
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic normal-cone characterization of projection onto a closed convex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty closed convex \(K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), \(\widehat\theta=P_K(y)\) if and only if \(\widehat\theta\in K\) and \(y-\widehat\theta\in N_K(\widehat\theta)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normal-cone residual condition characterizes Euclidean projection onto any closed convex set.
assumptions_latex: K\subseteq\mathbb R^n\text{ is nonempty, closed, and convex}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat\theta=P_K(y)\iff \widehat\theta\in K\ \text{and}\ y-\widehat\theta\in N_K(\widehat\theta).

notation.meaning: Normal cone to K at the fitted vector.

children.top_down_role: Convex classification model family; hinge-loss construction, kernel theory, and statistical learning guarantees retain separate primary homes.
