top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Steinwart and Christmann, Support Vector Machines

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual characterization of the feasible two-class hard-margin linear SVM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The dual of the hard-margin primal is
\[
\max_{\alpha\ge0}\left\{\mathbf1^\top\alpha-\frac12\sum_{i,j}\alpha_i\alpha_jy_iy_jx_i^\top x_j\right\}
\quad\text{subject to}\quad y^\top\alpha=0.
\]
Both optima are attained with equal values. A primal-dual feasible pair is optimal exactly when
\[
w=\sum_i\alpha_i y_i x_i,
\qquad
\alpha_i\bigl(y_i(w^\top x_i+b)-1\bigr)=0\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The feasible two-class hard-margin SVM has an attained nonnegative quadratic dual, and feasibility, stationarity, and complementarity certify optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^*=d^*,\quad w=\sum_i\alpha_i y_i x_i,\quad \alpha_i[y_i(w^\top x_i+b)-1]=0.

notation.meaning: Multiplier of the ith unit-margin inequality.

knowledge_statements.title: Hard-Margin Dual and KKT Characterization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Solution structure for a feasible sample containing both classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a feasible sample containing both classes, the optimal normal vector \(w^*\) is unique. For fixed \(w^*\), feasibility requires
\[
\max_{i:y_i=1}(1-w^{*\top}x_i)\le b\le
\min_{i:y_i=-1}(-1-w^{*\top}x_i).
\]
At optimality these endpoints coincide; otherwise an interior intercept would make every margin inequality strict, permitting a positive rescaling that decreases \(\|w^*\|_2\). Hence the optimal intercept and separating hyperplane are also unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With both classes present, strict convexity makes the optimal normal unique, and optimality forces the feasible intercept interval to collapse to one point.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w^*\text{ and }b^*\text{ are unique}.
review_flags: revises_builder_claim: a non-singleton optimal intercept interval is impossible for a feasible two-class hard-margin optimum
knowledge_statements.title: Uniqueness of the Hard-Margin Hyperplane

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Convex-Hull Characterization of the Hard Margin
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite binary samples containing both classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=\operatorname{conv}\{x_i:y_i=1\}\) and \(N=\operatorname{conv}\{x_i:y_i=-1\}\), with both sets nonempty. The hard-margin constraints are feasible if and only if \(P\cap N=\varnothing\). If \(\delta=\operatorname{dist}(P,N)>0\), the maximum distance from the separating hyperplane to the nearer class hull is \(\delta/2\), and the distance between the two supporting margin hyperplanes is \(\delta\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite two-class sample is hard-margin separable exactly when its class convex hulls are disjoint, and their distance determines the optimal margin.
assumptions_latex: \(P,N\subset\mathbb R^p\) are the two class convex hulls.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P\cap N=\varnothing\iff\exists(w,b):y_i(w^\top x_i+b)\ge1,\qquad \gamma^*=\tfrac12\operatorname{dist}(P,N).
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Hull Characterization of the Hard Margin

assumptions_latex: The labeled sample is affinely separable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimizer defines a separating hyperplane with maximum geometric margin \(1/\|w\|_2\).

notation.meaning: Normal vector and intercept of the separating hyperplane.
Signed functional margin of sample i.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: this is the canonical normalized primal formulation of the hard-margin linear SVM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linearly separable binary classification in the linear primal formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The hard-margin support vector machine solves
\[
\min_{w\in\mathbb R^p,\,b\in\mathbb R}\frac12\|w\|_2^2
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
y_i(w^\top x_i+b)\ge1\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).
\]
Under affine separability the feasible set is nonempty. The normalization fixes the closest signed functional margin at one, so minimizing \(\|w\|_2\) maximizes the geometric margin. Any optimizer classifies a point \(x\) by the sign of \(w^\top x+b\); training points attaining equality are margin support vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For separable binary data, hard-margin SVM finds the separating hyperplane with maximum geometric margin and no training violations.
knowledge_statements.title: Hard-Margin SVM

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The canonical hard-margin program fits the representation container, but no source is supplied. The maximum-margin and support-vector language also needs an explicit nondegeneracy convention, such as requiring both classes to occur, because a one-class sample can admit w=0 and make 1/||w|| undefined.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Existence and Partial Uniqueness of Soft-Margin Solutions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear L1-slack soft-margin SVM with an unregularized intercept.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(C>0\) and both labels occur, the soft-margin objective attains its minimum. All minimizers have the same normal vector \(w^*\), although the intercept and slack vector need not be unique. If only one label occurs, \(w=0\) and every intercept satisfying \(y_i b\ge1\) for all observations is optimal with zero slack, so the intercept is unboundedly nonunique.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With both classes present, a soft-margin optimum exists and its normal is unique; one-class data produce a degenerate family of zero-loss intercepts.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{y_i\}=\{-1,1\}\Longrightarrow\exists(w^*,b^*,\xi^*)\text{ and }w^*\text{ is unique}.
knowledge_statements.title: Existence and Partial Uniqueness of Soft-Margin Solutions

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The optimizer trades a small norm against violations of the unit-margin inequalities.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: this is the canonical L1-slack soft-margin linear SVM
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear soft-margin SVM with an unregularized intercept and linear slack penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The soft-margin support vector machine solves
\[
\min_{w,b,\xi}\frac12\|w\|_2^2+C\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_i
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
y_i(w^\top x_i+b)\ge1-\xi_i,\quad \xi_i\ge0.
\]
For fixed \((w,b)\), the smallest feasible slack is \(\xi_i=[1-y_i(w^\top x_i+b)]_+\). Hence the problem is equivalently the unconstrained convex minimization of \(\frac12\|w\|_2^2+C\sum_i[1-y_i(w^\top x_i+b)]_+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Soft-margin SVM permits margin violations and penalizes them linearly, yielding an equivalent regularized hinge-loss problem.
knowledge_statements.title: Soft-Margin SVM

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The L1-slack formulation and its hinge-loss equivalence are mathematically consistent and appropriately classified as a representation, but there is no inspectable citation.

children.title: Class-Imbalance Weighting
children.top_down_role: SVM regimes using class-dependent weighting to address unequal class prevalence.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual effect of assigning different hinge penalties to the two classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The class-weighted soft-margin primal has dual \max_{\alpha}\mathbf1^\top\alpha-\frac12\lVert\sum_i\alpha_i y_i x_i\rVert_2^2 subject to y^\top\alpha=0 and 0\leq\alpha_i\leq C_{y_i}. Thus class weighting changes the observation-specific box constraints but not the equality constraint or quadratic form.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Class weights become class-dependent upper bounds on the SVM dual coefficients.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\leq\alpha_i\leq C_{y_i}

notation.meaning: hinge penalty associated with observation i's class

knowledge_statements.title: Class-Weighted SVM Dual Bounds

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Replication Equivalence for Integer Class Weights
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact empirical-objective interpretation of integer-valued class weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If C_{y_i}/C_0=m_i is a positive integer for every observation, then \frac12\lVert w\rVert_2^2+\sum_iC_{y_i}[1-y_i(w^\top x_i+b)]_+ equals the ordinary C_0-weighted soft-margin objective on a multiset containing m_i copies of observation i. This is an objective equivalence and does not create independent observations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Integer class weighting is algebraically equivalent to replicating each observation according to its class weight.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sum_iC_{y_i}\ell_i=C_0\sum_i\sum_{j=1}^{m_i}\ell_i
knowledge_statements.title: Replication Equivalence for Integer Class Weights
Class-Imbalance Weighting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary linear SVM with class-dependent violation penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A class-weighted soft-margin SVM is
\[
\min_{w\in\mathbb R^p,\,b\in\mathbb R}\frac12\|w\|_2^2+\sum_{i=1}^n C_{y_i}[1-y_i(w^\top x_i+b)]_+.
\]
Equivalently, introduce \(\xi\in\mathbb R_+^n\), impose \(y_i(w^\top x_i+b)\ge1-\xi_i\) for \(i=1,\ldots,n\), and minimize \(\frac12\|w\|_2^2+\sum_{i=1}^n C_{y_i}\xi_i\). A larger weight for a class raises the objective cost of its margin violations while preserving convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Class-imbalance weighting gives positive and negative examples different hinge-loss penalties while preserving the convex soft-margin SVM formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each observation's hinge loss is multiplied by the positive weight \(C_{y_i}\) assigned to its class.

notation.meaning: Penalty assigned to the class of observation i.
Positive-part function used in the hinge loss.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: class-weighted hinge loss is the standard convex SVM correction for unequal class importance

children.title: Cost-Sensitive Margin Design
children.top_down_role: Margin models reflecting unequal consequences for different error types.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual representation of the class-target and class-penalty primal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For m_{y_i}>0 and C_{y_i}>0, the dual is \max_{\alpha}\sum_i m_{y_i}\alpha_i-\frac12\lVert\sum_i\alpha_i y_i x_i\rVert_2^2 subject to y^\top\alpha=0 and 0\leq\alpha_i\leq C_{y_i}. Target margins alter the dual linear reward, while violation costs alter the coefficient bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Class-specific target margins and violation costs affect different parts of the SVM dual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{0\leq\alpha_i\leq C_{y_i},\ y^\top\alpha=0}\sum_i m_{y_i}\alpha_i-\frac12\left\lVert\sum_i\alpha_i y_i x_i\right\rVert_2^2
knowledge_statements.title: Dual of Class-Dependent Margin Design

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of unequal positive and negative target margins when the intercept is unrestricted.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let M=(m_++m_-)/2 and \delta=(m_+-m_-)/2. With h(x)=w^\top x+b-\delta, the constraints y_i(w^\top x_i+b)\geq m_{y_i}-\xi_i are equivalent to y_i h(x_i)\geq M-\xi_i. Thus unequal target margins do not change the fitted symmetric margin slab after an intercept reparameterization; they change the location of the zero-score prediction threshold relative to that slab.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With a free intercept, unequal class targets are a symmetric target plus a fixed score-threshold shift.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y_i(w^\top x_i+b)\geq m_{y_i}-\xi_i\iff y_i(w^\top x_i+b-\delta)\geq M-\xi_i

notation.meaning: average of the two class target margins
half-difference of the class target margins

knowledge_statements.title: Target-Asymmetry Intercept Reparameterization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact parameter equivalence under simultaneous scaling of scores, slacks, targets, and penalties.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a>0, the map (w,b,\xi)\mapsto(aw,ab,a\xi) is a feasibility bijection from target margins m_y to target margins am_y. If penalties are simultaneously changed from C_y to aC_y, the transformed objective is exactly a^2 times the original objective. Therefore the common scale of the target margins is redundant after the corresponding penalty normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common target-margin scale can be absorbed by scaling the scores, slacks, and penalty parameters.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_{am,aC}(aw,ab,a\xi)=a^2P_{m,C}(w,b,\xi)

notation.meaning: class-dependent margin primal with target vector m and penalties C

knowledge_statements.title: Common-Scale Redundancy of Target Margins
Cost-Sensitive Margin Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One explicit class-dependent margin-and-slack parameterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A class-dependent margin design is
\[
\min_{w\in\mathbb R^p,\,b\in\mathbb R,\,\xi\in\mathbb R_+^n}\frac12\|w\|_2^2+\sum_{i=1}^n C_{y_i}\xi_i
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
y_i(w^\top x_i+b)\ge m_{y_i}-\xi_i\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).
\]
Eliminating \(\xi\) gives the convex objective
\[
\frac12\|w\|_2^2+\sum_{i=1}^n C_{y_i}[m_{y_i}-y_i(w^\top x_i+b)]_+.
\]
Thus \(m_y\) specifies a class-dependent target functional margin and \(C_y\) specifies the cost of its violation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cost-sensitive linear SVM can use a positive target margin and violation penalty specific to each class, producing a convex optimization problem.
assumptions_latex: Target margins satisfy \(m_+>0\) and \(m_->0\), and violation penalties satisfy \(C_+>0\) and \(C_->0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Class-specific targets \(m_y\) and penalties \(C_y\) define the displayed convex margin classifier.

notation.meaning: Required functional margin for class y.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: class-dependent target margins and slack costs give a convex cost-sensitive margin template

children.title: Minority-Class Failure Regimes
children.top_down_role: Decision-boundary failures affecting underrepresented classes.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Balanced Weighting Can Still Reject an Overlapped Minority Point
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit sample showing that balanced aggregate class weights do not ensure minority training recall.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take one positive and one negative observation at the same feature point x=0, with C_+=C_->0 and an unregularized intercept. For w=0 the weighted hinge loss is C_+[1-b]_++C_-[1+b]_+, whose minimum is attained by every b\in[-1,1]. In particular b=-1 is optimal and classifies the positive observation as negative. Hence balanced weights permit an optimum with zero positive-class recall when opposite labels coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coincident opposite-label observations admit an optimal balanced-weight solution that rejects the positive observation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (w,b)=(0,-1)\text{ is optimal and }\operatorname{recall}_+=0
knowledge_statements.title: Balanced Weighting Can Still Reject an Overlapped Minority Point

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Inverse-Frequency Weighting Has No Recall Guarantee
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Precise limit of count balancing as a remedy for minority rejection.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Choosing weights with C_+n_+=C_-n_- makes the constant scores b=-1 and b=1 have equal weighted hinge loss, but it does not constrain an optimizer's minority recall. Feature overlap or the regularized margin geometry can still produce optimal solutions that misclassify minority observations. Count balancing therefore removes the seed's specific constant-rule preference, not the general minority-failure regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse-frequency weighting neutralizes the constant-classifier count comparison but does not guarantee minority recall.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C_+n_+=C_-n_-\centernot\Longrightarrow\operatorname{recall}_+=1

notation.meaning: fraction of positive observations predicted positive

knowledge_statements.title: Inverse-Frequency Weighting Has No Recall Guarantee

assumptions_latex: A training sample contains \(n_+\) positive and \(n_-\) negative observations with \(n_->0\).
An intercept is unregularized, and the positive-class weight is \(C_+>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(C_+n_+<C_-n_-\), a classifier rejecting every positive example can have lower weighted hinge objective than the opposite constant classifier.

notation.meaning: Counts of positive and negative training labels.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: constant-score comparison is a direct failure mechanism for unbalanced weighted hinge risk
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete constant-classifier failure mechanism for an unregularized intercept.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider the weighted hinge objective with \(w=0\). The constant score \(b=-1\) rejects every positive observation and has loss \(2C_+n_+\), while \(b=1\) rejects every negative observation and has loss \(2C_-n_-\). Therefore, when \(C_+n_+<C_-n_-\), the all-negative constant rule is preferred to the all-positive constant rule by the training objective. In particular, with equal class weights and \(n_+\ll n_-\), empirical hinge-risk comparison alone can favor complete minority-class rejection; inverse-frequency weighting removes this specific count imbalance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With equal weights and severe imbalance, weighted hinge risk may prefer a constant classifier that rejects every minority example.
knowledge_statements.title: Minority-Class Failure Regimes

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constant-score calculation is correct and the failure_boundary kind fits the leaf. It proves only that the all-negative constant rule beats the all-positive constant rule, not that it is globally preferred over every classifier; the plain text should retain that comparison-level qualification. No citation is supplied.

children.title: SVM Primal Margin Representation
children.top_down_role: Application-facing primal representation of margin-based classification.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary for interpreting the normalized primal as a finite geometric-margin problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If both labels occur and the hard-margin inequalities are feasible, every feasible normal satisfies \(w\ne0\), so the geometric margin and the supporting-hyperplane width \(2/\|w\|_2\) are well defined. If only one label occurs, \(w=0\) with a suitable intercept is feasible and optimal, so \(1/\|w\|_2\) and the asserted pair of supporting margin hyperplanes are not meaningful.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The usual hard-margin geometry requires both classes; one-class data admit an optimal zero normal and invalidate inverse-norm margin formulas.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{y_i\}=\{-1,1\}\Longrightarrow w\ne0;\qquad |\{y_i\}|=1\Longrightarrow w=0\text{ can be optimal}.
knowledge_statements.title: Nondegenerate Margin-Normalization Condition

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal quadratic program minimizes inverse squared geometric margin subject to correct unit-margin classification.

notation.meaning: Geometric distance from x to the hyperplane when the score is nonzero.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: normalized maximum-margin separation has the canonical convex quadratic primal representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized hard-margin primal representation for a linear SVM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Because multiplying \((w,b)\) by a positive scalar leaves the classifier unchanged, impose the normalization \(\min_i y_i f_{w,b}(x_i)=1\). The maximum-margin problem then has the convex primal representation
\[
\min_{w\in\mathbb R^p,\,b\in\mathbb R}\frac12\|w\|_2^2
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
y_i f_{w,b}(x_i)\ge1\quad(i=1,\ldots,n).
\]
At an optimum, the distance between the two supporting hyperplanes \(f_{w,b}(x)=1\) and \(f_{w,b}(x)=-1\) is \(2/\|w\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After fixing the functional-margin scale, maximum-margin classification becomes a convex quadratic program minimizing the squared normal-vector norm.
knowledge_statements.title: SVM Primal Margin Representation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized hard-margin quadratic program and supporting-hyperplane width are standard, but no source is supplied. Requiring both classes to occur would exclude the degenerate w=0 case in which the asserted geometric-margin quantities are undefined.

children.title: SVM Slack-Variable Representation
children.top_down_role: Representation of margin violations through explicit slack variables.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quadratic-slack variant distinct from the immutable linear-slack epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For fixed \((w,b)\),
\[
[1-y_i(w^\top x_i+b)]_+^2
=
\min_{\xi_i\ge0}\{\xi_i^2:y_i(w^\top x_i+b)\ge1-\xi_i\}.
\]
Consequently the squared-hinge SVM is exactly
\[
\min_{w,b,\xi\ge0}\frac12\|w\|_2^2+\frac C2\sum_i\xi_i^2
\quad\text{subject to}\quad y_i(w^\top x_i+b)\ge1-\xi_i.
\]
At every optimum, \(\xi_i=[1-y_i(w^\top x_i+b)]_+\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing the linear slack cost by a quadratic slack cost gives an exact constrained representation of squared hinge loss.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{\xi_i\ge0,\ \xi_i\ge1-y_if_i}\xi_i^2=[1-y_if_i]_+^2.
knowledge_statements.title: Squared-Hinge Slack Representation

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Introducing nonnegative slack variables gives an exact epigraph representation of the hinge-loss SVM.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: hinge loss is exactly represented by a nonnegative epigraph slack
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact slack-variable epigraph of the linear hinge-loss objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every fixed \((w,b)\),
\[
[1-y_i(w^\top x_i+b)]_+
=
\min_{\xi_i}\{\xi_i:\xi_i\ge0,\ \xi_i\ge1-y_i(w^\top x_i+b)\}.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\min_{w,b}\frac12\|w\|_2^2+C\sum_i[1-y_i(w^\top x_i+b)]_+
=
\min_{w,b,\xi}\frac12\|w\|_2^2+C\sum_i\xi_i
\]
subject to \(y_i(w^\top x_i+b)\ge1-\xi_i\) and \(\xi_i\ge0\). At any optimum each \(\xi_i\) equals the corresponding hinge loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonnegative slack variable exactly represents each hinge loss, converting soft-margin SVM into a linearly constrained quadratic program.
knowledge_statements.title: SVM Slack-Variable Representation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The slack-variable epigraph identity and constrained reformulation are correct, mutually consistent, and well matched to the representation container, but no inspectable source is cited.

children.title: SVM Penalty-Constraint Interface
children.top_down_role: Structural relationship between violation budgets and penalty-based control.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero-Multiplier Boundary of Reverse Parameter Matching
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp boundary in converting a regularizer-constrained solution to a finite-penalty SVM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\min L(w,b)\) subject to \(R(w)\le r\), an attained optimal multiplier \(\mu\ge0\) makes constrained optima satisfying the associated saddle conditions minimize \(L+\mu R\). A multiplier \(\mu>0\) corresponds, after positive rescaling, to the finite soft-margin parameter \(C=1/\mu\). If every applicable optimal multiplier is zero, multiplier matching yields only the unregularized limiting problem and does not establish correspondence with any finite \(C\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reverse constrained-to-penalized matching gives a finite SVM parameter only when an applicable optimal budget multiplier is strictly positive.
assumptions_latex: Strong Lagrangian duality and multiplier attainment hold for the constrained problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mu>0\Longrightarrow C=1/\mu<\infty;\qquad \mu=0\not\Longrightarrow\exists C<\infty\text{ with the same solution set}.

notation.meaning: Optimal multiplier of the regularizer-budget constraint.

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Multiplier Boundary of Reverse Parameter Matching

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonicity Along the SVM Penalty Path
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tradeoff between empirical hinge loss and squared-norm regularization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((w_{\lambda},b_{\lambda})\) minimize \(L(w,b)+\lambda R(w)\). For \(0<\lambda_1<\lambda_2\), any selected minimizers satisfy
\[
R(w_{\lambda_2})\le R(w_{\lambda_1}),
\qquad
L(w_{\lambda_2},b_{\lambda_2})\ge L(w_{\lambda_1},b_{\lambda_1}).
\]
Equivalently, in the normalization \(R+C L\), increasing \(C\) cannot increase the attained optimal hinge loss and cannot decrease the attained squared-norm regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: More regularization yields a no-larger norm and no-smaller training hinge loss; increasing C reverses those monotonic directions.
assumptions_latex: Minimizers exist at both parameter values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: R_{\lambda_2}\le R_{\lambda_1},\qquad L_{\lambda_2}\ge L_{\lambda_1}.
knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity Along the SVM Penalty Path

assumptions_latex: The feasible parameter set is nonempty, and the convex loss \(L\) and regularizer \(R\) are proper and lower semicontinuous.
An optimizer exists for the penalized problem at the selected \(\lambda>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every penalized optimizer also solves a constraint-form problem at the regularizer level it attains.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: penalized-to-constrained equivalence follows from comparing the penalized optimizer at its attained regularizer level
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-way penalty-to-constraint correspondence; reverse parameter matching requires regularity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \((w_\lambda,b_\lambda)\) minimize \(L(w,b)+\lambda R(w)\), and set \(r_\lambda=R(w_\lambda)\). Then
\[
(w_\lambda,b_\lambda)\in\mathop{\rm argmin}_{R(w)\le r_\lambda}L(w,b).
\]
Indeed, any feasible point with smaller loss would also have a smaller penalized objective. For the SVM, multiplying the objective by a positive constant identifies \(R+C L\) with \(L+\lambda R\) through \(\lambda=1/C\). Conversely, a solution of the constrained problem corresponds to a penalized solution when an appropriate nonnegative optimal multiplier exists, as under standard convex constraint qualification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalized SVM solution also solves a loss-minimization problem constrained at its attained norm; reverse matching uses an optimal constraint multiplier.
knowledge_statements.title: SVM Penalty-Constraint Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-way penalized-to-constrained implication is correct. The reverse correspondence depends on multiplier existence and the relationship between the multiplier and a strictly positive penalty parameter, so the stated qualification needs a precise source. The property kind fits the interface leaf.

children.title: SVM Dual Representation
children.top_down_role: Dual application interface for margin models.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: RKHS extension of the L1-slack dual through a positive-semidefinite kernel.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(K\) be a positive-semidefinite kernel with feature map \(\phi\) into a Hilbert space \(\mathcal H\). Replacing \(x_i\) by \(\phi(x_i)\) in the L1-slack primal leaves the dual constraints unchanged and replaces inner products by \(K(x_i,x_j)\):
\[
\max_{0\le\alpha\le C,\ y^\top\alpha=0}
\left\{\mathbf1^\top\alpha- rac12\sum_{i,j}\alpha_i\alpha_jy_i y_jK(x_i,x_j)\right\}.
\]
Every primal-dual optimum satisfies \(w=\sum_i\alpha_i y_i\phi(x_i)\), and prediction uses \(\sum_i\alpha_i y_iK(x_i,x)+b\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because the soft-margin dual depends only on Gram entries, a positive-semidefinite kernel yields the corresponding RKHS SVM and finite support-vector predictor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w^*=\sum_i\alpha_i^*y_i\phi(x_i),\qquad f(x)=\sum_i\alpha_i^*y_iK(x_i,x)+b^*.

notation.meaning: Kernel Hilbert space and feature map.

knowledge_statements.title: Kernelized Soft-Margin Dual Representation
SVM Dual Representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear L1-slack soft-margin SVM dual with an unregularized intercept.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The dual of the linear L1-slack soft-margin primal is
\[
\max_{\alpha\in\mathbb R^n}\left\{\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i-\frac12\sum_{i,j=1}^n\alpha_i\alpha_jy_iy_jK_{ij}\right\}
\quad\text{subject to}\quad
0\le\alpha_i\le C\ \ (i=1,\ldots,n),\qquad \sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i y_i=0.
\]
A strictly feasible slack choice exists, so convex strong duality applies. At every primal-dual optimum, \(w=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i y_i x_i\). Complementary slackness implies that \(\alpha_i>0\) only if the corresponding margin inequality is active after slack is included.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The linear L1-slack soft-margin SVM has a box-constrained quadratic dual whose multipliers reconstruct the primal normal vector and identify active margin constraints.
assumptions_latex: The soft-margin primal uses a penalty \(C>0\) and an unregularized intercept \(b\in\mathbb R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The primal and displayed dual have equal optimal values, and every primal-dual optimum satisfies \(w=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i y_i x_i\).

notation.meaning: Dual multipliers for the margin inequalities.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: Lagrangian duality gives the canonical box-constrained quadratic dual of the L1-slack SVM

children.title: Support-Vector Certificate Interface
children.top_down_role: Certificate interpretation centered on active training observations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directly checkable exact or approximate certificate for the L1-slack linear SVM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For any primal-feasible \((w,b,\xi)\) and dual-feasible \(\alpha\), define \(w_\alpha=\sum_i\alpha_i y_i x_i\) and \(s_i=y_i(w^\top x_i+b)-1+\xi_i\ge0\). Then
\[
P(w,b,\xi)-D(\alpha)=\frac12\|w-w_\alpha\|_2^2+
\sum_i\alpha_i s_i+
\sum_i(C-\alpha_i)\xi_i\ge0.
\]
The gap is zero exactly when stationarity and both complementary-slackness families hold. A gap at most \(\varepsilon\) certifies primal suboptimality at most \(\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The SVM duality gap decomposes into nonnegative stationarity and complementarity residuals, yielding exact and epsilon-optimality certificates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P-D=\tfrac12\|w-w_\alpha\|^2+\sum_i\alpha_i s_i+\sum_i(C-\alpha_i)\xi_i\ge0.

notation.meaning: Normal vector reconstructed from dual coefficients.

knowledge_statements.title: Decomposed Soft-Margin Primal-Dual Gap
Support-Vector Certificate Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: KKT certificate for the binary soft-margin linear SVM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given an optimal primal-dual tuple \((w,b,\xi,\alpha)\), dual feasibility requires \(0\leq\alpha_i\leq C\) and \(\sum_i\alpha_i y_i=0\), while stationarity gives \(w=\sum_i\alpha_i y_i x_i\). Complementarity requires \(\alpha_i[y_i(w^\top x_i+b)-1+\xi_i]=0\) and \((C-\alpha_i)\xi_i=0\). Consequently, \(\alpha_i>0\) certifies that observation \(i\) is a support vector, and every index satisfying \(0<\alpha_i<C\) has \(\xi_i=0\) and \(y_i(w^\top x_i+b)=1\). Such a free support vector recovers the intercept as \(b=y_i-w^\top x_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual coefficients and KKT residuals certify support vectors; any coefficient strictly between zero and C identifies a margin point and determines the intercept.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0<\alpha_i<C\Longrightarrow \xi_i=0,\quad y_i(w^\top x_i+b)=1,\quad b=y_i-w^\top x_i

notation.meaning: dual multiplier for the ith margin constraint

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate role fits the leaf and the stated soft-margin KKT implications are mathematically standard and internally consistent. However, no source reference or inspectable locator supports the KKT system, support-vector interpretation, or intercept-recovery claim.

children.title: Degenerate SVM Certificate Regimes
children.top_down_role: Nonunique or unstable certificate behavior in degenerate data configurations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Intercept Interval Without a Free Support Vector
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recovery of all KKT-compatible intercepts when no coefficient lies strictly inside its box.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix \(C>0\), a dual optimum \(\alpha\), and \(w=\sum_i\alpha_i y_i x_i\). If no index satisfies \(0<\alpha_i<C\), every KKT-compatible intercept belongs to
\[
\left[
\max\!\left\{\max_{y_i=1,\alpha_i=0}(1-w^\top x_i),\max_{y_i=-1,\alpha_i=C}(-1-w^\top x_i)\right\},
\min\!\left\{\min_{y_i=-1,\alpha_i=0}(-1-w^\top x_i),\min_{y_i=1,\alpha_i=C}(1-w^\top x_i)\right\}
\right],
\]
where bounds over empty index sets are omitted. The interval can contain multiple values, so absence of a free support vector removes point recovery but not interval certification.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When no free support vector exists, KKT conditions still bound every valid intercept by an explicit interval, which can be non-singleton.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: b\in[b_{\min}(w,\alpha),b_{\max}(w,\alpha)].

notation.meaning: KKT-derived intercept bounds after omitting empty index sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Intercept Interval Without a Free Support Vector

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Criterion for Equivalent Optimal Dual Coefficients
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonuniqueness of soft-margin dual coefficients representing the same primal normal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(Q_{ij}=y_i y_jx_i^\top x_j\). If \(\alpha\) is dual optimal, a distinct feasible vector \(\alpha+d\) is also optimal and represents the same normal whenever
\[
y^\top d=0,\qquad Qd=0,\qquad \mathbf1^\top d=0,
\qquad 0\le\alpha+d\le C.
\]
Conversely, any two optimal dual vectors differ by a vector satisfying these relations. Thus singularity of \(Q\) alone is insufficient: an admissible null direction must also respect the equality, linear-objective, and box constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual nonuniqueness requires a feasible labeled-Gram null direction with zero coordinate sum; Gram singularity alone does not establish it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \alpha,\beta\text{ dual optimal}\Longrightarrow d=\beta-\alpha:\ Qd=0,\ y^\top d=0,\ \mathbf1^\top d=0.

notation.meaning: Difference between two dual coefficient vectors.

knowledge_statements.title: Criterion for Equivalent Optimal Dual Coefficients
Degenerate SVM Certificate Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundaries where usual support-vector or intercept certificates cease to be unique.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The standard dual certificate is degenerate in either of two regimes. If \(C=0\), the dual box constraints force \(\alpha=0\) and hence \(w=0\), while the primal intercept \(b\) is unrestricted because sufficiently large slacks remain unpenalized. If \(C>0\) but no index satisfies \(0<\alpha_i<C\), the usual equality \(b=y_i-w^\top x_i\) provides no intercept certificate. Moreover, if the labeled Gram matrix \(Q_{ij}=y_i y_j x_i^\top x_j\) is singular on the feasible dual affine space, distinct optimal vectors \(\alpha\) may represent the same primal normal \(w\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At zero penalty, or without a free support vector, the usual intercept certificate fails; singular labeled Gram matrices can also make dual coefficients nonunique.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: C=0\ \,\text{or}\ \,\{i:0<\alpha_i<C\}=\varnothing\Longrightarrow\text{the free-support-vector intercept certificate is unavailable}

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the degenerate-regime container. The zero-penalty, absent-free-support-vector, and possible dual-nonuniqueness claims require an authoritative source with a precise locator; in particular, singularity permits but does not by itself guarantee distinct optimal dual solutions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Training-point status determined from optimal dual coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At a primal-dual optimum, \alpha_i[1-\xi_i-y_i(f(x_i)+b)]=0 and (C-\alpha_i)\xi_i=0. Hence \alpha_i=0 implies \xi_i=0 and y_i(f(x_i)+b)\geq1; 0<\alpha_i<C implies \xi_i=0 and y_i(f(x_i)+b)=1; and \alpha_i=C permits a point on or inside the margin, including a misclassified point.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: KKT conditions distinguish non-support points, free support vectors on the margin, and bounded support vectors on or inside it.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0<\alpha_i<C\Longrightarrow y_i(f(x_i)+b)=1
knowledge_statements.title: Kernel SVM KKT Support-Vector Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual quadratic program for the binary kernelized C-SVM.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With K_{ij}=k(x_i,x_j), the RKHS soft-margin primal has dual \max_{\alpha}\mathbf1^\top\alpha-\frac12\alpha^\top\operatorname{Diag}(y)K\operatorname{Diag}(y)\alpha subject to 0\leq\alpha_i\leq C and y^\top\alpha=0. Since K\succeq0, the objective is concave and the feasible set is compact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Kernelization replaces feature inner products in the binary SVM dual by a positive-semidefinite Gram matrix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max_{0\leq\alpha\leq C,\ y^\top\alpha=0}\mathbf1^\top\alpha-\frac12\alpha^\top\operatorname{Diag}(y)K\operatorname{Diag}(y)\alpha
knowledge_statements.title: Kernel Soft-Margin Dual

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity and convexity boundary for direct kernel substitution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A symmetric function k defines the standard RKHS interface exactly when all its finite Gram matrices are positive semidefinite. If a supplied symmetric similarity matrix K is indefinite, the standard RKHS interpretation fails, and its quadratic form can make the usual SVM dual nonconcave on its feasible affine subspace.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive semidefiniteness is essential; an indefinite similarity does not automatically define a convex RKHS SVM.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\not\succeq0\Longrightarrow\text{the standard RKHS justification fails and dual concavity is not guaranteed}
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Semidefinite Kernel Boundary
Kernelized SVM Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary soft-margin SVM represented in a reproducing-kernel Hilbert space.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(k\) be a positive-semidefinite kernel with reproducing-kernel Hilbert space \(\mathcal H_k\) and feature map \(\phi\). The kernelized soft-margin SVM minimizes \(\frac12\lVert f\rVert_{\mathcal H_k}^2+C\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_i\) subject to \(y_i(f(x_i)+b)\geq1-\xi_i\) and \(\xi_i\geq0\). An optimizer admits the finite representation \(f(\cdot)=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i y_i k(x_i,\cdot)\), where \(0\leq\alpha_i\leq C\) and \(\sum_i\alpha_i y_i=0\). Prediction uses \(\operatorname{sign}(\sum_i\alpha_i y_i k(x_i,x)+b)\), requiring only kernel evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite kernel replaces feature inner products, and the optimal classifier is a finite expansion over training observations.
assumptions_latex: k\text{ is a positive-semidefinite kernel on }\mathcal X
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f^*(\cdot)=\sum_{i=1}^n\alpha_i^*y_i k(x_i,\cdot)

notation.meaning: RKHS induced by the kernel k
a feature map realizing the kernel

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the kernelized-interface leaf, and the RKHS primal, finite expansion, dual constraints, and prediction rule form a coherent binary soft-margin interface. No cited source or locator supports these claims.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Identifiability of joint linear multiclass scores.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For s_k(x)=w_k^\top x, prediction by \arg\max_k s_k(x) and every pairwise score difference are unchanged when the same vector a is added to every w_k. Among these equivalent parameterizations, the one minimizing \sum_k\lVert w_k\rVert_2^2 satisfies \sum_k w_k=0.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Joint multiclass decisions depend only on score differences, and minimum-norm regularization selects centered class weights.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w_k\mapsto w_k+a\ \forall k\text{ preserves predictions},\qquad\sum_kw_k=0\text{ for the minimum-norm representative}
knowledge_statements.title: Common-Score-Shift Invariance

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise binary decomposition and voting aggregation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: One-versus-one training fits a binary SVM for each unordered pair of classes using only observations from that pair. At prediction, each of the \binom K2 classifiers votes for one class, and a maximal-vote class is returned under a fixed tie rule. The binary fits are convex, but their voting aggregation is not one joint margin optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-versus-one uses one convex binary fit per class pair and aggregates their votes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: N_{\mathrm{binary}}=\binom K2
knowledge_statements.title: One-versus-One Multiclass Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of K-class prediction to K convex binary SVM fits.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each class k, define y_i^{(k)}=1 when y_i=k and -1 otherwise, and fit an independent binary SVM score s_k. Prediction returns an element of \arg\max_k s_k(x) under a fixed tie rule. The scores arise from different binary problems, so their raw magnitudes require a common scaling or calibration convention before comparison.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-versus-rest trains one binary classifier per class and predicts with the largest comparable score.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat y(x)\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{1\leq k\leq K}s_k(x)

notation.meaning: binary label for class k versus all remaining classes

knowledge_statements.title: One-versus-Rest Multiclass Interface

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Joint multiclass formulation with one slack for each incorrect class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A sum-of-hinges multiclass SVM solves \min_{W,\xi\geq0} rac12\sum_{k=1}^K\lVert w_kVert_2^2+C\sum_i\sum_{k
e y_i}\xi_{ik} subject to (w_{y_i}-w_k)^	op x_i\geq1-\xi_{ik} for every i and k
e y_i. Eliminating the slacks gives the loss \sum_{k
e y_i}[1+w_k^	op x_i-w_{y_i}^	op x_i]_+, in contrast with the single maximum hinge in the Crammer-Singer seed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Weston-Watkins variant sums the hinge violations against all incorrect classes rather than taking only their maximum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L_i(W)=\sum_{k\ne y_i}[1+w_k^\top x_i-w_{y_i}^\top x_i]_+

notation.meaning: margin slack for observation i against competing class k

knowledge_statements.title: Weston-Watkins Sum-of-Hinges Interface
Multiclass SVM Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Crammer–Singer linear multiclass hinge-loss formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For labels \(y_i\in\{1,\ldots,K\}\), associate each class with a score \(s_k(x)=w_k^\top x\). The Crammer–Singer SVM solves \(\min_{W,\xi\geq0}\frac12\sum_{k=1}^K\lVert w_k\rVert_2^2+C\sum_{i=1}^n\xi_i\) subject to \(w_{y_i}^\top x_i-w_k^\top x_i\geq1-\xi_i\) for every \(i\) and every \(k\neq y_i\). Equivalently, its loss on observation \(i\) is \(\max_{k\neq y_i}[1+w_k^\top x_i-w_{y_i}^\top x_i]_+\). The prediction interface returns \(\arg\max_{1\leq k\leq K}w_k^\top x\), with a fixed rule for ties.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Crammer–Singer SVM jointly learns one score per class by enforcing the true-class score to exceed every competing score by one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat y(x)\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_{1\leq k\leq K}w_k^{*\top}x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind is suitable for this interface, and the record consistently selects the Crammer-Singer multiclass formulation. Because the terminal title does not itself select that variant, a specific authoritative citation is needed for both the variant choice and its formulation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Residual-based characterization of dual support vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let r_i=y_i-f(x_i)-b. At an optimum, |r_i|<\varepsilon implies \alpha_i^+=\alpha_i^-=0. If 0<\alpha_i^+<C, then r_i=\varepsilon; if 0<\alpha_i^-<C, then r_i=-\varepsilon. A coefficient equal to C may correspond to a residual outside the epsilon tube.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Only observations on or outside the epsilon tube can be support vectors; free dual coefficients identify its two boundaries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: |r_i|<\varepsilon\Longrightarrow\alpha_i^+=\alpha_i^-=0
knowledge_statements.title: SVR Tube KKT Test

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual interface for linear or kernel epsilon-insensitive regression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \alpha_i^+ and \alpha_i^- be the multipliers for y_i-f(x_i)-b\leq\varepsilon+\xi_i and f(x_i)+b-y_i\leq\varepsilon+\xi_i^*. The dual is \max_{0\leq\alpha^+,\alpha^-\leq C}-\frac12(\alpha^+-\alpha^-)^\top K(\alpha^+-\alpha^-)-\varepsilon\mathbf1^\top(\alpha^++\alpha^-)+y^\top(\alpha^+-\alpha^-) subject to \mathbf1^\top(\alpha^+-\alpha^-)=0. The fitted RKHS component is f(\cdot)=\sum_i(\alpha_i^+-\alpha_i^-)k(x_i,\cdot).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Epsilon-SVR has paired bounded dual coefficients whose difference forms the kernel predictor.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f^*(\cdot)=\sum_i(\alpha_i^{+*}-\alpha_i^{-*})k(x_i,\cdot)

notation.meaning: dual coefficients for the upper and lower residual inequalities

knowledge_statements.title: Epsilon-SVR Dual and Kernel Expansion

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard SVR variant that optimizes the tube width.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A normalized nu-SVR formulation is \min_{f,b,\varepsilon,\xi,\xi^*}\frac12\lVert f\rVert_{\mathcal H_k}^2+C\left(\nu\varepsilon+\frac1n\sum_i(\xi_i+\xi_i^*)\right) subject to y_i-f(x_i)-b\leq\varepsilon+\xi_i, f(x_i)+b-y_i\leq\varepsilon+\xi_i^*, and \varepsilon,\xi_i,\xi_i^*\geq0. Unlike epsilon-SVR, the insensitive width is optimized rather than fixed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nu-SVR jointly chooses the insensitive tube width through a convex objective controlled by nu.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \varepsilon\text{ is an optimization variable in nu-SVR}

notation.meaning: coefficient controlling the optimized insensitive-tube term

knowledge_statements.title: Nu-SVR Interface
Support Vector Regression Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear epsilon-insensitive soft-margin support-vector regression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For responses \(y_i\in\mathbb R\), epsilon-insensitive support-vector regression solves \(\min_{w,b,\xi,\xi^*}\frac12\lVert w\rVert_2^2+C\sum_{i=1}^n(\xi_i+\xi_i^*)\) subject to \(y_i-w^\top x_i-b\leq\varepsilon+\xi_i\), \(w^\top x_i+b-y_i\leq\varepsilon+\xi_i^*\), and \(\xi_i,\xi_i^*\geq0\). This is equivalent to regularized empirical risk with loss \(L_\varepsilon(y,t)=[|y-t|-\varepsilon]_+\). The fitted output is \(\widehat y(x)=w^{*\top}x+b^*\); observations strictly inside the epsilon tube have zero loss and need not carry nonzero dual coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support vector regression fits a regularized affine predictor while ignoring residuals within an epsilon-wide tube and penalizing only excess deviations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat y(x)=w^{*\top}x+b^*,\qquad L_\varepsilon(y,t)=[|y-t|-\varepsilon]_+

notation.meaning: half-width of the insensitive residual tube

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the regression-interface leaf, and the primal constraints, epsilon-insensitive loss, fitted output, and interior-tube observation are mutually consistent. No authoritative source or specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Nonseparable Data Regimes
children.top_down_role: SVM application regimes lacking complete class separation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite-sample certificate for failure of affine strict separation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let I_+=\{i:y_i=1\} and I_-=\{i:y_i=-1\}, with both classes nonempty. Strict affine separation fails if and only if \operatorname{conv}\{x_i:i\in I_+\}\cap\operatorname{conv}\{x_i:i\in I_-\}\ne\varnothing. Equivalently, there exists \alpha\geq0, \alpha\ne0, such that \sum_i\alpha_i y_i=0 and \sum_i\alpha_i y_i x_i=0. These coefficients certify infeasibility of the hard-margin constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Intersecting class convex hulls, equivalently a balanced nonnegative affine dependence, exactly certify finite-sample nonseparability and hard-margin infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{nonseparable}\iff\exists\alpha\geq0:\ \alpha\ne0,\ \sum_i\alpha_i y_i=0,\ \sum_i\alpha_i y_i x_i=0
knowledge_statements.title: Convex-Hull Certificate of Nonseparability

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual manifestation of hard-margin infeasibility for a finite sample containing both labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The hard-margin dual is \sup_{\alpha\geq0,\ y^\top\alpha=0}\mathbf1^\top\alpha-\frac12\lVert\sum_i\alpha_i y_i x_i\rVert_2^2. If d\geq0 is a nonzero convex-hull certificate with y^\top d=0 and \sum_i d_i y_i x_i=0, then \alpha=td is dual feasible and has objective t\mathbf1^\top d\to+\infty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A nonseparability certificate generates an unbounded feasible ray in the hard-margin dual.
assumptions_latex: \{(x_i,y_i)\}_{i=1}^n\text{ is a finite nonseparable binary sample}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{\alpha\geq0,\ y^\top\alpha=0}\left(\mathbf1^\top\alpha-\frac12\left\lVert\sum_i\alpha_i y_i x_i\right\rVert_2^2\right)=+\infty
knowledge_statements.title: Hard-Margin Dual Ray Under Nonseparability
Nonseparable Data Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility boundary between hard-margin and slack-penalized binary SVMs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For finitely many labeled observations, the hard-margin constraints \(y_i(w^\top x_i+b)\geq1\) are feasible exactly when the data are strictly linearly separable: any strict separator can be positively rescaled to attain unit functional margin. Thus nonseparable data make the hard-margin primal infeasible. Introducing slacks \(\xi_i\geq0\) and constraints \(y_i(w^\top x_i+b)\geq1-\xi_i\) restores feasibility for every finite dataset, because sufficiently large slacks always satisfy the constraints. For \(C>0\), the soft-margin objective \(\frac12\lVert w\rVert_2^2+C\sum_i\xi_i\) trades norm against total hinge violation rather than certifying separability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hard-margin SVM is infeasible on nonseparable data, whereas nonnegative slacks make the soft-margin problem feasible and quantify margin violations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nexists(w,b):y_i(w^\top x_i+b)>0\ \forall i\Longrightarrow\text{hard-margin infeasibility, while soft-margin feasibility holds}

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind correctly matches the separability-regime leaf. The finite-sample equivalence between strict separability and hard-margin feasibility, together with universal soft-margin feasibility, is stated precisely but has no supporting citation or locator.

children.title: Feature-Scaling Sensitivity
children.top_down_role: Dependence of margin geometry on feature units or preprocessing choices.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Special scaling regime in which retuning regularization preserves an SVM fit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[\min_{w,b}\frac\lambda2\|w\|_2^2+\frac1n\sum_i[1-y_i(w^\top x_i+b)]_+.\] If \(z_i=cx_i\) with \(c\ne0\), then \(w'=w/c\) preserves every score. Choosing \(\lambda'=c^2\lambda\) makes the scaled-coordinate objective identical under this substitution. Thus uniform feature scaling can be compensated exactly, whereas unequal coordinate scaling generally cannot be compensated by one scalar regularization parameter.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A common feature scale can be offset by rescaling the SVM regularization parameter, but anisotropic scaling changes the penalty metric.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w'=w/c,\quad\lambda'=c^2\lambda\Longrightarrow w'^\top z_i+b=w^\top x_i+b\ \text{and the objectives agree}.

notation.meaning: Compensating regularization parameter in scaled coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Scaling Compensation
Feature-Scaling Sensitivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Effect of invertible coordinate scaling on the Euclidean SVM regularizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let transformed features be \(z=Dx\), where \(D\) is an invertible diagonal matrix, and fit a linear SVM using the Euclidean penalty \(\frac12\lVert w\rVert_2^2\). Writing the same score in original coordinates as \(w^\top Dx=v^\top x\) gives \(v=D^\top w\). Therefore the transformed-feature penalty equals \(\frac12v^\top(DD^\top)^{-1}v\), not \(\frac12\lVert v\rVert_2^2\) unless \(DD^\top\) is a scalar multiple of the identity. Coordinatewise rescaling consequently changes the implicit metric, the regularization tradeoff, and generally the fitted separating hyperplane.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unequal coordinate scaling changes the metric used by the SVM norm penalty, so it can change both the optimizer and predictions.
assumptions_latex: D\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d}\text{ is invertible and diagonal}
\text{the SVM uses the Euclidean norm penalty}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \frac12\lVert w\rVert_2^2=\frac12v^\top(DD^\top)^{-1}v,\qquad v=D^\top w

notation.meaning: equivalent normal vector in original coordinates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the sensitivity leaf, and the coordinate transformation and induced quadratic metric are algebraically consistent. The resulting optimizer and prediction sensitivity claim lacks an authoritative source with a specific locator.

children.title: Scaling-Induced Margin Distortion
children.top_down_role: Decision-boundary distortions caused by poorly balanced feature scales.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Anisotropic Scaling Can Change the Maximum-Margin Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A separable three-point sample witnessing strict scaling-induced boundary distortion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Take positive points a=(1,1), q=(2,-1) and the negative point 0. In the original Euclidean metric the nearest point of \operatorname{conv}\{a,q\} to 0 is p=(6/5,3/5), giving the bisecting maximum-margin boundary 4x_1+2x_2=3. Under D=\operatorname{diag}(2,1), the transformed positive points are (2,1) and (4,-1); the nearest point is (2,1), and the pulled-back boundary is 8x_1+2x_2=5. The boundaries differ although invertibility of D preserves separability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A three-point separable sample shows that anisotropic scaling can change the maximum-margin decision boundary without changing separability.
knowledge_statements.title: Anisotropic Scaling Can Change the Maximum-Margin Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact original-coordinate form of a soft-margin SVM trained after invertible feature scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For z_i=Dx_i with D invertible, the scaled-coordinate problem \min_{w,b}\frac12\lVert w\rVert_2^2+C\sum_i[1-y_i(w^\top z_i+b)]_+ is equivalent under v=D^\top w to \min_{v,b}\frac12v^\top(DD^\top)^{-1}v+C\sum_i[1-y_i(v^\top x_i+b)]_+. Thus scaling preserves the attainable affine scores but changes the regularization metric.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Invertible feature scaling is exactly an anisotropic quadratic regularizer in the original coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \lVert w\rVert_2^2=v^\top(DD^\top)^{-1}v\quad\text{for }v=D^\top w

notation.meaning: hyperplane normal in the original coordinates

knowledge_statements.title: Scaling as Anisotropic Regularization
Scaling-Induced Margin Distortion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Geometric margin measured after anisotropic feature scaling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under the invertible scaling \(z=Dx\), a hyperplane represented in original coordinates by \(v^\top x+b=0\) has scaled-coordinate normal \(w=D^{-\top}v\). Its geometric margin for an observation \((x_i,y_i)\), when distance is measured in scaled Euclidean coordinates, is \(y_i(v^\top x_i+b)/\lVert D^{-\top}v\rVert_2\). Hence anisotropic scaling replaces the original denominator \(\lVert v\rVert_2\) by the metric-dependent denominator \(\sqrt{v^\top D^{-1}D^{-\top}v}\). Margins are preserved up to one common factor only for conformal scalings \(D^\top D=cI\) with \(c>0\); otherwise their geometry is direction dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Anisotropic scaling measures margins in a different metric, distorting hyperplane directions and relative distances unless the scaling is conformal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \gamma_i^{(D)}=\frac{y_i(v^\top x_i+b)}{\sqrt{v^\top D^{-1}D^{-\top}v}}

notation.meaning: signed geometric margin in scaled coordinates

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the margin-distortion leaf, and the displayed transformed-margin formula is consistent. The claim that preservation up to a common factor occurs only for conformal scalings must be understood uniformly over all normal directions; that quantifier should be confirmed by a cited source and made explicit in any sourced revision.

children.title: Hinge-Loss Surrogate Interface
children.top_down_role: Use of hinge loss as an application-facing classification surrogate.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional epigraph representation for linear soft-margin SVMs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(f(x)=w^\top x+b\), \[\min_{w,b}\frac\lambda2\|w\|_2^2+\frac1n\sum_i[1-y_i(w^\top x_i+b)]_+\] is equivalent to \[\min_{w,b,\xi}\frac\lambda2\|w\|_2^2+\frac1n\sum_i\xi_i\quad\text{s.t.}\quad y_i(w^\top x_i+b)\ge1-\xi_i,\quad\xi_i\ge0.\] Thus the Euclidean-regularized linear hinge interface is a convex quadratic program. A polyhedral convex regularizer instead gives an LP-representable model after its epigraph lift.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Slack variables turn empirical linear hinge minimization into the standard soft-margin convex program.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \xi_i^*=[1-y_i(w^\top x_i+b)]_+\ \text{at every optimum}.
knowledge_statements.title: Slack-Variable Hinge-Loss Interface
Hinge-Loss Surrogate Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary hinge loss as a convex surrogate for misclassification loss.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a binary label \(y\in\{-1,1\}\) and real score \(t\in\mathbb R\), the hinge loss is \(\ell_{\mathrm h}(y,t)=[1-yt]_+=\max\{0,1-yt\}\). It is convex and piecewise affine in \(t\), and it upper-bounds the zero-one loss: \(\mathbf 1\{yt\leq0\}\leq\ell_{\mathrm h}(y,t)\). For a score function \(f\) in a normed hypothesis space, the regularized empirical interface minimizes \(\frac{\lambda}{2}\lVert f\rVert^2+\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n\ell_{\mathrm h}(y_i,f(x_i))\), where \(\lambda>0\). Classification returns \(\operatorname{sign}(f(x))\), subject to a declared convention at zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Hinge loss convexly upper-bounds classification error and yields the standard regularized empirical-risk interface for binary SVM classification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell_{\mathrm h}(y,t)=[1-yt]_+,\qquad \mathbf 1\{yt\leq0\}\leq\ell_{\mathrm h}(y,t)

notation.meaning: positive part, equal to the maximum of u and zero

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind is acceptable for the surrogate-interface leaf, and the hinge-loss definition, convexity, zero-one upper bound, regularized risk, and prediction interface agree. No source or inspectable locator is provided.

children.title: Classification Calibration Boundary
children.top_down_role: Regimes governing alignment between surrogate optimization and classification decisions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Population binary classification calibration in excess-risk form.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a deterministic convention assigning a label \(\widehat y_f(x)\in\{-1,1\}\) when \(f(x)=0\), and define \(R_{01}(f)=\mathbb P(Y\ne\widehat y_f(X))\) and \(R_h(f)=\mathbb E[1-Yf(X)]_+\). If \(R_{01}^*\) and \(R_h^*\) are the unrestricted Bayes infima, then \[R_{01}(f)-R_{01}^*\le R_h(f)-R_h^*.\] Hence convergence to optimal population hinge risk implies convergence to Bayes classification risk. Restricted hypothesis classes additionally require approximation and estimation control.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary zero-one excess risk is bounded by hinge excess risk, so unrestricted population hinge-risk consistency implies Bayes classification consistency.
assumptions_latex: \widehat y_f\text{ uses a fixed deterministic convention at }f=0

notation.meaning: Binary misclassification risk under the declared tie convention.

review_flags: corrected_builder_statement: replaced the incompatible expression P(Yf(X)<=0), which counts a zero score as an error for both labels, by an explicit label-valued tie convention
knowledge_statements.title: Hinge Excess-Risk Calibration Inequality
Classification Calibration Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pointwise binary classification calibration of hinge loss, including the tie boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\eta=\mathbb P(Y=1\mid X=x)\) and define the conditional hinge risk \(R_\eta(t)=\eta[1-t]_++(1-\eta)[1+t]_+\). Its minimizer set is \(\{1\}\) when \(\eta>1/2\), \(\{-1\}\) when \(\eta<1/2\), and \([-1,1]\) when \(\eta=1/2\). Therefore every conditional minimizer has the Bayes-optimal classification sign whenever \(\eta\neq1/2\). At the boundary \(\eta=1/2\), both classes have equal Bayes risk and hinge minimization does not select a unique sign. Thus calibration holds for binary classification, with indeterminacy precisely at the Bayes tie.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Conditional hinge-risk minimizers have the Bayes-optimal sign away from probability one-half; at one-half, every score between minus one and one minimizes risk.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \eta\neq\frac12\Longrightarrow \operatorname{sign}(t^*)=\operatorname{sign}\!\left(\eta-\frac12\right)\quad\text{for every }t^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_tR_\eta(t)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the calibration-boundary leaf. The conditional-risk minimizer sets and Bayes-tie qualification are mathematically coherent, but the calibration result has no authoritative citation or specific locator.

children.title: Probability-Estimation Limitation
children.top_down_role: Limits of margin outputs as direct probability estimates.

knowledge_statements.title: Probability-Estimation Limitation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of uncalibrated hinge-risk scores to identify class probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For conditional class probability \(\eta\in(1/2,1)\), the conditional hinge risk \(R_\eta(t)=\eta[1-t]_++(1-\eta)[1+t]_+\) has the unique minimizer \(t^*=1\), independently of the numerical value of \(\eta\). Likewise, every \(\eta\in(0,1/2)\) yields \(t^*=-1\). Hence the population-optimal hinge score is not an injective function of \(\eta\): for example, \(\eta=0.6\) and \(\eta=0.9\) produce the same optimal score. No fixed inverse link applied solely to an uncalibrated optimal hinge score can therefore recover general conditional probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Optimal hinge scores collapse all probabilities above one-half to one and all probabilities below one-half to minus one, preventing direct probability recovery.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \eta_1\neq\eta_2,\quad \eta_1,\eta_2>\frac12\Longrightarrow \operatorname*{arg\,min}_tR_{\eta_1}(t)=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_tR_{\eta_2}(t)=\{1\}

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the probability-estimation limitation. The noninjectivity argument is precise for population-optimal, uncalibrated hinge scores, but no cited source or locator supports the minimizer characterization or inverse-link limitation.

children.title: Logistic Likelihood Models
children.top_down_role: Likelihood-based classification and binary-response estimation templates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact first-order certificate for convexly regularized logistic regression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r\) be proper, closed, and convex and leave the intercept unpenalized. A finite parameter \(\widehat w=(\widehat\beta,\widehat b)\) minimizes \(L(\beta,b)+r(\beta)\) if and only if \(0\in Z^\top(\widehat p-y)+(\partial r(\widehat\beta),0)\), where \(\widehat p_i=\sigma(z_i^\top\widehat w)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A logistic parameter is optimal exactly when the likelihood score is canceled by a coefficient-penalty subgradient.
assumptions_latex: The objective is proper at \(\widehat w\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in Z^\top(\widehat p-y)+(\partial r(\widehat\beta),0).
knowledge_statements.title: Regularized Logistic Optimality Condition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recession boundary for an unregularized finite-parameter binary logistic MLE.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write \(s_i=2y_i-1\). If a nonzero direction \(v\) satisfies \(s_i z_i^\top v\ge0\) for every observation and the inequality is strict for at least one observation, the unregularized logistic likelihood improves along a ray and has no finite maximizer. Complete separation, where all inequalities are strict, is a special case and gives \(\inf L=0\). If no such improving recession direction exists, a finite minimizer exists modulo directions on which every \(z_i^\top v=0\); full column rank then removes those flat directions. A coercive convex regularizer restores attainment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete or quasi-complete separation prevents a finite unregularized logistic MLE; absence of an improving recession direction gives attainment, with rank controlling uniqueness.
assumptions_latex: No coercive regularizer is present in the nonattainment statement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[\exists v:\ s_i z_i^\top v\ge0\ \forall i,\ \max_i s_i z_i^\top v>0\bigr]\Longrightarrow\operatorname*{argmin}L=\varnothing.
knowledge_statements.title: Separation and Finite-MLE Existence Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differential structure of binary logistic negative log-likelihood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With augmented rows \(z_i^\top=(x_i^\top,1)\), \(w=(\beta,b)\), \(p_i=\sigma(z_i^\top w)\), \(Z\) the augmented design, and \(W=\operatorname{diag}(p_i(1-p_i))\), the negative log-likelihood satisfies \(\nabla L(w)=Z^\top(p-y)\) and \(\nabla^2L(w)=Z^\top WZ\succeq0\). At every finite \(w\), it is strictly convex if and only if \(Z\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Logistic loss has a probability-residual score and positive-semidefinite weighted-Gram Hessian; full augmented-design rank gives strict convexity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \nabla L(w)=Z^\top(p-y),\qquad \nabla^2L(w)=Z^\top WZ\succeq0.
knowledge_statements.title: Logistic Score and Curvature
Logistic Likelihood Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Binary logistic model and its convex negative log-likelihood.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For covariates \(x_i\in\mathbb R^d\) and labels \(y_i\in\{0,1\}\), a logistic likelihood model specifies \(\mathbb P(Y_i=1\mid x_i)=\sigma(\beta^\top x_i+b)\), where \(\sigma(t)=(1+e^{-t})^{-1}\). Under conditional independence, the negative log-likelihood is \(L(\beta,b)=\sum_{i=1}^n[\log(1+e^{\beta^\top x_i+b})-y_i(\beta^\top x_i+b)]\). This function is convex in \((\beta,b)\). Adding any convex regularizer \(r(\beta)\) preserves convexity, giving the estimation problem \(\min_{\beta,b}L(\beta,b)+r(\beta)\). The fitted probability is \(\widehat p(x)=\sigma(\widehat\beta^\top x+\widehat b)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary logistic regression models class probability through the sigmoid; its negative log-likelihood is convex, and remains convex after adding a convex regularizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: (\widehat\beta,\widehat b)\in\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{\beta,b}\left\{L(\beta,b)+r(\beta)\right\},\qquad \widehat p(x)=\sigma(\widehat\beta^\top x+\widehat b)

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition kind fits the logistic-likelihood leaf, and the model, negative log-likelihood, and convexity claims are standard. No relevant source is supplied. In addition, an arbitrary extended-real convex regularizer need not ensure that the displayed argmin is attained, so a sourced version should either assume existence of a minimizer or state the fitted-probability formula conditionally on attainment.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Logistic maximum likelihood under strict linear separation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the binary logistic likelihood representation, corrects the separation boundary to nonattainment of a zero infimum, and records the probability-one-half classification rule under the logistic model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let s_i=a^Tx_i-b and r_j=a^Ty_j-b for samples x_i labeled 1 and y_j labeled 0. The negative log-likelihood is
\[
L(a,b)=\sum_{i=1}^N\log\!\left(1+e^{-s_i}\right)+\sum_{j=1}^M\log\!\left(1+e^{r_j}\right),
\]
which is convex in \((a,b)\). If there exist \((\bar a,\bar b)\) such that \(\bar a^Tx_i-\bar b>0\) for every \(i\) and \(\bar a^Ty_j-\bar b<0\) for every \(j\), then \(L(\tau\bar a,\tau\bar b)\to0\) as \(\tau\to\infty\). Hence \(\inf_{a,b}L(a,b)=0\), but no finite \((a,b)\) attains this value. Under the logistic conditional model \(\Pr(z=1\mid u)=e^{a^Tu-b}/(1+e^{a^Tu-b})\), thresholding at \(a^Tu-b=0\) is equivalent to thresholding the class probability at \(1/2\) and minimizes misclassification probability among linear classifiers under the stated model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Binary logistic fitting minimizes a convex negative log-likelihood. For strictly linearly separable samples, that objective is bounded below by zero and approaches zero as the separating parameters are scaled, but it has no finite minimizer. Under the logistic model, the zero-score hyperplane is the one-half-probability decision boundary and gives the minimum-error linear classification rule.
assumptions_latex: x_i\text{ has label }1\text{ and }y_j\text{ has label }0
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: L\text{ is convex};\quad \bigl[\exists(\bar a,\bar b):\bar a^Tx_i-\bar b>0\ (\forall i),\ \bar a^Ty_j-\bar b<0\ (\forall j)\bigr]\Longrightarrow \inf L=0\text{ with no finite minimizer};\quad \widehat z(u)=\mathbf 1\{a^Tu-b\ge0\}\text{ is the probability-}\tfrac12\text{ linear rule under the model}.
