knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimality and sufficient uniqueness certificate for a fixed noiseless signal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For feasible \(x_0\), with \(S=\operatorname{supp}(x_0)\), optimality is equivalent to existence of \(u\) satisfying \[(A^{\mathsf T}u)_S=\operatorname{sign}((x_0)_S),\qquad\|(A^{\mathsf T}u)_{S^c}\|_\infty\le1.\] If \(A_S\) has full column rank and the off-support inequality is strict, \(x_0\) is the unique optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A range-space vector matching signs on the support and bounded off it certifies optimality; strictness and support injectivity certify uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_0\text{ is optimal}\iff\exists u:\ A^{\mathsf T}u\in\partial\|x_0\|_1.
review_flags: uniqueness condition stated only as sufficient
knowledge_statements.title: Range-Space Dual Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact linear-program form of noiseless basis pursuit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Noiseless basis pursuit is equivalently \[\min_{x,t}\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}t\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=y,\qquad-t\le x\le t.\] Projection of the LP solution set onto \(x\) gives exactly the basis-pursuit solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Introducing absolute-value epigraph variables expresses noiseless basis pursuit as an LP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x\operatorname*{argmin}_{x,t}\{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}t:Ax=y,-t\le x\le t\}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{Ax=y}\|x\|_1.
knowledge_statements.title: Basis-Pursuit Linear Program

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp uniform exact-recovery characterization for noiseless basis pursuit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every \(s\)-sparse vector is uniquely recovered by basis pursuit if and only if, for every \(0\ne h\in\ker A\) and every \(|S|\le s\), \[\|h_S\|_1<\|h_{S^c}\|_1.\] Failure of this inequality produces a sparse measurement instance for which uniform unique l1 recovery fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The strict null-space property is necessary and sufficient for uniform unique recovery of all s-sparse vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\text{ uniformly and uniquely recovers all s-sparse vectors by BP}\iff\forall0\ne h\in\ker A,\ |S|\le s:\ \|h_S\|_1<\|h_{S^c}\|_1.

notation.meaning: restriction of h to coordinates in S

knowledge_statements.title: Null-Space Property Characterization
Noiseless Basis-Pursuit Application
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact sparse recovery from noiseless linear measurements by an ℓ1 program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a sensing matrix \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and noiseless observations \(y=Ax_0\), basis pursuit computes \[\widehat x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\|x\|_1\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=y.\] This is a convex relaxation of minimum-support recovery. If \(x_0\) is the unique minimizer—under, for example, an appropriate null-space property—then \(\widehat x=x_0\). The equality constraint represents the noiseless observation regime and requires \(y\in\operatorname{range}(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noiseless basis pursuit recovers a sparse signal by minimizing its ℓ1 norm over all vectors exactly matching the measurements.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{\|x\|_1:Ax=y\}\), and uniqueness of \(x_0\) implies \(\widehat x=x_0\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly describes noiseless basis pursuit and fits the application leaf, but no authoritative compressed-sensing citation is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual program and primal-dual certificate for basis-pursuit denoising.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The dual of BPDN is \[\max_{u\in\mathbb R^m}\ y^{\mathsf T}u-\varepsilon\|u\|_2\quad\text{subject to}\quad \|A^{\mathsf T}u\|_\infty\le1.\] Weak duality always holds. If \(\varepsilon>0\) and the residual constraint is strictly feasible, or if \(\varepsilon=0\) and \(Ax=y\) is feasible, strong duality holds. Feasible \(x,u\) are optimal exactly when \[\|x\|_1=y^{\mathsf T}u-\varepsilon\|u\|_2.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: BPDN has an infinity-norm-constrained dual; equality of feasible primal and dual values certifies optimality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^*=d^*=\max_{\|A^{\mathsf T}u\|_\infty\le1}(y^{\mathsf T}u-\varepsilon\|u\|_2).
review_flags: qualification sharpened for positive and zero tolerance
knowledge_statements.title: BPDN Dual and Optimality Certificate

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-dimensional conic representation of BPDN.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: BPDN is equivalently \[\min_{x,t}\ \mathbf1^{\mathsf T}t\quad\text{subject to}\quad -t\le x\le t,\qquad (\varepsilon,Ax-y)\in\mathcal Q_{m+1},\] where \(\mathcal Q_{m+1}=\{(s,r):\|r\|_2\le s\}\). Projection of its solution set onto \(x\) gives exactly the BPDN solution set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Epigraphing the l1 norm and conically representing the residual makes BPDN an SOCP.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname*{argmin}_x\{\|x\|_1:\|Ax-y\|_2\le\varepsilon\}=\operatorname{proj}_x\operatorname*{argmin}_{x,t}\{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}t:-t\le x\le t,(\varepsilon,Ax-y)\in\mathcal Q_{m+1}\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Second-Order-Cone Representation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stable and robust BPDN recovery under the l1 robust null-space property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(A\) has the \(\ell_1\) robust null-space property of order \(s\), \[\|h_S\|_1\le\rho\|h_{S^c}\|_1+\tau\|Ah\|_2,\qquad 0\le\rho<1,\] then every BPDN minimizer satisfies \[\|\widehat x-x_0\|_1\le\frac{2(1+\rho)}{1-\rho}\sigma_s(x_0)_1+\frac{4\tau}{1-\rho}\varepsilon.\] Uniform control degenerates as \(\rho\uparrow1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust null-space property bounds BPDN error by best sparse-approximation error plus observation noise.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|\widehat x-x_0\|_1\le \frac{2(1+\rho)}{1-\rho}\sigma_s(x_0)_1+\frac{4\tau}{1-\rho}\varepsilon.

notation.meaning: best s-term approximation error in l1

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Null-Space Recovery Bound
Basis-Pursuit Denoising Application
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noise-aware ℓ1 recovery with a prescribed residual tolerance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), observations \(y=Ax_0+e\), and a known bound \(\|e\|_2\le\varepsilon\), basis-pursuit denoising computes \[\widehat x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\|x\|_1\quad\text{subject to}\quad \|Ax-y\|_2\le\varepsilon.\] The true signal \(x_0\) is feasible whenever the noise bound is valid. At \(\varepsilon=0\), the formulation reduces to noiseless basis pursuit. Recovery accuracy beyond feasibility requires an additional sensing condition such as a robust null-space property or restricted isometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Basis-pursuit denoising minimizes ℓ1 norm while allowing a residual no larger than a known noise bound; zero tolerance recovers ordinary basis pursuit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{\|x\|_1:\|Ax-y\|_2\le\varepsilon\}\), with \(x_0\) feasible.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The constrained noise-aware representation is precise and appropriately scoped, but it lacks an authoritative citation with a section, theorem, or page locator.

children.title: Lagrangian Sparse-Recovery Interface
children.top_down_role: Sparse-recovery applications using a penalized residual-versus-sparsity representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Canonical first-order algorithms for l1-penalized least squares.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: With \(L=\|A\|_2^2\), ISTA uses \[x^{k+1}=S_{t\lambda}(x^k-tA^{\mathsf T}(Ax^k-y)),\qquad0<t\le1/L.\] Its objective gap is \(O(1/k)\); at \(t=1/L\), \[F(x^k)-F(x^*)\le\frac{L\|x^0-x^*\|_2^2}{2k}.\] The standard accelerated proximal-gradient variant has objective gap \(O(1/k^2)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: ISTA alternates a gradient step and soft thresholding; acceleration improves the objective rate from O(1/k) to O(1/k²).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F(x^k)-F(x^*)=O(1/k)\text{ for ISTA and }O(1/k^2)\text{ for its standard accelerated variant}.
review_flags: standard ISTA and accelerated proximal-gradient rates
knowledge_statements.title: ISTA and Accelerated Variant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fenchel dual and zero-gap certificate for penalized sparse recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The dual is \[\max_{u\in\mathbb R^m}\ y^{\mathsf T}u-\frac12\|u\|_2^2\quad\text{subject to}\quad\|A^{\mathsf T}u\|_\infty\le\lambda.\] Strong duality holds. A feasible pair is optimal exactly when \(u=y-Ax\) and \(A^{\mathsf T}u\in\lambda\partial\|x\|_1\), equivalently when its primal and dual values agree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lasso dual is a concave quadratic over a correlation ball, and its optimal variable is the fitted residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^*=\max_{\|A^{\mathsf T}u\|_\infty\le\lambda}(y^{\mathsf T}u-\tfrac12\|u\|_2^2),\quad u^*=y-A\widehat x.
knowledge_statements.title: Lasso Fenchel Dual

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniqueness of fitted values and boundary of coefficient uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(x_1,x_2\) are minimizers, then \[Ax_1=Ax_2,\qquad\|x_1\|_1=\|x_2\|_1.\] Thus the residual and dual solution are unique, but coefficients can be nonunique. Full column rank of \(A\) is sufficient, though not necessary, for coefficient uniqueness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lasso minimizers share the same fitted value and l1 norm, although their coefficient vectors can differ.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Ax_1=Ax_2\quad\text{and}\quad\|x_1\|_1=\|x_2\|_1.
review_flags: strict convexity in the fitted value
knowledge_statements.title: Shared Fit and Coefficient-Nonuniqueness Boundary
Lagrangian Sparse-Recovery Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalized least-squares interface for convex sparse recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\lambda>0\), the Lagrangian sparse-recovery problem is \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\frac12\|Ax-y\|_2^2+\lambda\|x\|_1.\] A vector \(\widehat x\) is optimal exactly when there exists \(z\in\partial\|\widehat x\|_1\) such that \[A^{\mathsf T}(y-A\widehat x)=\lambda z,\qquad z_j=\operatorname{sign}(\widehat x_j)\ \text{if }\widehat x_j\ne0,\quad |z_j|\le1\ \text{otherwise}.\] Thus \(\lambda\) directly bounds the correlations between predictors and the fitted residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Lagrangian interface balances squared residual and ℓ1 sparsity. Optimality is certified by residual correlations matching an ℓ1 subgradient scaled by the penalty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x\) is optimal if and only if \(A^{\mathsf T}(y-A\widehat x)\in\lambda\partial\|\widehat x\|_1\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: lasso formulation and subgradient optimality condition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The penalized formulation and subgradient optimality condition are correct and fit the interface leaf, but no supporting source is cited.

children.title: Dantzig-Selector Interface
children.top_down_role: Sparse-recovery applications using a correlation-constrained representation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact deterministic condition for feasibility of the true signal.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under \(y=Ax_0+e\), \[A^{\mathsf T}(y-Ax_0)=A^{\mathsf T}e.\] Hence \(x_0\) is Dantzig-feasible exactly when \(\|A^{\mathsf T}e\|_\infty\le\lambda\). An energy bound alone yields this only through \(\|A^{\mathsf T}e\|_\infty\le(\max_j\|a_j\|_2)\|e\|_2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The true signal is feasible exactly when all sensing-column correlations with the noise are within the tolerance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x_0\text{ is feasible}\iff\|A^{\mathsf T}e\|_\infty\le\lambda.
knowledge_statements.title: Correlation-Noise Calibration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact linear-program representation of the Dantzig selector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The Dantzig selector is equivalently \[\min_{x,t}\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}t\quad\text{subject to}\quad-t\le x\le t,\quad-\lambda\mathbf1\le A^{\mathsf T}(y-Ax)\le\lambda\mathbf1.\] Its projected \(x\)-solution set equals that of the norm formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Dantzig selector is an LP after epigraphing the l1 objective and expanding its infinity-norm constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x\operatorname*{argmin}_{x,t}\{\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}t:-t\le x\le t,-\lambda\mathbf1\le A^{\mathsf T}(y-Ax)\le\lambda\mathbf1\}\text{ equals the Dantzig solution set}.
knowledge_statements.title: Dantzig Linear-Program Representation
Dantzig-Selector Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse recovery constrained by predictor-residual correlations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(y\in\mathbb R^m\), and \(\lambda\ge0\), the Dantzig-selector interface is \[\widehat x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\|x\|_1\quad\text{subject to}\quad \|A^{\mathsf T}(y-Ax)\|_\infty\le\lambda.\] The constraint bounds every columnwise correlation between the residual and the sensing matrix. It is convex because the objective is a norm and the feasible set is the inverse image of an \(\ell_\infty\)-ball under an affine mapping.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Dantzig selector minimizes ℓ1 norm subject to uniformly bounded correlations between each sensing column and the observation residual.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{\|x\|_1:\|A^{\mathsf T}(y-Ax)\|_\infty\le\lambda\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Dantzig-selector representation is correctly formulated and matches the container, but it has no authoritative source reference with a specific locator.

children.title: Sparse-Recovery Tuning Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Regime-dependent relationships among tuning choices across the two interfaces.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact upper endpoint of the penalized tuning path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The zero vector is lasso-optimal exactly when \[A^{\mathsf T}y\in\lambda[-1,1]^n,\] equivalently \[\lambda\ge\lambda_{\max}:=\|A^{\mathsf T}y\|_\infty.\] At equality, nonzero optima can coexist if coefficient uniqueness fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The lasso solution includes zero exactly when the penalty reaches the maximum predictor-observation correlation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{\tfrac12\|Ax-y\|_2^2+\lambda\|x\|_1\}\iff\lambda\ge\|A^{\mathsf T}y\|_\infty.

notation.meaning: smallest penalty for which zero is optimal

knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Solution Tuning Threshold

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Ordering of residual and l1 levels along the penalized path.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(0<\lambda_1<\lambda_2\) and \(x_i\) minimizes \(r(x)+\lambda_i\|x\|_1\), then \[\|x_2\|_1\le\|x_1\|_1,\qquad r(x_1)\le r(x_2),\quad r(x)=\tfrac12\|Ax-y\|_2^2.\] The inequalities can be non-strict, so tuning-to-level mappings need not be one-to-one.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Increasing the l1 penalty cannot increase the selected l1 norm or decrease the residual, but flat path segments prevent a bijection.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|x_2\|_1\le\|x_1\|_1\quad\text{and}\quad r(x_1)\le r(x_2).
knowledge_statements.title: Pareto Monotonicity and Non-Bijection

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Qualified converse from an active residual constraint to a penalized solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\bar x\) solve \(\min\{\|x\|_1:r(x)\le\tau\}\). If the constraint is active and Slater's condition holds, a positive KKT multiplier \(\mu\) may be selected so that \[0\in\partial\|\bar x\|_1+\mu A^{\mathsf T}(A\bar x-y).\] With \(\lambda=1/\mu\), \(\bar x\) solves \(\min_x r(x)+\lambda\|x\|_1\). Inactivity or absence of a positive multiplier can prevent representation by a finite positive penalty.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An active residual-constrained optimum with a positive qualified multiplier is penalized-optimal at the reciprocal parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\lambda>0:\ \bar x\in\operatorname*{argmin}_x\{r(x)+\lambda\|x\|_1\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Constrained-to-Penalized Multiplier Correspondence
Sparse-Recovery Tuning Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Parameter correspondences and limits among constrained and penalized sparse-recovery formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat x_\lambda\) minimize \(\frac12\|Ax-y\|_2^2+\lambda\|x\|_1\) with \(\lambda>0\). Then \(\widehat x_\lambda\) also minimizes \(\|x\|_1\) subject to \(\frac12\|Ax-y\|_2^2\le\tau\), where \(\tau=\frac12\|A\widehat x_\lambda-y\|_2^2\). Moreover, its optimality condition gives \(\|A^{\mathsf T}(y-A\widehat x_\lambda)\|_\infty\le\lambda\), so it is feasible for the Dantzig constraint at the same tolerance. These facts do not generally imply that it minimizes the Dantzig-selector objective; equality of solution sets requires additional assumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A penalized solution determines an equivalent residual-constrained level and is Dantzig-feasible at the same penalty, but need not be Dantzig-optimal.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat x_\lambda\in\operatorname*{argmin}\{\|x\|_1:\frac12\|Ax-y\|_2^2\le\tau\}\) and \(\|A^{\mathsf T}(y-A\widehat x_\lambda)\|_\infty\le\lambda\).

notation.meaning: residual level induced by the penalized solution

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: convex level-set correspondence and lasso KKT implication

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The level-set correspondence and distinction between Dantzig feasibility and optimality are mathematically sound, but the precise boundary claim requires a cited source.

children.title: Sparse-Recovery Condition Families
children.top_down_role: Named guarantee families are indexed without carrying their statements or proofs.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative kernel and off-kernel variants of the null-space property.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A matrix \(A\) has the stable null-space property of order \(s\) with \(0\le\rho<1\) if \[\|h_S\|_1\le\rho\|h_{S^c}\|_1\] for every \(h\in\ker A\) and \(|S|\le s\). It has the l2-robust null-space property with constants \(0\le\rho<1\) and \(\tau\ge0\) if \[\|v_S\|_2\le\frac{\rho}{\sqrt{s}}\|v_{S^c}\|_1+\tau\|Av\|_2\] for every \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) and \(|S|\le s\). The robust property implies the stable property on restriction to \(\ker A\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stable NSP controls kernel vectors quantitatively; robust NSP extends the control off the kernel through a residual term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The l2-robust NSP implies the stable NSP of the same order and imbalance constant.
knowledge_statements.title: Stable and Robust Null-Space Properties

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Finite-Dimensional Equivalence of Strict and Stable NSP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform-margin form of the strict null-space property for a fixed matrix and order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed finite-dimensional matrix \(A\) and fixed order \(s\), \[\|h_S\|_1<\|h_{S^c}\|_1\quad(0\ne h\in\ker A,\ |S|\le s)\] holds if and only if there exists \(\rho<1\) such that \[\|h_S\|_1\le\rho\|h_{S^c}\|_1\quad(h\in\ker A,\ |S|\le s).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a fixed finite-dimensional sensing matrix, strict NSP is equivalent to NSP with a uniform margin below one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strict NSP of order \(s\) is equivalent to stable NSP for some \(\rho<1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Dimensional Equivalence of Strict and Stable NSP
Null-Space Property Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact order-s null-space characterization of uniform noiseless basis-pursuit recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(s\in\{1,\ldots,n\}\). The matrix \(A\) has the strict null-space property of order \(s\) when, for every \(0\ne h\in\ker A\) and every \(S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}\) with \(|S|\le s\), \[\|h_S\|_1<\|h_{S^c}\|_1.\] This property holds if and only if every vector \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(\|x_0\|_0\le s\) is the unique solution of \[\min_{x\in\mathbb R^n}\|x\|_1\quad\text{subject to}\quad Ax=Ax_0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strict null-space imbalance on every support of size at most s is equivalent to uniform, unique ℓ1 recovery of all s-sparse vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\) has the strict null-space property of order \(s\) if and only if basis pursuit uniquely recovers every \(s\)-sparse vector.

notation.meaning: restriction of h to coordinates in S, zero elsewhere
complement of the index set S
number of nonzero coordinates of x

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Sparse Injectivity Does Not Ensure l1 Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between identifiability and uniform basis-pursuit recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The condition \(\delta_{2s}(A)<1\) guarantees uniqueness among \(s\)-sparse representations, but it does not by itself imply the null-space property of order \(s\). Consequently, it does not by itself guarantee uniform basis-pursuit recovery; a stronger quantitative RIP restriction is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Order-2s RIP below one guarantees sparse uniqueness, not automatically uniform l1 recovery.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sparse injectivity follows, but uniform basis-pursuit recovery does not follow from this condition alone.
knowledge_statements.title: Sparse Injectivity Does Not Ensure l1 Recovery

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Monotonicity and Sparse Injectivity of RIP Constants
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Order structure and identifiability consequence of restricted isometry.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(1\le s\le t\le n\), then \(\delta_s(A)\le\delta_t(A)\). Moreover, \(\delta_{2s}(A)<1\) implies that \(A\) is injective on differences of \(s\)-sparse vectors: if \(Ax=Az\) and \(\|x\|_0,\|z\|_0\le s\), then \(x=z\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: RIP constants are monotone in their order, and order-2s RIP below one guarantees sparse identifiability.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_s(A)\le\delta_t(A)\), and \(\delta_{2s}(A)<1\) implies injectivity on s-sparse vectors.

notation.meaning: restricted isometry constant of order s

knowledge_statements.title: Monotonicity and Sparse Injectivity of RIP Constants

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Locally owned implication from a restricted-isometry threshold to the null-space condition mediating recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\delta_{2s}(A)<\sqrt2-1\), then \(A\) satisfies the l2-robust null-space property of order \(s\) for constants \(0\le\rho<1\) and \(\tau>0\) depending only on \(\delta_{2s}(A)\). The displayed threshold is a classical sufficient condition and is not asserted to be sharp.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A classical small order-2s RIP bound implies the robust null-space property needed for stable and noisy recovery.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\) has the l2-robust null-space property of order \(s\) with constants depending only on \(\delta_{2s}(A)\).
knowledge_statements.title: Classical RIP-to-Robust-NSP Implication
Restricted-Isometry Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Near-isometry condition on all sparse vectors of a prescribed order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and an integer \(s\ge1\), the restricted isometry constant \(\delta_s(A)\) is the smallest \(\delta\ge0\) such that \[(1-\delta)\|x\|_2^2\le\|Ax\|_2^2\le(1+\delta)\|x\|_2^2\] for every \(x\in\mathbb R^n\) with \(\|x\|_0\le s\). The matrix has the restricted isometry property of order \(s\) when \(\delta_s(A)<1\). Equivalently, every submatrix formed from at most \(s\) columns has all squared singular values in \([1-\delta_s(A),1+\delta_s(A)]\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: RIP requires the sensing matrix to approximately preserve the Euclidean norm of every s-sparse vector, equivalently controlling singular values of all small column submatrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\) has RIP of order \(s\) precisely when \(\delta_s(A)<1\).

notation.meaning: restricted isometry constant of order s
number of nonzero coordinates of x

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition correctly defines the restricted isometry family and its submatrix interpretation, but no authoritative compressed-sensing source is cited.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: RIP-Based Stable and Robust Basis-Pursuit Recovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rejected locally because the full noisy recovery guarantee belongs to recovery-regime leaves rather than this condition-family leaf.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(\delta_{2s}(A)<\sqrt2-1\), \(y=Ax+e\), \(\|e\|_2\le\varepsilon\), and \(\widehat x\) minimizes \(\|z\|_1\) subject to \(\|Az-y\|_2\le\varepsilon\), then \(\|\widehat x-x\|_2\le C\sigma_s(x)_1/\sqrt{s}+D\varepsilon\) for constants depending only on \(\delta_{2s}(A)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A small RIP constant yields stable and noise-robust basis-pursuit-denoising recovery.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|\widehat x-x\|_2\le C\sigma_s(x)_1/\sqrt{s}+D\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.title: RIP-Based Stable and Robust Basis-Pursuit Recovery

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory contains the RIP definition and spectral equivalence, monotonicity, sparse injectivity, the identifiability-versus-l1 boundary, and a classical RIP-to-robust-NSP implication. The proposed full noisy recovery theorem was deferred as recovery-regime material; coherence calculations and probabilistic constructions were also excluded.

children.title: Mutual-Coherence Conditions
children.top_down_role: Recovery regimes organized by pairwise measurement-column interactions.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Coherence Control of Sparse Gram Matrices
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sparse-submatrix spectral consequence of pairwise column coherence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) have unit-norm columns and mutual coherence \(\mu(A)\). For every \(S\) with \(|S|=k\), \[\operatorname{spec}(A_S^{\mathsf T}A_S)\subseteq[1-(k-1)\mu(A),1+(k-1)\mu(A)].\] Consequently, \(\delta_k(A)\le(k-1)\mu(A)\), and \(A_S\) is injective whenever \((k-1)\mu(A)<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise coherence controls every sparse Gram spectrum and upper-bounds the corresponding restricted isometry constant.
assumptions_latex: Every column of \(A\) has Euclidean norm one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\delta_k(A)\le(k-1)\mu(A)\), with injectivity when \((k-1)\mu(A)<1\).

notation.meaning: submatrix containing columns indexed by S
restricted isometry constant of order k

knowledge_statements.title: Coherence Control of Sparse Gram Matrices
Mutual-Coherence Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Computable coherence-based sufficient condition for uniform exact sparse recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=[a_1\ \cdots\ a_n]\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have unit-norm columns and mutual coherence \[\mu(A)=\max_{i\ne j}|a_i^{\mathsf T}a_j|.\] If \(0<\mu(A)\le1\) and an integer \(s\) satisfies \[s<\frac12\left(1+\frac1{\mu(A)}\right),\] then every \(s\)-sparse vector \(x_0\) is the unique sparsest representation of \(Ax_0\) and is also the unique minimizer of basis pursuit subject to \(Ax=Ax_0\). The condition is sufficient rather than necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If sparsity is below half of one plus inverse mutual coherence, every such sparse signal is uniquely recovered by basis pursuit.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every \(x_0\) with \(\|x_0\|_0\le s\) is uniquely recovered from \(Ax_0\) by basis pursuit.

notation.meaning: largest absolute inner product between distinct normalized columns

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coherence bound is a theorem-level sufficient condition suitably placed under this conditions leaf, but its recovery conclusion needs an authoritative theorem citation.

children.title: Spark-Based Conditions
children.top_down_role: Recovery regimes organized by minimal linear-dependence structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Elementary structural bounds for an underdetermined matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) with \(m<n\). Then \[1\le\operatorname{spark}(A)\le\operatorname{rank}(A)+1\le m+1,\] where spark equals one exactly when a zero column is present. If there is no zero column, then \(2\le\operatorname{spark}(A)\le m+1\). Moreover, \(A\) is full spark exactly when every set of at most \(m\) columns is linearly independent, equivalently \(\operatorname{spark}(A)=m+1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an underdetermined matrix, spark is at most rank plus one; full spark means every set of at most m columns is independent.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{spark}(A)\le\operatorname{rank}(A)+1\le m+1\), with full spark equivalent to \(\operatorname{spark}(A)=m+1\).

notation.meaning: smallest cardinality of a linearly dependent column set

knowledge_statements.title: Spark Range and Full-Spark Matrices
Spark-Based Conditions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp null-vector support condition for uniqueness of sparse linear representations in the underdetermined regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) with \(m<n\), and define \[\operatorname{spark}(A)=\min\{\|h\|_0:0\ne h\in\ker A\}.\] For an integer \(s\) with \(1\le s\le n\), every vector \(x_0\in\mathbb R^n\) satisfying \(\|x_0\|_0\le s\) is the unique sparsest solution of \(Ax=Ax_0\) if and only if \(\operatorname{spark}(A)>2s\). This criterion characterizes uniqueness for cardinality minimization; by itself it does not guarantee that basis pursuit selects the unique sparsest solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an underdetermined matrix, all s-sparse representations are unique exactly when every nonzero null vector uses more than 2s coordinates. This condition alone does not guarantee ℓ1 recovery.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform uniqueness of all \(s\)-sparse representations holds if and only if \(\operatorname{spark}(A)>2s\).

notation.meaning: smallest support size of a nonzero null vector

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: classical spark uniqueness characterization in the underdetermined regime

children.title: Condition-Strength Comparison
children.top_down_role: Relative informativeness, accessibility, and conservatism of the two condition families.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Computational Accessibility of Coherence and Spark
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Evaluation-cost comparison for the two deterministic condition families.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For normalized columns, mutual coherence is obtained from the off-diagonal entries of \(A^{\mathsf T}A\), requiring \(O(mn^2)\) arithmetic by direct Gram-matrix formation. An exhaustive exact-spark procedure tests column subsets in increasing cardinality; through size \(q\) it performs \(\sum_{k=1}^{q}\binom nk\) rank tests, each polynomial in \(m\) and \(k\). Thus coherence is directly computable, whereas this general exact-spark procedure has combinatorial worst-case growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Coherence is computed from the Gram matrix, while exhaustive exact spark determination requires combinatorially many subset rank tests.
assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) has normalized columns for coherence evaluation.
Arithmetic-operation counts use direct Gram formation and standard polynomial-time rank tests.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Direct coherence evaluation costs \(O(mn^2)\), while exhaustive spark evaluation uses combinatorially many subset tests in the worst case.
knowledge_statements.title: Computational Accessibility of Coherence and Spark

assumptions_latex: \(A\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) has unit-norm columns and mutual coherence \(\mu(A)>0\).
The target sparsity is an integer \(s\geq 1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coherence condition implies the spark-based uniqueness condition.

notation.meaning: Smallest number of linearly dependent columns of A.
Largest absolute inner product between distinct columns of A.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compares uniform coherence and spark sufficient conditions for noiseless sparse identifiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The standard inequality \(\operatorname{spark}(A)\geq 1+\mu(A)^{-1}\) yields
\[
s<\frac{1}{2}\left(1+\frac{1}{\mu(A)}\right)\quad\Longrightarrow\quad 2s<\operatorname{spark}(A).
\]
Consequently, the coherence condition guarantees that every vector having at most \(s\) nonzero entries is the unique sparsest solution of \(Az=Ax\). The converse implication need not hold: the actual spark can exceed its coherence lower bound, so \(2s<\operatorname{spark}(A)\) is generally the weaker, sharper uniqueness condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The mutual-coherence bound is a computable but generally stronger sufficient condition than the corresponding spark-based sparse-uniqueness condition.
knowledge_statements.title: Condition-Strength Comparison

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The coherence-to-spark comparison is mathematically standard and fits the property container, but no inspectable authoritative citation is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual program and exact optimality certificate for noiseless basis pursuit.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The dual of \[\min_z\ \|z\|_1\quad\text{subject to }Az=b\] is \[\max_y\ b^{\mathsf T}y\quad\text{subject to }\|A^{\mathsf T}y\|_\infty\le1.\] A primal-feasible \(x\) is optimal if and only if some \(y\) satisfies \(A^{\mathsf T}y\in\partial\|x\|_1\), equivalently \((A^{\mathsf T}y)_S=\operatorname{sign}(x_S)\) and \(\|(A^{\mathsf T}y)_{S^c}\|_\infty\le1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible vector solves basis pursuit exactly when a dual feasible vector matches an l1 subgradient at that vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x\text{ is optimal}\Longleftrightarrow\exists y:\ A^{\mathsf T}y\in\partial\|x\|_1\).

notation.meaning: Subdifferential of the l1 norm at x.
Dual multiplier for the measurement equality.

assumptions_latex: The submatrix \(A_S\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A strict dual certificate proves that \(x\) uniquely solves basis pursuit with data \(Ax\).

Restriction of a vector to coordinates outside S.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact noiseless basis-pursuit certificate for a fixed support and sign pattern.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A vector \(y\in\mathbb{R}^m\) is a strict sparse dual certificate for \(x\) when
\[
A_S^{\mathsf T}y=\operatorname{sign}(x_S),\qquad \left\|A_{S^c}^{\mathsf T}y\right\|_\infty<1.
\]
Together with full column rank of \(A_S\), these verifiable relations certify that \(x\) is the unique solution of
\[
\min_{z\in\mathbb{R}^n}\|z\|_1\quad\text{subject to}\quad Az=Ax.
\]

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates inevitable ambient-space ambiguity from sparsity-restricted identifiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Because \(m<n\), rank-nullity gives \(\ker A\neq\{0\}\), so \(A\) cannot identify arbitrary vectors in \(\mathbb{R}^n\). Nevertheless, injectivity on \(\Sigma_s\) is possible. Its sharp boundary is
\[
A\text{ is injective on }\Sigma_s
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\ker A\cap\Sigma_{2s}=\{0\}.
\]
Hence undersampling alone does not preclude sparse recovery; failure begins when a nonzero null vector has at most \(2s\) nonzero coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fewer measurements than ambient coordinates cause global ambiguity, but sparse recovery remains identifiable exactly when no nonzero 2s-sparse vector lies in the kernel.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:

\[
(\Sigma_s-\Sigma_s)\cap\ker A\neq\{0\}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\ker A\cap\Sigma_{2s}\neq\{0\}
\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
\operatorname{spark}(A)\leq2s.
\]

children.title: Measurement-Ambiguity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Structural transition between recoverable and ambiguous signal classes.

knowledge_statements.title: Measurement-Ambiguity Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact noiseless injectivity threshold for sparse signals, independent of the reconstruction algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(\Sigma_s=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^n:\|x\|_0\leq s\}\). The measurement map is injective on \(\Sigma_s\) exactly when
\[
\forall x,z\in\Sigma_s,\quad Ax=Az\Longrightarrow x=z.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\ker(A)\cap\Sigma_{2s}=\{0\},
\qquad\text{or}\qquad
\operatorname{spark}(A)>2s.
\]
Thus \(\operatorname{spark}(A)>2s\) is the identifiable regime, whereas \(\operatorname{spark}(A)\leq 2s\) permits distinct \(s\)-sparse signals with identical measurements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sparse measurements are unambiguous exactly when the spark exceeds twice the sparsity; at or below that threshold, distinct sparse signals can share the same measurements.
assumptions_latex: \(\operatorname{spark}(A)\) denotes the minimum support size of a nonzero vector in \(\ker(A)\), with value \(+\infty\) when \(\ker(A)=\{0\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\) is injective on \(\Sigma_s\) if and only if \(\operatorname{spark}(A)>2s\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete one-sparse family exhibiting divergent noise amplification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The signals \(x_0=0\) and \(x_1=t e_1\) satisfy
\[
\|x_1-x_0\|_2=|t|,
\qquad
\|A_\alpha x_1-A_\alpha x_0\|_2=\alpha|t|.
\]
Therefore any inverse that distinguishes these signals has local Lipschitz constant at least \(1/\alpha\). Although every \(A_\alpha\) is injective, arbitrarily small measurement perturbations can represent fixed signal perturbations as \(\alpha\downarrow0\). knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient deterministic distinguishability condition under bounded corruption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal Y_x=Ax+\varepsilon B_2^m\). Uniform exact deterministic recovery on \(K\) is possible exactly when these sets are pairwise disjoint, equivalently \[\|A(x_1-x_0)\|_2>2\varepsilon\quad\text{for all distinct }x_0,x_1\in K.\] At equality or below the immutable midpoint attack gives ambiguity; under strict separation each admissible observation has a unique compatible signal.

Adversarial Measurement Corruption
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic adversarial-corruption boundary for an arbitrary structured signal class.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let distinct \(x_0,x_1\in K\) satisfy \(\|A(x_1-x_0)\|_2\leq2\varepsilon\), and define
\[
e_0=\frac{A(x_1-x_0)}{2},
\qquad
e_1=-\frac{A(x_1-x_0)}{2}.
\]
Then \(\|e_0\|_2\leq\varepsilon\), \(\|e_1\|_2\leq\varepsilon\), and
\[
Ax_0+e_0=Ax_1+e_1.
\]
Thus admissible corruptions can make the two signals observationally indistinguishable, so no deterministic decoder can guarantee exact recovery of every signal in \(K\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When two admissible signals have measurements within twice the corruption radius, bounded adversarial corruptions can make their observations identical and prevent uniform exact recovery.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Any distinct \(x_0,x_1\in K\) satisfying \(\|A(x_1-x_0)\|_2\leq2\varepsilon\) can be made observationally indistinguishable by admissible corruptions.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If for some \(y\), \[F_y=\{x\in K:\|Ax-y\|_2\le\varepsilon\}\] is unbounded, then every decoder \(\Delta\) satisfies \[\sup_{x\in K,\|e\|_2\le\varepsilon}\|\Delta(Ax+e)-x\|_2=+\infty.\] This occurs, in particular, when \(K\) contains an unbounded affine ray in a null direction of \(A\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F_y=\{x\in K:\|Ax-y\|_2\le\varepsilon\}\), let \(\operatorname{rad}(F_y)=\inf_c\sup_{x\in F_y}\|c-x\|_2\). Then, allowing \(+\infty\), \[\inf_\Delta\sup_{x\in K,\|e\|_2\le\varepsilon}\|\Delta(Ax+e)-x\|_2=\sup_{y:F_y\ne\varnothing}\operatorname{rad}(F_y).\] Exact or arbitrarily accurate fiber centers attain or approximate the minimax value. The immutable two-point bound follows from \(\operatorname{rad}(F_y)\ge\tfrac12\operatorname{diam}(F_y)\).

Worst-Case Recovery Breakdown
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithm-independent worst-case lower bound induced by a two-signal ambiguity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exist corruptions \(e_0,e_1\in\mathbb{R}^m\) with \(\|e_i\|_2\leq\varepsilon\) that produce a common observation \(y=Ax_0+e_0=Ax_1+e_1\). For every decoder \(\Delta:\mathbb{R}^m\to\mathbb{R}^n\),
\[
\max_{i\in\{0,1\}}\|\Delta(y)-x_i\|_2
\geq\frac{1}{2}\|x_1-x_0\|_2.
\]
Consequently,
\[
\sup_{x\in K,\,\|e\|_2\leq\varepsilon}
\|\Delta(Ax+e)-x\|_2
\geq\frac{1}{2}\|x_1-x_0\|_2.
\]
This lower bound applies to every reconstruction algorithm.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any pair that bounded corruption can make indistinguishable forces every decoder to incur at least half the pair's separation as worst-case reconstruction error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{x\in K,\,\|e\|_2\leq\varepsilon}\|\Delta(Ax+e)-x\|_2\geq\frac12\|x_1-x_0\|_2\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact coefficient-domain representation under an assumed orthogonal sparsifying basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For orthogonal \(\Phi\), the substitution \(z=\Phi\alpha\) gives \[\operatorname*{argmin}_{Az=y}\|\Phi^{\mathsf T}z\|_1=\Phi\operatorname*{argmin}_{(A\Phi)\alpha=y}\|\alpha\|_1.\] Thus sparse-recovery conditions apply to \(A\Phi\) and the assumed coefficients \(\Phi^{\mathsf T}x\), not to coefficients in a different basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An orthogonal-basis analysis problem is ordinary basis pursuit for the transformed sensing matrix, so guarantees require sparsity in the assumed basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{Az=y}\|\Phi^{\mathsf T}z\|_1=\Phi\operatorname*{argmin}_{(A\Phi)\alpha=y}\|\alpha\|_1\).
knowledge_statements.title: Coefficient-Domain Reduction of Basis Mismatch
Sparsity-Model Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete failure caused solely by using the wrong sparsifying basis.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x=e_1\in\mathbb R^2\), let \(A=(1,0)\), and observe \(y=Ax=1\). In the correct canonical basis, \(x\) is one-sparse and is the unique vector supported on \(\{1\}\) satisfying the observation. Instead use the orthogonal basis \(\Phi=2^{-1/2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix}\) and solve \[\min_{z\in\mathbb R^2}\|\Phi^{\mathsf T}z\|_1\quad\text{subject to}\quad Az=y.\] Every \(z=(1,t)\) with \(|t|\le 1\) is optimal, because \(\|\Phi^{\mathsf T}z\|_1=\sqrt2\). Thus the mismatched basis-pursuit model does not uniquely recover \(x\), although the stated observation identifies it within the correct support model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A signal identifiable under its correct sparse support can become nonidentifiable when basis pursuit uses a mismatched sparsifying basis.
assumptions_latex: \(\Phi\) is the displayed rotated orthogonal basis.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_{Az=Ax}\|\Phi^{\mathsf T}z\|_1=\{(1,t):|t|\le1\}\), so exact recovery is not guaranteed.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient uniqueness test for a fixed noiseless completion instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) be feasible for nuclear-norm completion with \(\mathcal A=P_\Omega\). Then \(M\) is the unique optimizer if and only if \[\|M+H\|_*>\|M\|_*\quad\text{for every }0\ne H\in\ker\mathcal A.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unique recovery holds exactly when every nonzero feasible perturbation strictly increases nuclear norm.
assumptions_latex: The objective is the nuclear norm
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is uniquely optimal}\iff \forall H\in\ker P_\Omega\setminus\{0\},\ \|M+H\|_*>\|M\|_*.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Tangent-Space Dual Certificate for Exact Completion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sufficient uniqueness certificate for a fixed rank-r matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\) and \(T=\{UZ^{\mathsf T}+WV^{\mathsf T}\}\). If \(P_\Omega\) is injective on \(T\) and there exists \(Y=P_\Omega Y\) with \(P_TY=UV^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\|P_{T^\perp}Y\|_2<1\), then \(M\) is the unique minimizer of noiseless nuclear-norm completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tangent-space injectivity and a strict observed-support dual certificate guarantee unique exact completion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: M\text{ is the unique solution of }\min_X\|X\|_*\text{ subject to }P_\Omega X=P_\Omega M.
knowledge_statements.title: Tangent-Space Dual Certificate for Exact Completion
Exact Matrix-Completion Application
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Noiseless nuclear-norm completion from a prescribed set of entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For observations \(b_{ij}=M_{ij}\) on an index set \(\Omega\subseteq[m]\times[n]\), exact convex matrix completion is represented by \[\widehat M\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}}\|X\|_*\quad\text{subject to}\quad P_\Omega X=P_\Omega M.\] Here \(P_\Omega\) retains entries in \(\Omega\) and sets all other entries to zero, while \(\|X\|_*\) is the sum of the singular values of \(X\). Exact completion occurs precisely when the optimizer is unique and equals \(M\); otherwise the program supplies a minimum-nuclear-norm completion consistent with the observed entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact matrix completion minimizes nuclear norm among matrices agreeing with every noiseless observed entry; recovery is exact when the true matrix is the unique minimizer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat M=M\) whenever \(M\) is the unique feasible matrix of minimum nuclear norm.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nuclear-norm-regularized least squares on observed entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\lambda>0\), define \[\widehat M_\lambda\in\operatorname*{argmin}_X\frac12\|P_\Omega(X-Y)\|_F^2+\lambda\|X\|_*.\] A matrix \(\widehat M_\lambda\) is optimal if and only if \[0\in P_\Omega(\widehat M_\lambda-Y)+\lambda\partial\|\widehat M_\lambda\|_*.\] This is a penalized counterpart of residual-constrained completion; no one-to-one correspondence between their tuning parameters is asserted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The penalized noisy estimator balances observed least-squares error against nuclear norm and has a subgradient optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\in P_\Omega(\widehat M_\lambda-Y)+\lambda\partial\|\widehat M_\lambda\|_*.
knowledge_statements.title: Penalized Noisy Completion Variant

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Error bound under a lower bound on nuclear-norm descent directions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\widehat M\) solve the residual-constrained program with \(Y=P_\Omega M+E\) and \(\|P_\Omega E\|_F\le\delta\). Let \(\mathcal D(M)=\{H:\|M+H\|_*\le\|M\|_*\}\). If \(\|P_\Omega H\|_F\ge\alpha\|H\|_F\) for every \(H\in\mathcal D(M)\) and some \(\alpha>0\), then \[\|\widehat M-M\|_F\le 2\delta/\alpha.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform lower bound for the observation operator on all nuclear-norm descent perturbations gives a deterministic noise-stability bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|\widehat M-M\|_F\le2\delta/\alpha.

notation.meaning: nuclear-norm descent perturbation set at M

Noisy Matrix-Completion Application
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Constrained nuclear-norm completion under bounded observation noise.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y=P_\Omega M+E\), where the observation noise satisfies \(\|P_\Omega E\|_F\le\delta\). A noisy matrix-completion estimate is any solution of \[\widehat M\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}}\|X\|_*\quad\text{subject to}\quad \|P_\Omega(X-Y)\|_F\le\delta.\] The feasible set contains \(M\), and the estimate has no larger nuclear norm than \(M\). This formulation specifies the estimator but does not by itself imply a reconstruction-error bound; stability additionally requires structural assumptions on \(M\) and the sampling operator.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Noisy completion minimizes nuclear norm while fitting observed entries within a Frobenius-noise tolerance; stability requires additional sampling and low-rank assumptions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) is feasible and every optimizer satisfies \(\|\widehat M\|_*\le\|M\|_*\).

children.title: Weighted Matrix Completion
children.top_down_role: Matrix-completion templates using entry-specific or region-specific weights.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between weighted fidelity and control of every listed observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(w_{i_0j_0}=0\), then \(\|W_\Omega(X+tE_{i_0j_0}-Y)\|_F=\|W_\Omega(X-Y)\|_F\) for every \(t\in\mathbb R\). Thus the weighted fidelity term contains no information about entry \((i_0,j_0)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero-weight observation is ignored by the fidelity term and cannot be controlled through that term.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E_{i_0j_0}\in\ker W_\Omega.
knowledge_statements.title: Zero-Weight Information Loss

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Penalized counterpart of weighted residual-budget completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(w_{ij}\ge0\) and \(\lambda>0\), \[\widehat M\in\operatorname*{argmin}_X\left\{\frac12\sum_{(i,j)\in\Omega}w_{ij}(X_{ij}-Y_{ij})^2+\lambda\|X\|_*\right\}\] is a convex estimator. A constrained optimizer with an active residual constraint and positive optimal multiplier \(\eta\) also solves the penalized problem with \(\lambda=1/\eta\). Conversely, a penalized optimizer solves the constrained problem whose radius equals its achieved weighted residual.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted completion has a convex penalized form; constrained and penalized optimizers correspond when their residual radius and positive multiplier are matched.
assumptions_latex: The constrained-to-penalized implication assumes a positive optimal multiplier and an active constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat M\text{ solves a convex weighted nuclear-norm problem}.

notation.meaning: multiplier of the constrained residual inequality

knowledge_statements.title: Penalized Weighted Completion
Weighted Matrix Completion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex completion with entrywise weighted data fidelity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given observed values \(Y_{ij}\), positive weights \(w_{ij}>0\) for \((i,j)\in\Omega\), and a tolerance \(\delta\ge0\), weighted matrix completion is the convex program \[\widehat M\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}}\|X\|_*\quad\text{subject to}\quad \sum_{(i,j)\in\Omega}w_{ij}(X_{ij}-Y_{ij})^2\le\delta^2.\] Equivalently, with \((W_\Omega Z)_{ij}=\sqrt{w_{ij}}Z_{ij}\) on \(\Omega\) and zero elsewhere, the constraint is \(\|W_\Omega(X-Y)\|_F\le\delta\). Positive weights preserve convexity and permit heterogeneous noise or sampling scales.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted completion minimizes nuclear norm subject to a convex, entry-weighted residual bound, allowing observed entries to have different reliability or sampling scales.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed optimization problem is convex in \(X\).

children.title: Nonuniform Observation Sampling

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Entrywise Variance of the Unbiased Sampling Operator
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact mean-square identity for heterogeneous Bernoulli inverse-probability sampling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under Bernoulli sampling with \(0<p_{ij}\le1\), \[\mathbb E\|\mathcal R_\Omega(X)-X\|_F^2=\sum_{i,j}\frac{1-p_{ij}}{p_{ij}}X_{ij}^2.\] Thus unbiasedness does not provide uniform concentration when relevant inclusion probabilities approach zero.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The unbiased sampling operator has exact mean-square error \(\sum (1-p_{ij})X_{ij}^2/p_{ij}\), exposing instability at small probabilities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathbb E\|\mathcal R_\Omega(X)-X\|_F^2=\sum_{i,j}(p_{ij}^{-1}-1)X_{ij}^2.
knowledge_statements.title: Entrywise Variance of the Unbiased Sampling Operator
Nonuniform Observation Sampling
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Independent entry sampling with heterogeneous inclusion probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A nonuniform Bernoulli observation model is specified by probabilities \(p_{ij}\in(0,1]\) and independent indicators \(\delta_{ij}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_{ij})\), with \(\Omega=\{(i,j):\delta_{ij}=1\}\). The inverse-probability sampling operator is \[\mathcal R_\Omega(X)=\sum_{i=1}^m\sum_{j=1}^n\frac{\delta_{ij}}{p_{ij}}X_{ij}e_ie_j^{\mathsf T}.\] For every fixed \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), it is unbiased: \(\mathbb E[\mathcal R_\Omega(X)]=X\). Uniform Bernoulli sampling is the special case \(p_{ij}=p\) for all entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Nonuniform Bernoulli sampling observes each entry independently with its own probability; inverse-probability scaling yields an unbiased matrix observation operator.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathbb E[\mathcal R_\Omega(X)]=X\) for every fixed \(X\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\).

children.title: Weight-Misspecification Boundary
children.top_down_role: Completion degradation caused by weights that poorly reflect the sampling pattern.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Stochastic amplification caused by using assumed probabilities in inverse weighting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\delta_{ij}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_{ij})\) and \(Z_{ij}=\delta_{ij}X_{ij}/q_{ij}\), \[\operatorname{Var}(Z_{ij})=\frac{p_{ij}(1-p_{ij})}{q_{ij}^2}X_{ij}^2.\] Consequently, even when mean distortion \(p_{ij}/q_{ij}\) is considered separately, assumed weights \(q_{ij}\) approaching zero can cause unbounded stochastic amplification. Stable correction therefore requires quantitative control of both calibration ratios and weight magnitudes on relevant entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Incorrect probabilities affect both mean calibration and variance; very small assumed probabilities can amplify noise without bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{Var}(\delta_{ij}X_{ij}/q_{ij})=p_{ij}(1-p_{ij})X_{ij}^2/q_{ij}^2.
knowledge_statements.title: Variance Under Misspecified Inverse-Probability Weights

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Expectation distortion when assumed and true probabilities are uniformly comparable.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D(X)=\mathbb E[\widetilde{\mathcal R}_\Omega(X)]\), so \(D(X)_{ij}=(p_{ij}/q_{ij})X_{ij}\). If \(0<\ell\le p_{ij}/q_{ij}\le u<\infty\), then \[\ell^2\|X\|_F^2\le\|D(X)\|_F^2\le u^2\|X\|_F^2,\qquad \|D(X)-X\|_F\le\max\{|u-1|,|\ell-1|\}\|X\|_F.\] Without either ratio bound, deterministic calibration can be arbitrarily distorted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-sided comparability of true and assumed probabilities bounds mean calibration distortion.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded Multiplicative Misspecification Distortion
Weight-Misspecification Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of distribution-correcting guarantees under inaccurate inverse-probability weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Under nonuniform Bernoulli sampling, let an estimator use positive scaling values \(q_{ij}\) in place of the true probabilities \(p_{ij}\), defining \[\widetilde{\mathcal R}_\Omega(X)=\sum_{i,j}\frac{\delta_{ij}}{q_{ij}}X_{ij}e_ie_j^{\mathsf T}.\] Then \[\mathbb E[\widetilde{\mathcal R}_\Omega(X)]=\sum_{i,j}\frac{p_{ij}}{q_{ij}}X_{ij}e_ie_j^{\mathsf T}.\] Hence the weighted observation is unbiased for every \(X\) if and only if \(q_{ij}=p_{ij}\) for every entry. If some ratio \(p_{ij}/q_{ij}\) is arbitrarily large or small, no probability-independent conditioning or noise-amplification bound follows from this weighting alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Using incorrect inclusion probabilities biases inverse-probability observations entrywise; unbounded probability-to-weight ratios destroy uniform conditioning and noise-control guarantees.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Unbiasedness for all \(X\) holds exactly when \(q_{ij}=p_{ij}\) for all \((i,j)\).

notation.meaning: sampling probability assumed by the estimator

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximally coherent rank-one obstruction to entrywise recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M=e_ie_j^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), the minimal left and right coherence parameters under the standard rank-one normalization are \(m\) and \(n\). If \((i,j)\notin\Omega\), then \(P_\Omega M=P_\Omega0\), despite \(M\ne0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A one-entry matrix is rank one but maximally coherent and is invisible unless its nonzero entry is sampled.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: P_\Omega M=P_\Omega0\quad\text{with}\quad M\ne0.
knowledge_statements.title: Coordinate-Spike Coherence Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Equivalent projector-diagonal formulation and minimal parameter range.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(U\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\) with \(U^{\mathsf T}U=I_r\), define \(\ell_i=e_i^{\mathsf T}UU^{\mathsf T}e_i=\|U^{\mathsf T}e_i\|_2^2\). Then \(\sum_i\ell_i=r\), and \(\max_i\ell_i\le\mu r/m\) is the leverage-score form of subspace incoherence. The smallest admissible \(\mu\) lies in \([1,m/r]\). The same statements hold for \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Subspace incoherence bounds coordinate leverage scores; their sum determines the natural range of the minimal coherence parameter.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ell_i=(UU^{\mathsf T})_{ii},\qquad\sum_i\ell_i=r,\qquad1\le\mu_{\min}\le m/r.

notation.meaning: smallest coherence parameter satisfying the displayed bound

review_flags: corrected builder wording: the range applies to the minimal parameter, since any larger parameter also satisfies the inequality
knowledge_statements.title: Leverage-Score Form of Subspace Incoherence
Matrix Incoherence Condition Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard singular-subspace and entrywise incoherence conditions for rank-\(r\) matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) have rank \(r\), where \(U\in\mathbb R^{m\times r}\) and \(V\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\) have orthonormal columns. Subspace incoherence with parameter \(\mu_0\ge 1\) means \[\max_{1\le i\le m}\|U^{\mathsf T}e_i\|_2^2\le\frac{\mu_0r}{m},\qquad \max_{1\le j\le n}\|V^{\mathsf T}e_j\|_2^2\le\frac{\mu_0r}{n}.\] An additional entrywise incoherence condition, under a common normalization, is \[\|UV^{\mathsf T}\|_\infty\le\mu_1\sqrt{\frac{r}{mn}},\] where \(\|Z\|_\infty=\max_{i,j}|Z_{ij}|\). These conditions limit concentration of the singular subspaces, but neither specifies a sampling distribution or by itself guarantees recovery.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Matrix incoherence limits coordinate concentration of the left and right singular subspaces. A commonly imposed additional condition bounds the largest entry of their cross-product; these conditions alone do not guarantee recovery.
assumptions_latex: \(M=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) is a compact singular-value decomposition of rank \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed inequalities define subspace incoherence and an additional commonly used entrywise incoherence condition.

notation.meaning: entrywise incoherence parameter under the displayed normalization

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local deterministic sampling geometry at a fixed low-rank matrix.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\) have fixed-rank tangent space \(T\). Then \[\ker(P_\Omega)\cap T=\{0\}\] is equivalent to injectivity of \(P_\Omega|_T\), and in finite dimensions to the existence of \(c>0\) such that \(\|P_\Omega H\|_F\ge c\|H\|_F\) for every \(H\in T\). Failure leaves a nonzero first-order rank-compatible direction invisible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A pattern is first-order informative at a low-rank matrix exactly when coordinate sampling is injective on its tangent space.
assumptions_latex: \(T\) is the corresponding tangent space at \(M\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \ker(P_\Omega)\cap T=\{0\}\iff P_\Omega|_T\text{ is injective}.
knowledge_statements.title: Tangent-Space Injectivity Condition

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic obstruction to uniform rank-r identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If some row of \(\Omega\) has fewer than \(r\) observed entries, there exist distinct matrices \(M,M'\) of rank at most \(r\) with \(P_\Omega M=P_\Omega M'\). The analogous statement holds when a column has degree below \(r\). Hence minimum row and column degree at least \(r\) is necessary for uniform identification over all rank-at-most-\(r\) matrices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform rank-r identification requires every row and column of the sampling graph to have degree at least r.
assumptions_latex: Some row or column of \(\Omega\) has degree strictly below \(r\).
The model class contains all matrices of rank at most \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists M\ne M':\operatorname{rank}(M),\operatorname{rank}(M')\le r,\quad P_\Omega M=P_\Omega M'.

notation.meaning: sampling-graph degree of a row or column vertex

knowledge_statements.title: Insufficient Row or Column Degree
Matrix Sampling-Pattern Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic coverage requirements separating potentially identifiable from impossible patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\subseteq[m]\times[n]\) be a deterministic observation pattern. If a row \(i_0\) is unobserved, then exact completion is impossible even over rank-one matrices: choose nonzero \(v\in\mathbb R^n\) and vectors \(u,u'\in\mathbb R^m\) that agree except at \(i_0\). The distinct rank-one matrices \(uv^{\mathsf T}\) and \(u'v^{\mathsf T}\) agree on every entry in \(\Omega\). The analogous statement holds for an unobserved column. Therefore every row and column must be sampled for uniform identifiability over such a class, although this coverage condition is not sufficient by itself.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Any sampling pattern omitting an entire row or column cannot uniformly identify rank-one matrices; full row-and-column coverage is necessary but not sufficient.
assumptions_latex: \(\Omega\) omits every entry of some row or some column.
The admissible class contains arbitrary rank-one matrices.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist distinct rank-one matrices \(M\neq M'\) with \(P_\Omega M=P_\Omega M'\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Subdifferential identity underlying matrix-completion certificates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(M=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\), \[\partial\|M\|_*=\{UV^{\mathsf T}+W:P_TW=0,\ \|W\|_2\le1\}.\] Equivalently, \(G\in\partial\|M\|_*\) exactly when \(P_TG=UV^{\mathsf T}\) and \(\|P_{T^\perp}G\|_2\le1\).

Matrix Dual-Certificate Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tangent-space certificate for uniqueness in noiseless nuclear-norm completion.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\) and let \(T=\{UQ^{\mathsf T}+PV^{\mathsf T}:P\in\mathbb R^{m\times r},\ Q\in\mathbb R^{n\times r}\}\). Suppose \(P_\Omega\) is injective on \(T\). If there exists \(Y\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) satisfying \[P_\Omega Y=Y,\qquad P_TY=UV^{\mathsf T},\qquad \|P_{T^\perp}Y\|_2<1,\] then \(M\) is the unique minimizer of \(\min_X\|X\|_*\) subject to \(P_\Omega X=P_\Omega M\). The matrix \(Y\) is a verifiable strict dual certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sampled matrix matching the nuclear-norm subgradient on the tangent space and having strict spectral norm below one off it certifies unique completion.
assumptions_latex: \(P_\Omega\) is injective on the tangent space \(T\).
A matrix \(Y\) satisfies the displayed support and projection conditions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) is the unique solution of \(\min\{\|X\|_*:P_\Omega X=P_\Omega M\}\).

notation.meaning: tangent space of the rank-r matrix variety at M

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coupon-collector obstruction preceding matrix-specific recovery guarantees.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an \(n\times n\) matrix, sample \(s\) entries independently and uniformly with replacement. If \(s\le(1-\varepsilon)n\log n\) for fixed \(\varepsilon\in(0,1)\), then the probability that every row is observed tends to zero as \(n\to\infty\); consequently the probability that every row and column is observed also tends to zero. Because an omitted row or column prevents uniform rank-one identifiability, uniform recovery requires an \(n\log n\)-scale coverage regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform random sampling needs order n log n observations merely to cover all rows and columns, independently of rank degrees of freedom.
assumptions_latex: Entries are sampled independently and uniformly with replacement from \([n]\times[n]\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s\le(1-\varepsilon)n\log n\implies\Pr(\text{all rows and columns are covered})\to0.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic observation-count lower bound for rank-r matrix identification.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The smooth manifold of real \(m\times n\) matrices of rank exactly \(r\) has dimension \(r(m+n-r)\). Consequently, a coordinate-observation map with fewer than \(r(m+n-r)\) scalar outputs cannot be locally one-to-one on a generic rank-\(r\) neighborhood. Generic exact matrix completion therefore requires at least \(r(m+n-r)\) observed entries, independently of the recovery algorithm.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stable Recovery Under a Robust Nuclear Nullspace Property
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Deterministic approximation-and-noise error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume that for every \(H\), \[\|H_r\|_*\le\rho\|H-H_r\|_*+\tau\|\mathcal AH\|_2,\qquad0\le\rho<1,\] where \(H_r\) is a best rank-\(r\) approximation. If \(\|b-\mathcal AM\|_2\le\delta\) and \(\widehat M\) minimizes nuclear norm subject to \(\|\mathcal AX-b\|_2\le\delta\), then \[\|\widehat M-M\|_*\le\frac{2(1+\rho)}{1-\rho}\|M-M_r\|_*+\frac{4\tau}{1-\rho}\delta.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust nuclear nullspace property gives stable recovery controlled by the target's rank-r approximation tail and measurement noise.
assumptions_latex: The displayed robust nuclear nullspace property holds with \(0\le\rho<1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \|\widehat M-M\|_*\le\frac{2(1+\rho)}{1-\rho}\|M-M_r\|_*+\frac{4\tau}{1-\rho}\delta.

If \(\delta_{2r}<1\), then \(\mathcal A\) is injective on the set of matrices of rank at most \(r\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=L_0+S_0\), \(L_0=U\Sigma V^{\mathsf T}\), \(T\) be the fixed-rank tangent space, and \(\Gamma=\operatorname{supp}(S_0)\). If \[P_TY=UV^{\mathsf T},\quad\|P_{T^\perp}Y\|_2\le1,\quad P_\Gamma Y=\lambda\operatorname{sgn}(S_0),\quad\|P_{\Gamma^c}Y\|_\infty\le\lambda,\] then \(Y\in\partial\|L_0\|_*\cap\lambda\partial\|S_0\|_1\), and \((L_0,S_0)\) is optimal for principal component pursuit. Strict off-space inequalities together with \(T\cap\Omega_\Gamma=\{0\}\) certify uniqueness.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact sparse-component update with the other component fixed in a quadratic low-rank-plus-sparse model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(R\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\) and \(\tau>0\), the problem \[\min_S\ \frac12\|R-S\|_F^2+\tau\|S\|_1\] has the unique solution \[S^*=\mathcal S_\tau(R),\qquad (\mathcal S_\tau(R))_{ij}=\operatorname{sign}(R_{ij})(|R_{ij}|-\tau)_+.\] Hence \(S^*_{ij}=0\) exactly when \(|R_{ij}|\le\tau\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(W\in\mathbb R^{d\times T}\) and any integer \(r\ge\operatorname{rank}(W)\), \[\|W\|_*=\min_{U\in\mathbb R^{d\times r},\,V\in\mathbb R^{T\times r}:\,UV^\top=W}\frac12\bigl(\|U\|_F^2+\|V\|_F^2\bigr).\] Thus the trace-norm multitask objective has an equivalent value formulation whose factors expose a shared task subspace, although joint optimization over \((U,V)\) is generally nonconvex.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex shared-low-rank estimator for linear multitask prediction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For tasks \(t=1,\ldots,T\), let \(X_t\in\mathbb{R}^{n_t\times d}\), \(y_t\in\mathbb{R}^{n_t}\), and collect task parameters as \(W=[w_1,\ldots,w_T]\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times T}\). Trace-norm multitask estimation solves \[\widehat W\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{W\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times T}}\ \sum_{t=1}^{T}\ell_t(X_tw_t,y_t)+\lambda\|W\|_*,\] where every \(\ell_t(\cdot,y_t)\) is convex and \(\lambda\ge0\). The nuclear-norm penalty is convex and favors a coefficient matrix with low effective rank, thereby coupling the tasks through a shared parameter subspace.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matrix-completion nonidentifiability caused by a maximally coherent singular vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M=e_1e_1^{\mathsf T}\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\), a rank-one matrix whose singular vectors are coordinate vectors. If the sampled index set \(\Gamma\subseteq [n]\times[n]\) does not contain \((1,1)\), then \(P_\Gamma(M)=P_\Gamma(0)=0\). Consequently, no estimator using only \(P_\Gamma(M)\) can distinguish \(M\) from the zero matrix. Under uniform sampling of \(s\) entries without replacement, the failure event has probability \(1-s/n^2\). Thus rank alone cannot ensure completion when singular factors may be maximally coherent with the coordinate basis.

children.top_down_role: Completion failures caused by systematic preference for particular entries or regions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative indistinguishability caused by a strictly positive but very small entry-sampling probability.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(N\) entries be sampled independently with replacement from \(\pi\), and let \(0<\pi_{i_0j_0}<1\). For \(M_0=0\) and \(M_1=a e_{i_0}e_{j_0}^{\mathsf T}\), \(a\ne0\), the observations coincide whenever \((i_0,j_0)\) is never sampled, an event of probability \((1-\pi_{i_0j_0})^N\). Consequently, every estimator has worst-case exact-recovery error over \(\{M_0,M_1\}\) at least \(\tfrac12(1-\pi_{i_0j_0})^N\).

Biased Sampling Failures
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure under a sampling distribution assigning zero mass to informative entries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let entries be sampled independently from a distribution \(\pi\) on \([m]\times[n]\), and suppose \(\pi_{i_0j_0}=0\). Consider the two rank-at-most-one matrices \(M_0=0\) and \(M_1=e_{i_0}e_{j_0}^{\mathsf T}\). Every sample has the same observed value under \(M_0\) and \(M_1\), with probability one, regardless of the sample size. Hence their induced observation distributions coincide, and no estimator can recover both matrices exactly. Sampling bias that excludes an entry therefore destroys uniform identifiability over even the rank-one class.

children.title: Nonuniform Coverage Failures
children.top_down_role: Completion failures caused by uneven observational coverage.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rank-one nonidentifiability despite every row and column having an observation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate \(\Gamma\subseteq[m]\times[n]\) with its bipartite observation graph. If the graph has at least two edge-containing connected components, choose \(M=uv^{\mathsf T}\) with all coordinates nonzero. For one component \(C\) and \(c\ne0,1\), multiply row factors in \(C\) by \(c\) and column factors in \(C\) by \(c^{-1}\), leaving other factors unchanged. The resulting rank-one matrix \(M'\ne M\) satisfies \(P_\Gamma M'=P_\Gamma M\). Thus row-and-column incidence alone is insufficient; graph connectivity is also necessary for uniform rank-one identifiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A disconnected observation graph permits componentwise factor rescaling, so observing every row and column does not ensure rank-one completion.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Gamma\subseteq[m]\times[n]\) be the observed indices. If some row \(i_0\) is unobserved, then for any nonzero \(v\in\mathbb{R}^{n}\), the rank-one matrices \(0\) and \(e_{i_0}v^{\mathsf T}\) agree on \(\Gamma\). Likewise, if column \(j_0\) is unobserved, then \(0\) and \(ue_{j_0}^{\mathsf T}\) agree for every nonzero \(u\in\mathbb{R}^{m}\). Therefore observation of at least one entry in every row and every column is necessary for uniform exact recovery over the rank-one matrix class, though it is not sufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Uniform rank-one completion is impossible if any row or column has no observations; complete row-and-column coverage is necessary but not sufficient.
assumptions_latex: Recovery is required uniformly over all matrices of rank at most one
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An unobserved row or column makes the sampling operator noninjective on rank-at-most-one matrices.

children.title: Sampling-Correction Limits
children.top_down_role: Regimes where reweighting cannot adequately repair the observation imbalance.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Tradeoff when inverse-probability weights are capped.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(\delta_{ij}\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(p_{ij})\), define \(Z_{ij}=\delta_{ij}X_{ij}/\max\{p_{ij},\tau\}\), \(\tau>0\). Then \[\mathbb E Z_{ij}=\frac{p_{ij}}{\max\{p_{ij},\tau\}}X_{ij},\qquad \operatorname{Var}(Z_{ij})=\frac{p_{ij}(1-p_{ij})}{\max\{p_{ij},\tau\}^2}X_{ij}^2.\] Clipping bounds weights by \(1/\tau\) but biases entries with \(p_{ij}<\tau\). No fixed positive threshold preserves unbiasedness for every positive probability while uniformly bounding the weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Capping inverse-probability weights controls instability only by introducing bias on sufficiently rare entries.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p_{ij}<\tau\Rightarrow \mathbb E Z_{ij}=(p_{ij}/\tau)X_{ij}\ne X_{ij}\text{ in general}.
knowledge_statements.title: Clipped Inverse-Probability Bias–Variance Boundary
Sampling-Correction Limits
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Limits of inverse-probability correction under vanishing or very small inclusion probabilities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For independent entry samples with probabilities \(\pi_{ij}\), inverse-probability correction uses weights \(1/\pi_{ij}\). If \(\pi_{ij}=0\), no finite weight can make the missing entry observable, and matrices differing only there remain indistinguishable. If \(0<\pi_{ij}\ll1\), the corrected single-sample contribution \(Y_{ij}/\pi_{ij}\) has second moment proportional to \(1/\pi_{ij}\); thus variance and sensitivity become unbounded as \(\pi_{ij}\downarrow0\). Weighting can correct expectation under positive known probabilities, but cannot restore absent support or guarantee stable estimation without a positive lower-probability or comparable coverage condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Inverse-probability weighting corrects sampling bias only on sampled support; zero probabilities are irreparable, and probabilities near zero cause exploding variance and instability.
assumptions_latex: Entry \((i,j)\) is sampled with known probability \(\pi_{ij}\)
Observed entry values have finite nonzero second moment
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Stable inverse-probability correction requires \(\pi_{ij}>0\) on relevant entries and quantitative control away from zero.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: inverse-probability weighting requires positivity and variance control
A precise sampling model and direct source are needed for certification.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits, but the claimed second-moment scaling depends on the exact sampling indicator and corrected-contribution definition. A precise sampling model and a direct source with a specific locator are required.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unitarily invariant norm variants of the irreducible exact-rank mismatch.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M_r\) be the rank-\(r\) truncated singular-value decomposition of \(M\). For every \(X\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r\), \[\|M-X\|_2\ge\sigma_{r+1}(M)=\|M-M_r\|_2,\qquad \|M-X\|_*\ge\sum_{k>r}\sigma_k(M)=\|M-M_r\|_*.\] Thus \(M_r\) attains the irreducible mismatch floor in both norms.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The best rank-r approximation leaves spectral error sigma r+1 and nuclear error equal to the discarded singular-value sum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_r\) minimizes spectral- and nuclear-norm approximation error with the displayed singular-value tails.
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral- and Nuclear-Norm Rank-Mismatch Floors
Low-Rank Model Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Approximation boundary for enforcing an exact rank constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(M\in\mathbb{R}^{m\times n}\) have singular values \(\sigma_1(M)\ge\cdots\ge0\), and suppose an estimator is constrained to return a matrix \(X\) with \(\operatorname{rank}(X)\le r\). Even with complete noiseless observations, \[\|M-X\|_F\ge\left(\sum_{k>r}\sigma_k(M)^2\right)^{1/2}.\] Hence exact recovery is impossible whenever \(\operatorname{rank}(M)>r\). The singular-value tail is an irreducible approximation error caused by mismatch between the assumed exact low-rank model and the true matrix; incomplete or noisy observations can only add further error.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If the true matrix has rank above the imposed rank, every admissible estimate retains at least the Frobenius norm of the discarded singular-value tail as error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|M-X\|_F\ge(\sum_{k>r}\sigma_k(M)^2)^{1/2}\), precluding exact recovery when the tail is nonzero.
