children.title: Link-Capacity Coupling
children.top_down_role: Coupling induced by shared limits on network links.

assumptions_latex: The link-flow incidence matrix is \(B\in\{0,1\}^{m\times q}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Link-capacity coupling is represented by \(Bf\le c\), a system of affine inequalities.
review_flags: Authoritative multicommodity-flow source and exact locator are missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Fixed incidence between flows and capacitated links.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The link-capacity coupling condition is
\[
Bf\le c,
\]
meaning that every link \(\ell\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\) satisfies
\[
\sum_{j=1}^q B_{\ell j}f_j\le c_\ell.
\]
Thus flows using distinct routes remain coupled whenever their routes contain a common link. For fixed \(B\), the condition is affine in \(f\), so intersecting it with any other convex flow constraints preserves convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A link couples all flows that use it: their total load must stay below its capacity, producing linear constraints for fixed routes.
knowledge_statements.title: Link-Capacity Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-route link-capacity condition is mathematically coherent and correctly classified, but no multicommodity-flow source or inspectable locator is supplied.

children.title: Routing-Flow Coupling
children.top_down_role: Coupling between path choices and carried network flows.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear conservation equations on a finite directed graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D\) be a node-arc incidence matrix. The unrestricted equation \(Df=b\) is solvable if and only if \(\mathbf1_C^{\mathsf T}b_C=0\) for every weakly connected component \(C\). With \(f\ge0\), these component-balance conditions remain necessary but are not sufficient; directed transfer feasibility is additionally required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every connected component must have zero net supply; nonnegative directed flows also require compatible arc directions.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is the node-arc incidence matrix of a finite directed graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists f\in\mathbb R^m:Df=b\iff \mathbf1_C^{\mathsf T}b_C=0\text{ for every weak component }C.
knowledge_statements.title: Incidence Conservation Compatibility

assumptions_latex: The directed graph has node-arc incidence matrix \(D\in\mathbb{R}^{v\times m}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Continuous routing is coupled to commodity flow by the affine conservation equations \(Df^k=b^k\).
review_flags: Authoritative network-flow source and exact locator are missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Splittable multicommodity routing through node conservation constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every commodity \(k\), routing and flow are coupled by
\[
Df^k=b^k,
\]
which enforces flow conservation at every node, together with \(f^k\ge0\). If total link loads are \(y=\sum_k f^k\), capacity feasibility additionally requires \(y\le c\). These equations and inequalities give a convex routing-flow representation when flows may split continuously among arcs; integrality or single-path restrictions are excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Splittable routing represents each commodity by nonnegative arc flows satisfying node conservation; commodities interact through their aggregate link loads.
knowledge_statements.title: Routing-Flow Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The splittable multicommodity routing representation correctly distinguishes continuous routing from integral or single-path routing, but it has no authoritative source or specific locator.

children.title: Path-Based Capacity Allocation
children.top_down_role: Capacity organization using path-level network representations.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complete Path and Arc-Flow Rate Equivalence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite directed networks with splittable nonnegative commodities and all source-destination paths available.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Every feasible nonnegative commodity arc flow decomposes into source-destination path flows and directed circulations. Discarding circulations preserves commodity balances and cannot increase any link load. Hence, when every source-destination path is available and capacities are upper bounds, complete path-flow and arc-flow formulations yield the same feasible commodity-rate vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: With every path available, splittable path and arc formulations produce the same feasible rates; circulations can be discarded without consuming additional capacity.
assumptions_latex: Capacities are upper bounds on aggregate link load.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_{x}(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{path}})=\operatorname{proj}_{x}(\mathcal F_{\mathrm{arc}}).
review_flags: Equivalence is asserted for feasible rate projections, not for exact load vectors containing removable circulations.
knowledge_statements.title: Complete Path and Arc-Flow Rate Equivalence

assumptions_latex: Each demand \(i\) has a finite path set \(\mathcal{P}_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Path-based capacity feasibility is the linear system \(Az\le c\), with demand rate \(x_i=\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_i}z_{ip}\).

notation.meaning: flow assigned to path \(p\) of demand \(i\)
indicator that link \(\ell\) lies on path \(p\)

review_flags: Authoritative path-flow formulation source and exact locator are missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-path, splittable flow formulation with linear capacity constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(A_{\ell,ip}=1\) when link \(\ell\) belongs to path \(p\in\mathcal{P}_i\), and let it be zero otherwise. Path-based allocation is described by
\[
x_i=\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_i}z_{ip},\qquad
\sum_i\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}_i}A_{\ell,ip}z_{ip}\le c_\ell\quad\text{for every link }\ell.
\]
Equivalently, the capacity constraints are \(Az\le c\). With continuous \(z\ge0\), this feasible region is polyhedral and permits traffic splitting across paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Allocate each demand among candidate paths; a link's load is the sum of allocations on paths containing it and cannot exceed capacity.
knowledge_statements.title: Path-Based Capacity Allocation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-path, splittable capacity-allocation representation is precise and its content kind fits the leaf, but the formulation is unsupported by a cited source and locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uncapped fixed-target power control with a feasible affine interference map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Starting from \(p^{(0)}\ge0\), iterate \[p^{(k+1)}=Fp^{(k)}+u.\] If \(\rho(F)<1\), the iterates converge to \(p^{\min}=(I-F)^{-1}u\). The convergence is linear in any induced norm satisfying \(\|F\|<1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated interference-plus-noise power updates converge linearly to the least feasible power when the spectral radius is below one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^{(k+1)}=Fp^{(k)}+u\Longrightarrow p^{(k)}\to(I-F)^{-1}u.
knowledge_statements.title: Affine Interference Fixed-Point Iteration

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uncapped fixed-target power control under a nonnegative linear interference model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write the fixed-target inequalities as \(p\ge Fp+u\), where \(F\ge0\), \(u>0\), \(F_{ii}=0\), \(F_{ij}=\gamma_i g_{ij}/g_{ii}\) for \(j\ne i\), and \(u_i=\gamma_i\sigma_i/g_{ii}\). A finite nonnegative feasible power vector exists if and only if \(\rho(F)<1\). In that case \(p^{\min}=(I-F)^{-1}u\) is the componentwise least feasible vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed SIR targets are feasible exactly when the normalized interference matrix has spectral radius below one; the inverse gives the least feasible powers.
assumptions_latex: No additional finite upper power bounds are imposed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists p\ge0:p\ge Fp+u\iff\rho(F)<1,\qquad p^{\min}=(I-F)^{-1}u.
review_flags: Finite upper power bounds require the additional test \(p^{\min}\le\bar p\).
knowledge_statements.title: Spectral-Radius Feasibility Criterion

assumptions_latex: Powers satisfy \(p_j\ge0\), gains satisfy \(g_{ij}\ge0\), and noise satisfies \(\sigma_i>0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Fixed-target signal-to-interference constraints are affine in power, although rate optimization with variable targets may be nonconvex.
review_flags: The precise interference model varies by application.
Authoritative source and exact locator are missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Single-channel linear interference model with fixed signal-to-interference targets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The signal-to-interference ratio of user \(i\) is
\[
\operatorname{SIR}_i(p)=\frac{g_{ii}p_i}{\sigma_i+\sum_{j\ne i}g_{ij}p_j}.
\]
Interference coupling appears because every \(p_j\) with \(j\ne i\) enters receiver \(i\)'s denominator. For fixed \(\gamma_i\), the requirement \(\operatorname{SIR}_i(p)\ge\gamma_i\) is equivalent to the affine inequality
\[
g_{ii}p_i-\gamma_i\sum_{j\ne i}g_{ij}p_j\ge\gamma_i\sigma_i.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each transmitter raises its own received signal but may impair other receivers; fixed signal-to-interference targets nevertheless reduce to linear power inequalities.
knowledge_statements.title: Interference Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fixed-target SIR constraint is correctly converted to an affine inequality under the stated single-channel model, but the model-dependent claim lacks an authoritative source and exact locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dual minimization when local price-response maximizers are available.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At \(\lambda^k\ge0\), choose \[x_i^k\in\arg\max_{x_i\in X_i}\bigl(U_i(x_i)-{\lambda^k}^{\mathsf T}A_ix_i\bigr)\] and update \[\lambda^{k+1}=\left[\lambda^k+\alpha_k\left(\sum_iA_ix_i^k-c\right)\right]_+.\] If the dual-optimal set is nonempty, the resulting subgradients are uniformly bounded, and \(\alpha_k>0\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k=\infty\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k^2<\infty\), then the best dual values converge to the dual optimum and \(\operatorname{dist}(\lambda^k,\Lambda^*)\to0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Users optimize independently at current prices, and projected overload-based price updates converge under standard diminishing-step assumptions.
assumptions_latex: Each local maximizer exists at every iterate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_{0\le j\le k}g(\lambda^j)\to g^*,\qquad\operatorname{dist}(\lambda^k,\Lambda^*)\to0.
knowledge_statements.title: Projected Capacity-Price Subgradient Method

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable concave network utility maximization with shared affine capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A primal-feasible collection \(x_i^*\in X_i\) and \(\lambda^*\ge0\) are optimal if every \(x_i^*\) maximizes \(U_i(x_i)-{\lambda^*}^{\mathsf T}A_ix_i\) over \(X_i\) and \[{\lambda^*}^{\mathsf T}\left(c-\sum_iA_ix_i^*\right)=0.\] Under an applicable convex constraint qualification, these conditions are also necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local optimality at common prices, primal feasibility, nonnegative prices, and complementary slackness certify global network optimality.
assumptions_latex: A convex constraint qualification holds when necessity is asserted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: x^*\text{ primal feasible},\ \lambda^*\ge0,\ x_i^*\in\arg\max_{x_i\in X_i}(U_i(x_i)-{\lambda^*}^{\mathsf T}A_ix_i),\ {\lambda^*}^{\mathsf T}(c-\sum_iA_ix_i^*)=0\Rightarrow(x^*,\lambda^*)\text{ optimal}.
knowledge_statements.title: Network Capacity-Price KKT Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Slater Qualification for Network Utility Duality
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separable concave utility maximization with shared affine capacity inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose each \(X_i\) is convex, each \(U_i\) is proper upper-semicontinuous and concave, the primal value is finite, and there exist \(\bar x_i\in\operatorname{ri}X_i\) satisfying \(\sum_iA_i\bar x_i<c\). Then the capacity-price dual has zero duality gap and admits an optimal multiplier.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relative-interior allocation strictly below every capacity gives strong duality and an optimal capacity-price vector.
assumptions_latex: Each \(U_i\) is proper upper-semicontinuous and concave.
\(\bar x_i\in\operatorname{ri}X_i\) and \(\sum_iA_i\bar x_i<c\) for some \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^*=\min_{\lambda\ge0}g(\lambda).

notation.meaning: relative interior of local feasible set

review_flags: Relative-interior formulations can be weakened for capacity inequalities that are redundant on the feasible affine hull.
knowledge_statements.title: Slater Qualification for Network Utility Duality

assumptions_latex: Each local decision set \(X_i\) is nonempty and convex.
Each utility \(U_i\) is concave, and local load is \(A_i x_i\).
A constraint qualification ensures strong duality for \(\sum_i A_i x_i\le c\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Dualizing shared capacity separates the primal maximization across users, coupled only through the common price \(\lambda\).
review_flags: Authoritative dual-decomposition source and exact locator are missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Price decomposition for separable utility with shared affine capacities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For the problem of maximizing \(\sum_i U_i(x_i)\) subject to \(x_i\in X_i\) and \(\sum_i A_i x_i\le c\), introduce \(\lambda\ge0\). Its dual objective is
\[
g(\lambda)=\lambda^{\mathsf T}c+\sum_i\sup_{x_i\in X_i}\bigl(U_i(x_i)-\lambda^{\mathsf T}A_i x_i\bigr),
\]
and the dual problem is \(\inf_{\lambda\ge0}g(\lambda)\). For fixed \(\lambda\), every supremum is an independent local optimization; strong duality makes the dual optimum equal the primal optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing shared capacities with nonnegative multipliers decomposes network utility maximization into independent local problems plus a master price minimization.
knowledge_statements.title: Network Dual-Decomposition Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The dual objective and decomposition signs are consistent with a concave maximization problem having shared upper-bound constraints, and `duality` is the correct content kind. However, the constraint qualification is left abstract and neither it nor the decomposition claim has a supporting source and locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convexification of isolated finite route-selection variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite nonempty route set \(\mathcal P\), \[\operatorname{conv}\{e_p:p\in\mathcal P\}=\left\{z\in\mathbb R_+^{|\mathcal P|}:\sum_{p\in\mathcal P}z_p=1\right\}.\] Fractional points represent splittable routing and are not feasible unsplittable selections.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The simplex is the exact convex hull of one-route selections, but its fractional points describe split routing.
assumptions_latex: \(e_p\) is the unit vector for route \(p\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{conv}\{e_p:p\in\mathcal P\}=\{z\ge0:\mathbf1^{\mathsf T}z=1\}.
knowledge_statements.title: Convex Hull of Single-Path Selections

assumptions_latex: A source-destination pair has at least two admissible routes.
Exactly one route must be selected: \(\sum_p z_p=1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unsplittable routing feasible set is nonconvex; replacing \(z_p\in\{0,1\}\) by \(0\le z_p\le1\) is a relaxation.
review_flags: Authoritative integer-routing source and exact locator are missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Loss of convexity caused by single-path or integral routing decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(e_p\) and \(e_q\) select two distinct admissible routes. Both satisfy \(z\in\{0,1\}^{|\mathcal{P}|}\) and \(\sum_r z_r=1\), but their midpoint \((e_p+e_q)/2\) is not binary. Hence the single-path feasible set
\[
\left\{z\in\{0,1\}^{|\mathcal{P}|}:\sum_{p\in\mathcal{P}}z_p=1\right\}
\]
is nonconvex. Continuous path-flow formulations cross this boundary by allowing fractional routing, which changes the model to splittable flow.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Requiring one integral route destroys convexity: the midpoint of two valid route selections is fractional and therefore infeasible.
knowledge_statements.title: Discrete Routing Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary classification and nonconvexity claim are correct, but the statement includes a midpoint proof argument and supplies no authoritative integer-routing source or exact locator. Source support is required before choosing a proof-free final formulation.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Explicit Failure of Joint Rate Concavity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Normalized interference-as-noise rate with one desired and one interfering power.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r(p_1,p_2)=\log\!\left(1+p_1/(1+p_2)\right)\). Then \[r(1,1)<\tfrac12r(1,0)+\tfrac12r(1,2),\] so \(r\) is not jointly concave on \(\mathbb R_+^2\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A normalized two-power rate violates the midpoint inequality for concavity.
assumptions_latex: Noise and relevant channel gains are normalized to one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: r\text{ is not jointly concave on }\mathbb R_+^2.
knowledge_statements.title: Explicit Failure of Joint Rate Concavity

assumptions_latex: Direct and cross gains are positive, and noise powers are positive.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Joint rate expressions under mutual interference generally fail concavity, so maximizing their sum is not generally a convex program.

notation.meaning: channel gain from transmitter \(j\) to receiver \(i\)

review_flags: The failure claim requires an authoritative interference-optimization source.
Exact convex special cases depend on the selected physical model.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic mutual-interference rate model outside fixed-target convex formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For user \(i\), consider
\[
r_i(p)=\log\!\left(1+\frac{g_{ii}p_i}{\sigma_i+\sum_{j\ne i}g_{ij}p_j}\right).
\]
Although \(r_i\) is concave in \(p_i\) when the interfering powers are fixed, it is generally not jointly concave in the full vector \(p\). Consequently, maximizing \(\sum_i w_i r_i(p)\) over a convex power box need not be a convex optimization problem. Fixed interference, orthogonal channels, or suitable transformations are additional structures, not generic consequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When users mutually interfere, each rate depends nonconcavely on all powers; weighted sum-rate maximization can therefore fall outside convex optimization.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonconvex Interference Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The generic nonconcavity boundary is appropriately qualified and correctly classified as a failure boundary, but its precise validity and special cases depend on the interference model. No authoritative source or locator is supplied.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distinguishes GP log-domain convexity from ordinary convexity in the original variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The monomial, hence posynomial, \(f(x)=x^{1/2}\) on \(\mathbb R_{++}\) satisfies \(\log f(e^y)=y/2\), but \(f''(x)=-1/(4x^{3/2})<0\). Thus a posynomial need not be convex in its original variables; the standard GP property is convexity of \(\log f(e^y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A posynomial can be concave in its original variable even though its logarithmic transform is convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^{1/2}\) is a posynomial and log-log affine but is strictly concave in \(x\).
knowledge_statements.title: Original-Variable Nonconvexity Counterexample

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic closure rules used to construct and normalize standard posynomial constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(f\) and \(g\) are posynomials, \(m\) is a monomial, and \(\alpha>0\), then \(f+g\), \(fg\), \(\alpha f\), and \(f/m\) are posynomials. Substitution of positive monomials for every argument of a posynomial also preserves posynomial form. Hence \(f(x)\le m(x)\) is exactly normalized as \(f(x)/m(x)\le1\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Posynomials are closed under positive sums, products, positive scaling, monomial division, and monomial substitution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f+g\), \(fg\), \(\alpha f\), and \(f/m\) are posynomials, and positive monomial substitution preserves posynomial form.
knowledge_statements.title: Posynomial Closure and Normalization

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A posynomial is a finite positive sum of monomials and becomes a convex log-sum-exp function under logarithmic variables.
review_flags: Supplied locator hints do not support geometric programming.
Authoritative geometric-programming source and exact locator are missing.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Standard positive-variable posynomials used in geometric programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A monomial on \(\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\) has the form \(m(x)=c\prod_{j=1}^n x_j^{a_j}\), where \(c>0\) and \(a_j\in\mathbb{R}\). A posynomial is a finite sum
\[
f(x)=\sum_{k=1}^K c_k\prod_{j=1}^n x_j^{a_{kj}}.
\]
Under \(x_j=e^{y_j}\), its logarithm becomes
\[
\log f(e^y)=\log\!\left(\sum_{k=1}^K e^{a_k^{\mathsf T}y+\log c_k}\right),
\]
which is convex in \(y\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A posynomial is a positive sum of generalized monomials; after taking logarithmic variables and objective values, it becomes a convex log-sum-exp expression.
knowledge_statements.title: Posynomial Design Components

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic closure and inequality normalization for monomial GP components.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If \(m_1(x)=c_1x^{a^{(1)}}\) and \(m_2(x)=c_2x^{a^{(2)}}\), then \(m_1m_2\), \(m_1/m_2\), and \(m_1^q\) are monomials for every \(q\in\mathbb R\). Consequently \(m_1(x)\le m_2(x)\) is equivalent to \(m_1(x)/m_2(x)\le1\), which under \(y=\log x\) is \[\log(c_1/c_2)+(a^{(1)}-a^{(2)})^{\mathsf T}y\le0.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Monomials are closed under products, quotients and real powers, and comparisons of monomials become affine inequalities after logarithms.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(m_1m_2\), \(m_1/m_2\), and \(m_1^q\) are monomials, while \(m_1\le m_2\) is affine in \(\log x\).
knowledge_statements.title: Monomial Closure and Comparison
Monomial Balance Components
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive-variable monomials and their equality-balance form in geometric programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A monomial on \(\mathbb{R}_{++}^n\) is a function \(m(x)=c\prod_{k=1}^n x_k^{a_k}\), where \(c>0\) and \(a_k\in\mathbb{R}\). A monomial balance constraint has the form \(m_1(x)=m_2(x)\). Since both sides are positive, it is equivalently written as \(m_1(x)/m_2(x)=1\), and the quotient is again a monomial. Under \(y_k=\log x_k\), this balance becomes the affine equation \(\log(c_1/c_2)+(a^{(1)}-a^{(2)})^\mathsf{T}y=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A monomial is a positive coefficient times arbitrary real powers of positive variables. Equality between two monomials becomes an affine equation after taking logarithms.
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition, balance equivalence, logarithmic affine form, and definition content kind fit the terminal container, but the record has no inspectable citation. Supply an authoritative geometric-programming source with a section, definition, or page locator.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Differential curvature and flat directions of a log-transformed posynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(F(y)=\log\sum_{k=1}^K\exp(a_k^{\mathsf T}y+\log c_k)\), define \(w_k(y)=\exp(a_k^{\mathsf T}y+\log c_k)/\sum_\ell\exp(a_\ell^{\mathsf T}y+\log c_\ell)\) and \(\bar a(y)=\sum_kw_k(y)a_k\). Then \[\nabla F(y)=\bar a(y),\qquad \nabla^2F(y)=\sum_kw_k(y)(a_k-\bar a(y))(a_k-\bar a(y))^{\mathsf T}\succeq0.\] Along a direction \(d\), the curvature is positive exactly when the values \(a_k^{\mathsf T}d\) are not all equal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The Hessian of a transformed posynomial is the softmax-weighted covariance of its exponent vectors, characterizing convexity and flat directions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\nabla^2F(y)=\sum_kw_k(y)(a_k-\bar a(y))(a_k-\bar a(y))^{\mathsf T}\succeq0\).
knowledge_statements.title: Log-Posynomial Curvature
Geometric-Program Log-Convexification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact logarithmic transformation of a standard-form geometric program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider minimizing a posynomial \(f_0(x)\) subject to \(f_i(x)\leq 1\) and \(h_j(x)=1\), where each \(f_i\) is posynomial, each \(h_j\) is monomial, and \(x>0\). Set \(y=\log x\). If \(f_i(x)=\sum_k c_{ik}x^{a_{ik}}\), then \(F_i(y)=\log f_i(e^y)=\log\!\left(\sum_k\exp(a_{ik}^{\mathsf T}y+\log c_{ik})\right)\) is convex, while \(H_j(y)=\log h_j(e^y)\) is affine. Thus the original problem is equivalent to minimizing \(F_0(y)\) subject to \(F_i(y)\leq0\) and \(H_j(y)=0\).

children.title: Structural GP Design
children.top_down_role: Geometric-programming templates for structural sizing or configuration.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weight and compliance sizing of a fixed-geometry statically determinate truss under one fixed load case.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed-geometry statically determinate truss, let \(A_i>0\) be bar areas and let nonzero axial forces \(N_i\) be fixed by equilibrium under the prescribed load. With \(l_i,\rho_i,E_i,\sigma_i,C>0\), weight \(\sum_i\rho_il_iA_i\) is posynomial, stress limits are \(|N_i|/(\sigma_iA_i)\le1\), and the compliance limit is \[\frac{1}{C}\sum_i\frac{N_i^2l_i}{E_iA_i}\le1.\] Consequently weight minimization subject to these limits and positive monomial area bounds is a geometric program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed-geometry statically determinate truss has a GP sizing model because weight and compliance are posynomials and each stress limit is monomial.
assumptions_latex: Geometry and the load case are fixed
The truss is statically determinate, so \(N_i\) do not depend on \(A\)
Zero-force members are omitted from stress constraints
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The stated truss weight-minimization model is a geometric program.

notation.meaning: fixed axial force in bar i

review_flags: The fixed-force representation does not extend directly to statically indeterminate trusses, where member forces depend on the sizing variables.
knowledge_statements.title: Statically Determinate Truss-Sizing GP
Structural GP Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: GP representation of positive structural sizing models with posynomial performance constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let the positive sizing variables be \(x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\). Suppose cost \(c_0(x)\) and every normalized stress, displacement, buckling, or frequency-limit function \(c_j(x)\) are posynomials, while required design identities are monomial equations \(m_k(x)=1\). Then structural sizing is represented by the geometric program \[\min_{x>0}\ c_0(x)\quad\text{subject to}\quad c_j(x)\le 1\ (j=1,\ldots,p),\qquad m_k(x)=1\ (k=1,\ldots,q).\] Under \(y_i=\log x_i\), its objective and inequality functions become convex log-sum-exp functions and its equalities become affine.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive structural sizing model is a geometric program when its normalized performance limits are posynomials and its design identities are monomials.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(y=\log x\) transforms the model into a convex optimization problem.

notation.meaning: posynomial objective or normalized performance functions

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and content kind fit the structural-design leaf, but no cited source supports the claimed structural GP template or the listed stress, displacement, buckling, and frequency applications.

children.title: GP Suitability Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits on geometric-programming representations for mechanical or structural behavior.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit failure of a lower bound on a nonmonomial posynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The posynomial \(p(x)=x+x^{-1}\) on \(\mathbb R_{++}\) does not yield a standard GP constraint when required to satisfy \(p(x)\ge3\). Under \(y=\log x\), the feasible set is \[\{y:e^y+e^{-y}\ge3\}=(-\infty,-\operatorname{arcosh}(3/2)]\cup[\operatorname{arcosh}(3/2),\infty),\] which is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A posynomial lower bound can become a disconnected nonconvex set in logarithmic variables.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x>0:x+x^{-1}\ge3\}\) is not log-convex and the displayed constraint is not a standard GP constraint.
knowledge_statements.title: Posynomial Lower-Bound Counterexample
GP Suitability Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary separating exact geometric-program models from non-GP mechanical or structural formulations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A positive-variable design model lies within the exact GP class only when, after algebraic normalization, its objective and inequality left sides are posynomials and every equality is monomial. A sign-indefinite sum, a lower bound on a nonmonomial posynomial, or an equality \(p(x)=1\) with nonmonomial posynomial \(p\) generally leaves this class: after \(y=\log x\), it produces respectively a difference of log-sum-exp terms, a nonconvex superlevel constraint, or a nonaffine equality. Such models require approximation, relaxation, or a different optimization class.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact GP modeling fails when normalization introduces signomial differences, posynomial lower bounds, or nonmonomial equalities, unless special structure restores convexity.
assumptions_latex: The proposed formulation is interpreted after algebraic normalization
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model is not an exact standard GP when its log-transformed feasible set or objective is nonconvex.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the leaf, but the claim needs a source distinguishing failure of the displayed standard formulation from failure of every equivalent GP reformulation, including reformulations using auxiliary variables or special structure.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the strictly positive subeigenvector equivalence at a boundary spectral radius without irreducibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(B=\begin{bmatrix}1&1\\0&1\end{bmatrix}\), one has \(B\ge0\) and \(\rho(B)=1\), but no \(v>0\) satisfies \(Bv\le v\), since the first component would require \(v_1+v_2\le v_1\). Thus for a reducible nonnegative matrix, \(\rho(B)\le r\) need not admit a strictly positive certificate \(Bv\le rv\) at equality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reducible nonnegative matrix can meet a spectral-radius bound without possessing the strictly positive boundary certificate used in the GP formulation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(B)=r\) but \(\nexists v>0:Bv\le rv\).
knowledge_statements.title: Reducible Boundary-Certificate Failure

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Discrete-time entrywise-positive system design with an attained Perron certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B(\theta)>0\) have posynomial entries for \(\theta>0\). For \(r>0\), \[\rho(B(\theta))\le r\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad\exists v>0:\ B(\theta)v\le rv.\] Componentwise normalization gives \[\frac{\sum_jB_{ij}(\theta)v_j}{rv_i}\le1,\] whose left sides are posynomials in \((\theta,v)\). Therefore a posynomial-cost design subject to this spectral-radius bound and other GP constraints is a geometric program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an entrywise-positive discrete-time system, a spectral-radius bound is equivalent to positive-vector inequalities having standard GP form.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho(B(\theta))\le r\iff\exists v>0:B(\theta)v\le rv\), and the normalized inequalities are posynomial.
review_flags: Entrywise positivity ensures irreducibility and an attained strictly positive certificate at the spectral-radius boundary.
knowledge_statements.title: Discrete-Time Positive-System GP
Positive-System GP Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: GP stability design for parameterized positive continuous-time linear systems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A(\theta)=M(\theta)-D(\theta)\), where \(\theta\in\mathbb R_{++}^p\), \(M(\theta)\ge0\) has posynomial entries, and \(D(\theta)\) is diagonal with positive monomial diagonal entries. The Metzler matrix \(A(\theta)\) is Hurwitz stable if and only if there exists \(v\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\) such that \(M(\theta)v<D(\theta)v\). Componentwise division by the monomial \(D_{ii}(\theta)v_i\) yields posynomial inequalities, so minimizing a posynomial design cost subject to these inequalities is a geometric program, with strictness implemented by a prescribed positive margin.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stability design of a structured positive system becomes a GP by introducing a positive vector satisfying a componentwise linear Lyapunov inequality.
assumptions_latex: \(M_{ij}\) are posynomials and \(D_{ii}\) are positive monomials
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(\theta)\) is Hurwitz exactly when \(\exists v>0: M(\theta)v<D(\theta)v\), and these inequalities have GP form.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits positive-system design, but the fixed positive margin used to implement a strict stability inequality generally gives a sufficient restricted design condition rather than an exact encoding of all Hurwitz-stable designs. An authoritative source is required to specify the certificate and margin formulation precisely.

children.title: Monomial Approximation
children.top_down_role: Approximation interfaces based on monomial surrogates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Globally valid tangent monomial lower bound for a posynomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p(x)=\sum_{k=1}^K u_k(x)\), where every \(u_k\) is a positive monomial, and fix \(x^0\in\mathbb R_{++}^n\). Define \(\alpha_k=u_k(x^0)/p(x^0)\) and \[m(x)=\prod_{k=1}^K\left(\frac{u_k(x)}{\alpha_k}\right)^{\alpha_k}.\] Then \(\alpha_k>0\), \(\sum_k\alpha_k=1\), \(m(x)\leq p(x)\) for all \(x>0\), \(m(x^0)=p(x^0)\), and their log-coordinate gradients agree at \(x^0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted AM–GM gives a global monomial lower bound tangent to a posynomial in logarithmic coordinates.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: m\leq p,\quad m(x^0)=p(x^0),\quad \nabla_{\log x}\log m(x^0)=\nabla_{\log x}\log p(x^0).

notation.meaning: normalized contribution of term k at the fitting point

knowledge_statements.title: Weighted AM–GM Monomial Condensation
Monomial Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: First-order log-domain monomial approximation of a positive differentiable function.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R_{++}^n\to\mathbb R_{++}\) be differentiable at \(x^0\). Define \(a_i=\left.\partial\log f(x)/\partial\log x_i\right|_{x=x^0}\). Its first-order monomial approximation is \[\widehat f(x)=f(x^0)\prod_{i=1}^n\left(\frac{x_i}{x_i^0}\right)^{a_i}.\] Equivalently, \(\log\widehat f(e^y)\) is the affine Taylor approximation of \(\log f(e^y)\) at \(y^0=\log x^0\). Consequently, \(\widehat f(x^0)=f(x^0)\) and the two functions have identical gradients with respect to logarithmic coordinates at \(x^0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exponentiating the affine Taylor model of a positive function in log-coordinates gives a monomial matching its value and log-gradient locally.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\widehat f(x^0)=f(x^0)\) and \(\nabla_y\log\widehat f(e^{y^0})=\nabla_y\log f(e^{y^0})\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The log-domain Taylor formula is mathematically coherent and representation is an appropriate kind, but the record supplies no inspectable source for the approximation formula and its value-and-log-gradient matching properties.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines ell-one residual approximation and gives its auxiliary-variable LP formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For A\in\mathbf{R}^{m\times n} and b\in\mathbf{R}^m, sum-of-absolute-residuals approximation is \min_{x\in\mathbf{R}^n}\|Ax-b\|_1=\min_x\sum_{i=1}^m|a_i^Tx-b_i|. It is equivalent to the linear program \min_{x,t}\mathbf{1}^Tt subject to -t\preccurlyeq Ax-b\preccurlyeq t, with t\in\mathbf{R}^m.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sum-of-absolute-residuals fitting minimizes the ell-one norm of the affine residual. Introducing one componentwise magnitude bound per residual gives an equivalent linear program.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min_x\|Ax-b\|_1=\min_{x,t}\{\mathbf{1}^Tt:-t\preccurlyeq Ax-b\preccurlyeq t\}.

source_evidence.locator: Approximation and fitting / 6.1. Norm approximation / Definition 6.1-extra-5

children.title: Posynomial Approximation
children.top_down_role: Approximation interfaces based on posynomial surrogates.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uniform multiplicative comparison between a posynomial sum and the largest constituent monomial.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For affine functions \(z_k(y)=a_k^Ty+b_k\), \[\max_k z_k(y)\leq\log\sum_{k=1}^K e^{z_k(y)}\leq\max_k z_k(y)+\log K.\] Equivalently, for positive monomials \(m_k(x)\), \[\max_k m_k(x)\leq\sum_{k=1}^K m_k(x)\leq K\max_k m_k(x).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sum of K monomials lies between their maximum and K times their maximum.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: 0\leq\log\!\left(\sum_km_k(x)\right)-\max_k\log m_k(x)\leq\log K.
knowledge_statements.title: Log-Sum-Exp Maximum Bound
Posynomial Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite positive-exponential approximation in logarithmic coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a positive target function \(f:\mathcal D\to\mathbb R_{++}\), where \(\mathcal D\subseteq\mathbb R_{++}^n\), a posynomial approximation is a function \[\widehat f(x)=\sum_{k=1}^K c_k\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{a_{ik}},\qquad c_k>0,\quad a_{ik}\in\mathbb R,\] selected to approximate \(f\) on a specified fitting region \(R\subseteq\mathcal D\) under a stated error criterion. In logarithmic coordinates \(y=\log x\), it satisfies \(\log\widehat f(e^y)=\log\sum_{k=1}^K\exp(a_k^Ty+\log c_k)\), hence is convex as a log-domain function and remains admissible in GP objectives and upper-bound inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A posynomial approximation is a finite positive sum of monomials fitted on a declared region and directly usable in GP upper-bound constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\log\widehat f(e^y)\) is convex in \(y\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and the stated log-sum-exp property is consistent with the formula, but no inspectable source supports this definition of a fitted posynomial approximation or its stated GP use.

children.title: Approximation-Fidelity Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes governing the faithfulness of geometric-programming approximations.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility and violation transfer from a surrogate inequality to its positive target.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(g,\widehat g:R\to\mathbb R_{++}\). If \(g\leq\widehat g\) on \(R\), then \(\widehat g(x)\leq1\) certifies \(g(x)\leq1\). More generally, if \(g\leq e^\varepsilon\widehat g\) on \(R\), then \(\widehat g(x)\leq1\) implies \(g(x)\leq e^\varepsilon\). A lower surrogate \(\widehat g\leq g\) alone gives neither implication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A uniform upper surrogate certifies original feasibility, while a multiplicative upper-error bound certifies bounded violation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \widehat g(x)\leq1\Rightarrow g(x)\leq e^\varepsilon\quad\text{if }g\leq e^\varepsilon\widehat g\text{ on }R.

notation.meaning: region on which the bound holds

knowledge_statements.title: One-Sided Fidelity Certificate

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Local Monomial Match Without Global Fidelity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A monomial first-order approximation with unbounded nonlocal relative error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f(x)=\exp((\log x)^2)\) on \(\mathbb R_{++}\). Its first-order log-domain monomial approximation at \(x^0=1\) is \(\widehat f(x)=1\): values and log-gradients agree at \(1\). Nevertheless, \[\log\frac{f(x)}{\widehat f(x)}=(\log x)^2,\] which is unbounded on \(\mathbb R_{++}\). Thus local first-order monomial matching implies no finite global multiplicative-error bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tangent monomial can match value and log-gradient yet have unbounded global relative error.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \sup_{x>0}\left|\log\frac{f(x)}{\widehat f(x)}\right|=+\infty.
knowledge_statements.title: Local Monomial Match Without Global Fidelity
Approximation-Fidelity Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local, regional, and global fidelity guarantees for GP-compatible approximations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f,\widehat f:R\to\mathbb R_{++}\). Local first-order fidelity at \(x^0\in R\) means equality of values and log-gradients there. Regional relative fidelity with tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\) means \(e^{-\varepsilon}f(x)\le\widehat f(x)\le e^{\varepsilon}f(x)\) for every \(x\in R\). Global fidelity is the same bound with \(R=\mathcal D\). A local monomial match alone implies neither regional nor global error control; either stronger analytic bounds or explicit validation over the intended region is required before an approximate GP solution can be interpreted outside its fitting neighborhood.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Value-and-gradient matching is local only; regional or global fidelity requires a uniform multiplicative error bound on the corresponding domain.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Local first-order agreement does not imply \(e^{-\varepsilon}f\le\widehat f\le e^{\varepsilon}f\) on a nonlocal region.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The property kind fits the fidelity-regime leaf, but the global domain \(\mathcal D\) is not introduced, and no source supports the selected local, regional, and global fidelity definitions or the asserted limitation of local matching.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Exact Epigraph Lift of Generalized Posynomials
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact standard-GP epigraph representation for finitely constructed generalized posynomials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(f:\mathbb R_{++}^n\to\mathbb R_{++}\) be obtained from monomials by finitely many additions, multiplications, positive powers, and pointwise maxima. Introducing a positive epigraph variable for each subexpression and imposing the corresponding monomial or posynomial upper-epigraph inequalities produces a standard-GP lift \(F_{\mathrm{lift}}\) satisfying \[\operatorname{proj}_x F_{\mathrm{lift}}=\{x\in\mathbb R_{++}^n:f(x)\leq1\}.\] For minimization of \(f\), an outer epigraph variable preserves the optimal value and yields an optimizer correspondence after auxiliary variables are eliminated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite generalized-posynomial inequality has an exact standard-GP epigraph lift; the auxiliary inequalities introduce no relaxation after projection.
assumptions_latex: All powers in the construction are positive
The expression uses finitely many monotone generalized-posynomial operations
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \operatorname{proj}_x F_{\mathrm{lift}}=\{x:f(x)\leq1\}.

notation.meaning: feasible set of the lifted standard GP

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Epigraph Lift of Generalized Posynomials
Geometric-Program Approximation Exactness
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Criterion for an application model to be represented exactly, rather than approximately, as a standard GP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a positive-variable optimization model. A proposed GP reformulation is exact when there is a bijection between its feasible points and those of a standard-form GP that preserves objective values and attainment. A sufficient algebraic criterion is that, after multiplying constraints by positive monomials and introducing only eliminable positive auxiliaries, the objective and every inequality have posynomial form \(p(x)\le1\), while every equality has monomial form \(m(x)=1\). The logarithmic substitution \(y=\log x\) then changes representation but introduces no approximation, relaxation, or loss of feasible designs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A GP reformulation is exact when admissible algebra and eliminable auxiliaries yield posynomial inequalities and monomial equalities without changing feasible points or objectives.
assumptions_latex: All physical variables represented logarithmically are strictly positive
Auxiliary-variable elimination preserves feasibility and objective values
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The GP and original model are equivalent, and \(y=\log x\) introduces no approximation.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the correct role for this leaf, but the asserted sufficient criterion, especially the treatment of eliminable auxiliaries and the bijection requirement, needs an authoritative source with a precise exact-reformulation statement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility-preserving local GP approximation for a difference-of-posynomials inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(p(x)\leq q(x)\) with posynomials \(p,q\), let \(x^r>0\) be feasible and let \(m_r\) be the weighted-AM–GM monomial lower bound of \(q\) at \(x^r\). Then \(m_r\leq q\), \(m_r(x^r)=q(x^r)\), and first-order log-coordinate agreement holds. The GP constraint \(p(x)/m_r(x)\leq1\) is an inner approximation: every point satisfying it obeys \(p(x)\leq q(x)\), and \(x^r\) remains feasible. Repetition is a local heuristic unless additional regularity and update assumptions establish stationarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Replacing the right-hand posynomial by its tangent monomial lower bound gives a conservative GP subproblem that preserves feasibility from a feasible iterate.
assumptions_latex: Each condensed GP is solved to a feasible point
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p(x)\leq m_r(x)\Rightarrow p(x)\leq q(x),\qquad p(x^r)\leq m_r(x^r).

notation.meaning: monomial condensation of q at iteration r

knowledge_statements.title: Sequential Inner GP Condensation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Log-domain representation after separating positive and negative signomial terms.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(s(x)=\sum_{k\in P}c_kx^{a_k}-\sum_{\ell\in N}d_\ell x^{b_\ell}\), where \(c_k,d_\ell>0\), \(x>0\), and both index sets are nonempty. With \(y=\log x\), \(s(x)\leq0\) is equivalent to \[\log\sum_{k\in P}e^{a_k^Ty+\log c_k}-\log\sum_{\ell\in N}e^{b_\ell^Ty+\log d_\ell}\leq0.\] Both terms are convex, but their difference and its sublevel set need not be convex.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed-sign signomial inequality becomes a difference of two convex log-sum-exp functions, not generally a convex constraint.
assumptions_latex: Both signed term groups are nonempty
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: s(x)\leq0\iff h_P(y)-h_N(y)\leq0,\quad h_P,h_N\text{ convex}.
knowledge_statements.title: Difference-of-Convex Log Representation

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete mixed-sign signomial showing loss of GP log-convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x>0\), the signomial constraint \(3-x-x^{-1}\le 0\) becomes, under \(y=\log x\), \(e^y+e^{-y}\ge 3\). Its feasible set is \[(-\infty,-\operatorname{arcosh}(3/2)]\cup[\operatorname{arcosh}(3/2),\infty),\] which is disconnected and nonconvex. Thus arbitrary signed monomial sums do not retain the general logarithmic convexification guarantee of geometric programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simple mixed-sign signomial has a disconnected feasible set in logarithmic coordinates, demonstrating the boundary of standard GP convexification.
assumptions_latex: The signomial inequality is imposed exactly, without relaxation
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{y:e^y+e^{-y}\ge3\}\text{ is nonconvex}.
knowledge_statements.title: Disconnected Log-Feasible Signomial Constraint
Signomial-Programming Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concrete signomial constraint whose logarithmic image is nonconvex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The positive-variable constraint \[3-x-x^{-1}\le0,\qquad x>0,\] is signomial because its nonconstant terms have negative coefficients. With \(y=\log x\), it becomes \(e^y+e^{-y}\ge3\). Its feasible set is \[\left(-\infty,-\operatorname{arcosh}(3/2)\right]\cup\left[\operatorname{arcosh}(3/2),\infty\right),\] which is not convex. Thus allowing arbitrary signed sums of monomials destroys the general convexity guarantee of geometric programming. Particular signomial expressions may still be reformulable, but coefficient signs alone do not supply an exact GP representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A signed monomial sum can become a disconnected feasible set after logarithmic transformation, demonstrating the boundary beyond standard geometric programming.
assumptions_latex: The signomial inequality is imposed without relaxation
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The log-domain feasible set is nonconvex, so the constraint is not a standard GP constraint.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample is internally consistent and its content kind fits the signomial boundary, but no inspectable source is supplied for this nontrivial boundary claim.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Stationary-Limit Guarantee for Sequential Inner GP
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Proposed convergence claim for sequential monomial condensation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The proposed KKT accumulation-point guarantee is deferred: compactness, exact surrogate solution, first-order consistency, a constraint qualification, and an informally stated anti-cycling condition do not identify a sufficiently precise sequential-convex-programming theorem or update rule.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The proposed stationary-limit theorem is too underspecified to publish as a general guarantee for sequential inner geometric programming.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{No general KKT convergence conclusion is accepted from the stated assumptions.}
knowledge_statements.title: Stationary-Limit Guarantee for Sequential Inner GP

intermediate_metadata.reason: The local inventory contains mixed-sign nonconvexity, the DC log representation, and feasibility-preserving monomial condensation. The proposed convergence theorem is deferred, so expansion remains necessary. Monomial–posynomial approximation mechanics and exact GP convexification are excluded to sibling leaves.

assumptions_latex: One fixed symmetry type is selected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: h_k=\pm h_{N-1-k}\text{ are affine constraints and preserve convexity}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex enforcement of standard real FIR linear-phase coefficient symmetries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a real length-\(N\) FIR filter, coefficient relations \(h_k=h_{N-1-k}\) impose symmetric linear phase, while \(h_k=-h_{N-1-k}\) impose antisymmetric linear phase. These are affine equality constraints, so adding either fixed family to a convex FIR response-error model preserves convexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Real FIR linear-phase symmetry or antisymmetry is imposed by affine coefficient equalities and preserves convexity.
knowledge_statements.title: Linear-Phase Affine Restrictions

assumptions_latex: The response functional is nonzero at the selected frequency.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{h:|H_h(\omega)|\ge\gamma\}\text{ is nonconvex}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvexity of general passband lower-magnitude constraints without fixed phase.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a fixed frequency \(\omega\) and \(\gamma>0\), the constraint \(|H_h(\omega)|\ge\gamma\) is nonconvex in \(h\): choose \(h_+\) with \(H_{h_+}(\omega)=\gamma\) and set \(h_-=-h_+\). Both are feasible, whereas their midpoint is not. Convex FIR formulations instead control complex response error, impose an affine phase convention, or use convex upper magnitude bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A direct lower bound on FIR response magnitude is generally nonconvex unless phase or additional structure is fixed.
knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Magnitude FIR Boundary

assumptions_latex: The FIR response is affine in \(h\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{The objective is convex quadratic; uniqueness holds exactly when }Q^{1/2}V\text{ has full column rank}.

notation.meaning: Matrix whose rows are sampled FIR response vectors.
Diagonal matrix of nonnegative sample weights.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-grid unconstrained quadratic design of an FIR frequency response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For sampled frequencies \(\omega_j\), desired responses \(D_j\), and weights \(q_j\ge0\), define \(v(\omega_j)=(1,e^{-\mathrm i\omega_j},\ldots,e^{-\mathrm i(N-1)\omega_j})\). Then \[\min_h\sum_{j=1}^m q_j|v(\omega_j)^{\mathsf T}h-D_j|^2\] is a convex quadratic least-squares problem. In the unconstrained coefficient space it has a unique minimizer exactly when the weighted design matrix \(Q^{1/2}V\) has full column rank.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sampled weighted least-squares FIR synthesis is a convex quadratic problem, with uniqueness exactly under full column rank of the weighted design matrix.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted Least-Squares FIR Design
FIR Filter Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex minimax design of a finite-impulse-response filter over prescribed frequency bands.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For coefficients \(h=(h_0,\ldots,h_{N-1})\in\mathbb C^N\), define \(H_h(\omega)=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}h_ke^{-\mathrm i k\omega}\). Given desired response \(D:\Omega\to\mathbb C\) and weight \(W:\Omega\to\mathbb R_+\), minimax FIR design is \[\min_{h,t}\ t\quad\text{subject to}\quad W(\omega)|H_h(\omega)-D(\omega)|\le t\quad\text{for all }\omega\in\Omega.\] Since each response value is affine in \(h\), every sampled-frequency constraint is second-order-cone representable. A finite grid gives an SOCP; the continuous-frequency version is a semi-infinite convex program unless an exact finite representation is supplied.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimax FIR design bounds the weighted complex response error; frequency sampling yields an SOCP, while continuous bands produce a semi-infinite convex problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The sampled formulation is an SOCP, and the continuous-band formulation is convex and semi-infinite.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits FIR filter design and the sampled versus continuous-frequency distinction is coherent, but no source supports the minimax formulation, sampled SOCP representation, and semi-infinite classification.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a real-coefficient finite-impulse-response filter, its impulse response, and its action on complex exponentials.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For $n\in\mathbb N$ and real coefficients $h_0,\ldots,h_{n-1}$, an FIR filter is given by $y(t)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}h_i u(t-i)$ for $t\in\mathbb Z$. Its frequency response is $H(\omega)=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}h_k e^{-\jmath\omega k}$. A unit-impulse input yields $y(t)=h_t$ for $0\le t\le n-1$ and zero otherwise, while $u(t)=e^{\jmath\omega_0t}$ yields $y(t)=H(\omega_0)e^{\jmath\omega_0t}$. Moreover, $H$ is $2\pi$-periodic and $H(-\omega)=H(\omega)^*$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An FIR filter convolves a discrete-time signal with a finite coefficient sequence. Its unit-impulse response is that sequence, and a complex exponential is reproduced with scaling given by the frequency response. Real coefficients imply periodicity and conjugate symmetry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: y(t)=\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}h_i u(t-i),\qquad H(\omega)=\sum_{k=0}^{n-1}h_k e^{-\jmath\omega k},\qquad u(t)=e^{\jmath\omega_0t}\Rightarrow y(t)=H(\omega_0)e^{\jmath\omega_0t}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Low-pass FIR band constraints and frequency-grid approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the interval-wide pass-band and stop-band specifications and their approximation by finitely many linear inequalities. The extract's inconsistent logarithmic approximation is excluded.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a linear-phase FIR amplitude response $\widetilde H(\omega)=a(\omega)^\top h$, low-pass specifications with $\delta_s,\delta_p>0$ impose $-\delta_s\le\widetilde H(\omega)\le\delta_s$ for every $\omega\in[\Omega_s,\pi]$ and $1-\delta_p\le\widetilde H(\omega)\le1+\delta_p$ for every $\omega\in[0,\Omega_p]$. Given finite grids $\{\omega_i\}_{i=1}^{N_s}\subset[\Omega_s,\pi]$ and $\{\omega_i\}_{i=N_s+1}^{N_s+N_p}\subset[0,\Omega_p]$, enforcing the corresponding inequalities only at the grid points produces a finite system of linear inequalities in $h$ that approximates, but does not by itself guarantee, the interval-wide constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A low-pass FIR design keeps the amplitude near one in the pass band and near zero in the stop band. The exact specifications contain inequalities at every frequency in the two intervals. Imposing them only on finite frequency grids gives a finite linear system in the filter coefficients, but does not ensure the constraints between grid points.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}-\delta_s&\le a(\omega_i)^\top h\le\delta_s&&i=1,\ldots,N_s,\\1-\delta_p&\le a(\omega_i)^\top h\le1+\delta_p&&i=N_s+1,\ldots,N_s+N_p.\end{aligned}

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes odd-length symmetric real FIR filters through a linear-phase factor and a real amplitude response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $n=2N+1$ and suppose the real impulse response satisfies $h_t=h_{n-1-t}$ for $t=0,\ldots,n-1$. Then, for $\omega\in[0,\pi]$, $H(\omega)=e^{-\jmath\omega N}\widetilde H(\omega)$, where $\widetilde H(\omega)=h_N+2\sum_{t=0}^{N-1}h_t\cos((N-t)\omega)=a(\omega)^\top h$ is real and $|H(\omega)|=|\widetilde H(\omega)|$. If $\widetilde H(0)\ne0$, changing the sign of all coefficients if necessary permits the normalization $\widetilde H(0)>0$.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An odd-length FIR filter whose real impulse response is symmetric about its midpoint has a fixed linear-phase factor and a real amplitude response. The amplitude response is linear in the independent coefficients, and its absolute value equals the frequency-response magnitude. Positive response at zero can be imposed by a global sign change only when that response is nonzero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: H(\omega)=e^{-\jmath\omega N}\widetilde H(\omega),\qquad \widetilde H(\omega)=h_N+2\sum_{t=0}^{N-1}h_t\cos((N-t)\omega)=a(\omega)^\top h\in\mathbb R,\qquad |H(\omega)|=|\widetilde H(\omega)|.

knowledge_statements.title: Antenna-Array Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex minimax synthesis of an array factor from affine steering responses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(w\in\mathbb C^n\) be array weights and \(a(\theta)\in\mathbb C^n\) the steering vector. For desired pattern \(d(\theta)\), weighted minimax synthesis is \[\min_{w,t}\ t\quad\text{subject to}\quad q(\theta)|a(\theta)^*w-d(\theta)|\le t\quad\text{for all }\theta\in\Theta,\] together with affine normalization constraints such as \(a(\theta_0)^*w=1\). Each finitely sampled magnitude constraint is second-order-cone representable because the array factor is affine in \(w\). Continuous angular regions instead give a semi-infinite convex program unless an exact finite robust or polynomial representation is used.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Array-pattern minimax synthesis is convex because each directional response is affine in the weights; sampled magnitude bounds are second-order-cone constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite-angle synthesis is SOCP-representable; continuous-angle synthesis is semi-infinite convex.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{w:|a^*w|\ge\gamma\}\text{ is nonconvex}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvexity of unfixed-phase lower response requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonzero \(a\in\mathbb C^n\) and \(\gamma>0\), the constraint \(|a^*w|\ge\gamma\) is nonconvex: choose \(w_+\) with \(a^*w_+=\gamma\) and let \(w_-=-w_+\). Both \(w_+\) and \(w_-\) are feasible, while their midpoint is not. Convex array models therefore use affine phase-normalized response constraints or convex upper magnitude bounds unless additional structure is introduced.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An unfixed-phase lower bound on array-response magnitude is nonconvex, unlike affine normalization or upper magnitude bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Lower-Magnitude Response Boundary

assumptions_latex: For the closed form and uniqueness, \(R\succ0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: w^*=R^{-1}a_0/(a_0^*R^{-1}a_0)\quad\text{when }R\succ0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Convex quadratic array-weight design with affine look-direction normalization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(R\in\mathbb H_+^n\) be a covariance matrix and \(a_0\in\mathbb C^n\) a nominal steering vector. The design \[\min_{w\in\mathbb C^n}w^*Rw\quad\text{subject to}\quad a_0^*w=1\] is a convex quadratic program. If \(R\succ0\), its unique solution is \[w^*=\frac{R^{-1}a_0}{a_0^*R^{-1}a_0}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Minimum-output-power array design is a convex quadratic program; with positive-definite covariance it has the normalized inverse-covariance solution.

children.title: Robust Filter Design
children.top_down_role: Filter-design templates incorporating bounded uncertainty.

assumptions_latex: \(\|\cdot\|\) is a norm on the complex vector space, hence absolutely homogeneous
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sup_{\|u\|\leq\rho}|\bar e(h,\omega)+q(h,\omega)^*u|=|\bar e(h,\omega)|+\rho\|q(h,\omega)\|_*\).
review_flags: The complex norm-ball assumption is essential; the same formula need not hold for a real uncertainty vector multiplying complex sensitivities.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact robust response bound for complex affine norm-bounded perturbations of a filter error.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For fixed \(\omega\), let \(e(h,\omega,u)=\bar e(h,\omega)+q(h,\omega)^*u\), where \(u\in\mathbb C^p\) ranges over \(U=\{u:\|u\|\leq\rho\}\). Then \[\sup_{u\in U}|e(h,\omega,u)|=|\bar e(h,\omega)|+\rho\|q(h,\omega)\|_*.\] Consequently, the robust magnitude constraint is exactly \(|\bar e(h,\omega)|+\rho\|q(h,\omega)\|_*\leq t\). It is second-order-cone representable when the complex magnitudes and the chosen dual norm have second-order-cone representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complex affine response uncertainty over a norm ball adds the uncertainty radius times the dual norm of the sensitivity to the nominal magnitude error.
knowledge_statements.title: Norm-Bounded Robust Filter Counterpart
Robust Filter Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case convex filter design with an uncertainty-indexed affine response.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(h\in\mathbb C^N\) be filter coefficients, \(u\in U\) an uncertain parameter, and \(H(h,\omega,u)\) affine in \(h\) for every \((\omega,u)\). Given response \(D(\omega,u)\) and nonnegative weight \(W(\omega,u)\), robust minimax design is \[\min_{h,t}\ t\quad\text{subject to}\quad W(\omega,u)|H(h,\omega,u)-D(\omega,u)|\le t\quad\text{for all }(\omega,u)\in\Omega\times U.\] This is a convex semi-infinite program. A finite SOCP or SDP representation requires additional structure in \(U\) and in the uncertain response; replacing the universal constraint by samples generally gives only sampled robustness.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robust filter design minimizes worst-case response error over frequencies and uncertainty; exact finite conic reformulation depends on the uncertainty structure.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The universal worst-case formulation is convex, while finite conic representability requires further structure.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The robust representation fits the leaf and correctly avoids claiming a universal finite conic reformulation, but no source supports the uncertainty-indexed filter model or the exact-versus-sampled robustness distinction.

children.title: Robust Array Design
children.top_down_role: Array-design templates incorporating bounded uncertainty.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \{w:|a^*w|\ge1\}\text{ is nonconvex}.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonconvexity of phase-free robust main-beam magnitude requirements, already present for singleton uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Even for the singleton uncertainty set \(A=\{a\}\) with \(a\ne0\), the phase-free robust constraint \[|a^*w|\ge1\quad\text{for every }a\in A\] is nonconvex: choose \(w_+\) with \(a^*w_+=1\) and let \(w_-=-w_+\). Both weights are feasible, while their midpoint is not. Hence a robust absolute-gain lower bound is not made convex by uncertainty quantification; a phase-fixed real-response specification or other additional structure is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A robust lower bound on absolute array gain is nonconvex without phase fixing, already for a singleton steering set.
knowledge_statements.title: Robust Absolute-Gain Lower-Bound Boundary

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite counterpart for one uncertain steering-vector magnitude upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(w,\bar a\in\mathbb C^n\), \(E\in\mathbb C^{n\times p}\), and \(u\in\mathbb C^p\) with \(\|u\|_2\le1\). For steering uncertainty \(a=\bar a+Eu\), \[\sup_{\|u\|_2\le1}|a^*w|=|\bar a^*w|+\|E^*w\|_2.\] Therefore the robust constraint \(|a^*w|\le t\) for every admissible \(a\) is exactly \[|\bar a^*w|+\|E^*w\|_2\le t,\] which is representable with second-order cones and auxiliary epigraph variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For complex Euclidean-ball steering uncertainty, worst-case response magnitude equals nominal magnitude plus an uncertainty norm, yielding an exact SOCP counterpart.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Complex-Ball Sidelobe Counterpart

assumptions_latex: \(\bar a,w\in\mathbb C^n\), \(E\in\mathbb C^{n\times p}\), and \(u\in\mathbb C^p\).
The nominal response phase is fixed by \(\operatorname{Im}(\bar a^*w)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \inf_{\|u\|_2\le1}\operatorname{Re}((\bar a+Eu)^*w)=\operatorname{Re}(\bar a^*w)-\|E^*w\|_2.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact worst-case real-response formulation under norm-bounded steering error and a nominal phase convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(a=\bar a+Eu\) with \(u\in\mathbb C^p\), \(\|u\|_2\le1\). After imposing the nominal phase convention \(\operatorname{Im}(\bar a^*w)=0\), the robust real-response requirement \[\operatorname{Re}(a^*w)\ge1\quad\text{for every }\|u\|_2\le1\] is equivalent to \[\operatorname{Re}(\bar a^*w)-\|E^*w\|_2\ge1,\qquad \operatorname{Im}(\bar a^*w)=0.\] This is second-order-cone representable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A phase-fixed worst-case real main-beam guarantee under Euclidean-ball steering uncertainty has an exact SOC representation.
knowledge_statements.title: Phase-Fixed Robust Main-Beam Constraint
Robust Array Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case convex array synthesis over steering-vector uncertainty.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(w\in\mathbb C^n\), and let the steering vector at direction \(\theta\) belong to a prescribed set \(A(\theta)\subseteq\mathbb C^n\). Robust sidelobe control has the form \[\min_{w,t}\ t\quad\text{subject to}\quad |a^*w|\le t\quad\text{for all }\theta\in\Theta_s\text{ and }a\in A(\theta),\] with affine main-beam normalization constraints. The feasible set is convex as an intersection of magnitude sublevel sets. For norm-bounded affine steering uncertainty \(a=\bar a+Eu\), \(\|u\|_2\le1\), exact finite conic reformulation may be obtained through appropriate robust-counterpart machinery; arbitrary uncertainty sets can leave a semi-infinite formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robust array synthesis enforces pattern bounds for every admissible steering vector; convexity is retained, but finite conic form depends on uncertainty geometry.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust feasible set is convex; finite conic representability depends on the sets \(A(\theta)\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Far-field beam pattern of a uniform linear antenna array
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives the nominal complex-weight field model and its far-field directional reduction for an equally spaced linear array.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Place $n$ harmonic antenna elements at $p_k=\ell k e_1$ with complex weights $z_k$, wavelength $\lambda$, and angular frequency $\omega$. At $p=ru$, where $\|u\|_2=1$, let $\varphi$ be the angle with the array and assume $r\gg n\ell$. Then $d_k=\|p-p_k\|_2\simeq r+k\ell\cos\varphi$, and the field admits the far-field approximation $E\simeq r^{-1}\operatorname{Re}\!\left(e^{\jmath\omega t-2\pi\jmath r/\lambda}D_z(\varphi)\right)$, where $D_z(\varphi)=\sum_{k=1}^n z_k\exp\!\left(-2\pi\jmath k\ell\cos\varphi/\lambda\right)$. The same weighted-sum diagram describes a receiving linear array after baseband conversion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For an equally spaced linear antenna array observed from a distance much larger than the array aperture, element distances can be linearized. The resulting field separates into a common spherical-wave factor and a directional beam pattern that is linear in the complex element weights. The same beam-pattern formula applies to a receiving array after baseband conversion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: E\simeq\frac1r\operatorname{Re}\!\left(e^{\jmath\omega t-2\pi\jmath r/\lambda}D_z(\varphi)\right),\qquad D_z(\varphi)=\sum_{k=1}^n z_k e^{-2\pi\jmath k\ell\cos\varphi/\lambda}.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertainty-Set Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function interface for robust signal-design constraints with affine uncertainty dependence.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb R^n\) be convex and let \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) be nonempty and closed. A robust design constraint of the form \(\alpha(x)+\langle g(x),u\rangle\leq0\) for every \(u\in\mathcal U\) has the uncertainty-set interface \[\alpha(x)+\sigma_{\mathcal U}(g(x))\leq0,\qquad \sigma_{\mathcal U}(z):=\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\langle z,u\rangle.\] If \(\alpha\) is convex and \(g\) is affine, this interface is convex. Its finite conic realization depends on the representation of \(\mathcal U\) and on whether its support function admits an exact tractable epigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A universally quantified affine uncertainty constraint equals a support-function constraint; tractability is determined by the uncertainty set’s representation.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal U\subseteq\mathbb R^p\) is nonempty and closed.
\(\alpha:X\to\mathbb R\) is convex and \(g:X\to\mathbb R^p\) is affine.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall u\in\mathcal U:\alpha(x)+\langle g(x),u\rangle\leq0\iff\alpha(x)+\sigma_{\mathcal U}(g(x))\leq0\).

notation.meaning: support function of the uncertainty set

assumptions_latex: \(U\) and \(V\) are nonempty subsets of finite-dimensional real vector spaces
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma_{a+AU}(z)=\langle z,a\rangle+\sigma_U(A^Tz)\), \(\sigma_{\lambda U}(z)=\lambda\sigma_U(z)\), \(\sigma_{U+V}(z)=\sigma_U(z)+\sigma_V(z)\), and \(\sigma_{U\times V}(z,w)=\sigma_U(z)+\sigma_V(w)\).
review_flags: Positive scaling is stated for \(\lambda>0\); separately, \(0U=\{0\}\) has zero support, avoiding an undefined product \(0\cdot(+\infty)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Support-function calculus for constructing uncertainty-set interfaces from affine images, positive scalings, sums, and products.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For nonempty sets \(U,V\), a linear map \(A\), translation \(a\), and \(\lambda>0\), \[\sigma_{a+AU}(z)=\langle z,a\rangle+\sigma_U(A^Tz),\qquad \sigma_{\lambda U}(z)=\lambda\sigma_U(z),\] \[\sigma_{U+V}(z)=\sigma_U(z)+\sigma_V(z),\qquad \sigma_{U\times V}(z,w)=\sigma_U(z)+\sigma_V(w).\] Also \(\sigma_{0U}=0\). These extended-real identities pass affine, additive, and block-separable uncertainty descriptions compositionally into robust constraints. If the resulting support value is \(+\infty\) and the deterministic offset is finite, the scalar robust inequality is infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Support functions transform predictably under affine images, positive scaling, Minkowski sums, and Cartesian products, providing a compositional uncertainty-set interface.
knowledge_statements.title: Compositional Support-Function Calculus

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(r_x(\omega_g)\leq\delta-L\eta\ \forall\omega_g\in G\Rightarrow r_x(\omega)\leq\delta\ \forall\omega\in\Omega\).

valid Lipschitz constant for the candidate residual

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe margin converting a finite signal-parameter grid into a continuum-feasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G\subset\Omega\) satisfy \(\sup_{\omega\in\Omega}\min_{\omega_g\in G}d(\omega,\omega_g)\leq\eta\), and suppose the residual \(r_x\) for the candidate design \(x\) is \(L\)-Lipschitz. If \[r_x(\omega_g)\leq\delta-L\eta\quad\text{for every }\omega_g\in G,\] then \(r_x(\omega)\leq\delta\) for every \(\omega\in\Omega\). Without a valid bound \(L\), this tightened-grid certificate is unavailable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A grid certifies a continuous-frequency bound when its sampled residual has a margin equal to a valid Lipschitz constant times the covering radius.
knowledge_statements.title: Lipschitz Grid Certificate

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p(\omega_i)=0\) for every \(\omega_i\in G\), while \(\max_{\omega\in[0,1]}p(\omega)>0\) unless \(G=[0,1]\), which is impossible for finite \(G\).

notation.meaning: continuous nonnegative response missed by the grid

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Explicit continuous-response witness showing that finite samples alone do not certify a continuum bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For any finite grid \(G=\{\omega_1,\ldots,\omega_m\}\subset[0,1]\), the polynomial \[p(\omega)=\prod_{j=1}^m(\omega-\omega_j)^2\] is continuous, vanishes at every sampled point, and is positive at every unsampled point. Thus all sampled inequalities \(p(\omega_j)\leq0\) hold although the continuum inequality \(p(\omega)\leq0\) fails.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite grid can miss a continuous violation: a nonnegative polynomial can vanish at all grid points and be positive between them.
knowledge_statements.title: Finite-Grid Noncertification Witness
Semi-Infinite Signal-Design Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between convex semi-infinite specifications and finite conic signal-design models.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Omega\) be compact, let \(a:\Omega\to\mathbb R^n\) and \(d:\Omega\to\mathbb R\) be continuous, and fix \(\delta\geq0\). The exact signal-design specification \[|a(\omega)^Tx-d(\omega)|\leq\delta\quad\text{for every }\omega\in\Omega\] defines a closed convex feasible set, because it is an intersection of convex constraints. It is nevertheless semi-infinite and need not possess a finite conic representation. Replacing \(\Omega\) by a finite grid yields only an outer relaxation of the exact requirement: feasibility on sampled frequencies does not, without an independent bound or exact elimination theorem, certify feasibility between samples.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous-frequency magnitude specifications are convex but generally semi-infinite; grid feasibility alone does not certify the unsampled frequencies.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{x:|a(\omega)^Tx-d(\omega)|\leq\delta\ \forall\omega\in\Omega\}\) is closed and convex, but finite sampling is generally not exact.

notation.meaning: continuous signal parameter or frequency domain

review_flags: Exact signal-design reference and finite-representation hypotheses are not supplied.

knowledge_statements.title: Norm-Constrained Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct second-order-cone representation of an affine Euclidean-norm design constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(A\in\mathbb R^{m\times n}\), \(b\in\mathbb R^m\), \(c\in\mathbb R^n\), and \(d\in\mathbb R\), the norm-constrained design condition \[\|Ax+b\|_2\leq c^Tx+d\] is equivalent to the Lorentz-cone membership \[(c^Tx+d,Ax+b)\in\mathcal Q^{m+1},\qquad \mathcal Q^{m+1}:=\{(t,z):\|z\|_2\leq t\}.\] Hence the constraint is convex and second-order-cone representable. Cone membership also enforces \(c^Tx+d\geq0\), so no separate sign constraint is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An affine Euclidean-norm upper bound is exactly one Lorentz-cone constraint, including the required nonnegativity of its right side.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\|Ax+b\|_2\leq c^Tx+d\iff(c^Tx+d,Ax+b)\in\mathcal Q^{m+1}\).

knowledge_statements.title: Quadratic-Cone Design
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Rotated-cone representation of a convex quadratic design inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q\in\mathbb S_+^n\) and choose \(L\) with \(Q=L^TL\). The convex quadratic constraint \[x^TQx+q^Tx+r\leq0\] is equivalent, after introducing \(s=-q^Tx-r\), to \[(s,1/2,Lx)\in\mathcal Q_r^{n+2},\qquad \mathcal Q_r^{n+2}:=\{(u,v,z):u\geq0,\ v\geq0,\ 2uv\geq\|z\|_2^2\}.\] Thus every convex quadratic inequality has an exact rotated-second-order-cone representation, with the affine equation defining \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A positive-semidefinite quadratic inequality becomes an affine equation plus one rotated second-order-cone constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x^TQx+q^Tx+r\leq0\iff s=-q^Tx-r\ \text{and}\ (s,1/2,Lx)\in\mathcal Q_r^{n+2}\).
