knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: z\mapsto\log p(e^z)\text{ is convex, and }p(x)\le1\text{ is equivalent to }\log p(e^z)\le0.

notation.meaning: Exponent vector of the j-th generalized monomial.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact logarithmic convexification of a positive-coefficient posynomial, marking the tractable side of the mixed-sign boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p(x)=\sum_{j=1}^m c_j\prod_{i=1}^n x_i^{a_{ij}}\) on \(\mathbb R_{++}^n\), with \(c_j>0\). Under \(x_i=e^{z_i}\), \[\log p(e^z)=\log\!\left(\sum_{j=1}^m\exp(a_j^Tz+\log c_j)\right),\] which is convex in \(z\). Consequently, \(p(x)\le1\) is equivalent to the convex constraint \(\log p(e^z)\le0\). Negative coefficients remove this general log-sum-exp representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Positive-coefficient posynomials become log-sum-exp constraints after logarithmic substitution; mixed signs remove this general convexification guarantee.
knowledge_statements.title: Positive-Coefficient Logarithmic Convexification

children.title: Model Misspecification Boundary
children.top_down_role: Covers divergence between the selected template model and the application mechanism.

assumptions_latex: A robust constraint is designed using a model \(f(x,u)\le0\) and uncertainty set \(U\).
The realized system is governed by \(\widehat f(x,u)\) and uncertainty set \(\widehat U\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The modeled robust guarantee does not imply \(\widehat f(x,u)\le0\) for every \(u\in\widehat U\) unless the true model and uncertainty are covered by the modeled ones.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical limit of robust feasibility under an incorrect constraint map or uncertainty model.

source_refs.locator: 5.6.1 Mixed uncertainty model p. 174

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: The modeled robust feasible set is \(X_U=\{x:f(x,u)\le0\ \text{for all }u\in U\}\), whereas realized feasibility requires membership in \(\widehat X=\{x:\widehat f(x,u)\le0\ \text{for all }u\in\widehat U\}\). Robust feasibility in the model transfers to the realized system only if \(X_U\subseteq\widehat X\). A sufficient coverage condition is \(\widehat U\subseteq U\) together with \(\widehat f(x,u)\le f(x,u)\) for every relevant \(x\) and \(u\in\widehat U\). Without such coverage, \(x\in X_U\) alone supplies no realized robust-feasibility guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robust feasibility protects only against the modeled uncertainty and constraint map; it need not survive an uncovered uncertainty realization or an incorrect system model.
knowledge_statements.title: Model Misspecification Boundary

source_witnesses.locator: 5.6.1 Mixed uncertainty model p. 174

assumptions_latex: The modeled and realized uncertainty sets are both \(\{0\}\).
The modeled and realized constraint maps are \(f(x,0)=-1\) and \(\widehat f(x,0)=1\), respectively.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: X_U=\mathbb R^n,\qquad \widehat X=\varnothing.

notation.meaning: Modeled and realized robust feasible sets.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal witness that constraint-map misspecification can destroy transfer even with exact uncertainty-set agreement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U=\widehat U=\{0\}\), but set \(f(x,0)=-1\) and \(\widehat f(x,0)=1\) for every \(x\). Then every decision is robust feasible for the modeled constraint, whereas no decision is feasible for the realized constraint. Exact agreement of the uncertainty sets therefore cannot compensate for an incorrect constraint map.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even identical modeled and true uncertainty sets provide no protection when the modeled constraint map is wrong.
knowledge_statements.title: Constraint-Map Misspecification Witness

children.title: Uncertainty-Representation Mismatch
children.top_down_role: Covers incompatibility between modeled uncertainty and application-facing variability.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertainty-Representation Mismatch
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Set-containment criterion for transferring a modeled robust constraint to the true uncertainty support.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_{\mathrm{mod}}\) and \(U_{\mathrm{true}}\) be the modeled and true uncertainty sets, respectively, and let \(f(x,u)\le0\) be the uncertain constraint. If a decision \(x\) satisfies \(f(x,u)\le0\) for every \(u\in U_{\mathrm{mod}}\), this modeled robust feasibility certifies the same constraint for every \(u\in U_{\mathrm{true}}\) whenever \(U_{\mathrm{true}}\subseteq U_{\mathrm{mod}}\). If \(U_{\mathrm{true}}\nsubseteq U_{\mathrm{mod}}\), modeled robust feasibility alone imposes no condition at the uncovered realizations and therefore does not certify true robust feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Robust feasibility over the modeled uncertainty set transfers automatically to the true uncertainty set when the true set is contained in the modeled set. If true realizations lie outside the modeled set, the modeled constraint alone does not certify them.
assumptions_latex: The true uncertainty can realize every element of \(U_{\mathrm{true}}\).
The optimization model enforces robustness only over \(U_{\mathrm{mod}}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(U_{\mathrm{true}}\nsubseteq U_{\mathrm{mod}}\), feasibility over \(U_{\mathrm{mod}}\) does not certify feasibility over \(U_{\mathrm{true}}\).

notation.meaning: Constraint function depending on decision and uncertainty.

source_refs.locator: 5.6.1 Mixed uncertainty model p. 174

source_witnesses.locator: 5.6.1 Mixed uncertainty model p. 174

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: f(x,0)\le0\quad\text{but}\quad f(x,1)>0\quad\text{for every }x.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal uncovered-realization witness for uncertainty-set mismatch with an unchanged constraint map.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(U_{\mathrm{mod}}=\{0\}\), \(U_{\mathrm{true}}=\{0,1\}\), and \(f(x,u)=u-\tfrac12\). Every decision satisfies \(f(x,u)\le0\) for all \(u\in U_{\mathrm{mod}}\), but the uncovered true realization \(u=1\) violates the constraint. Thus modeled robust feasibility need not transfer when the true set is not contained in the modeled set.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An uncertainty realization omitted from the modeled set can violate a constraint that is robust feasible over the modeled set.
knowledge_statements.title: Uncovered-Uncertainty Violation Witness

children.title: Robustness Handoff Boundary
children.top_down_role: Covers the transfer limit from mismatch assessment to robustness-oriented treatment.

assumptions_latex: For every uncertainty realization \(u\), the function \(x\mapsto f(x,u)\) is convex.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The robust constraint \(\sup_{u\in U}f(x,u)\le0\) is convex in \(x\), but it belongs to a tractable convex template only when its supremum admits a finite supported representation or oracle.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between abstract convex robust feasibility and finitely representable, computationally tractable robust counterparts.

source_refs.locator: 7.4 Solvable case III: convex quadratic inequality with unstructured norm-bounded uncertainty p. 206
7.5.1 Semidefinite representation of the RC of an uncertain CQI with simple ellipsoidal uncertainty p. 212

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(g(x)=\sup_{u\in U}f(x,u)\). Because a pointwise supremum of convex functions is convex, the robust feasible set \(\{x:g(x)\le0\}\) is convex. This fact alone does not provide a finite conic formulation or an efficient evaluation and separation oracle for \(g\). The application-facing convex template therefore ends at the representability boundary: direct modeling is justified only when the uncertainty structure and dependence of \(f\) yield a supported robust counterpart. Otherwise the model must be handed off to robust-optimization reformulation, approximation, or oracle methods.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A worst-case constraint may be convex yet lack a tractable finite representation; that is the handoff point from ordinary convex templates to specialized robust methods.
knowledge_statements.title: Robustness Handoff Boundary

source_witnesses.locator: 7.4 Solvable case III: convex quadratic inequality with unstructured norm-bounded uncertainty p. 206
7.5.1 Semidefinite representation of the RC of an uncertain CQI with simple ellipsoidal uncertainty p. 212

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Convexity of the pointwise supremum is standard, but the stronger assertion that tractable template membership occurs only with a finite representation or oracle is not formally defined and is not supported by the cited special solvable cases. An authoritative source and a precise computational model are needed for that handoff criterion.

children.title: Exact Relaxation Regime
children.top_down_role: Covers application settings where the relaxation preserves the relevant solution structure.

assumptions_latex: The original feasible set \(S\) is contained in the relaxation set \(R\).
The relaxed objective agrees with the original objective on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation is exact precisely when \(r^*=p^*\); if the relaxed optimum is attained at a point in \(S\), that point is also original-optimal.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Value exactness for a minimization relaxation, with an additional optimizer-recovery criterion.

source_refs.locator: 7 Convex Hulls of Algebraic Sets p. 293
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization problem, let \(p^*=\inf_{x\in S}f(x)\) and let \(r^*=\inf_{z\in R}\widetilde f(z)\), where \(S\subseteq R\) and \(\widetilde f(x)=f(x)\) for \(x\in S\). Then \(r^*\le p^*\). The relaxation is value-exact exactly when \(r^*=p^*\). If, additionally, a relaxed minimizer \(z^*\in R\) exists and satisfies \(z^*\in S\), then \(z^*\) is feasible and optimal for the original problem. Equality of values alone does not require every relaxed optimizer to belong to \(S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A minimization relaxation is exact when its optimal value equals the original value. A relaxed optimizer lying in the original feasible set also recovers an original optimizer.
knowledge_statements.title: Exact Relaxation Regime

source_witnesses.locator: 7 Convex Hulls of Algebraic Sets p. 293
source_witnesses.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

assumptions_latex: The common objective is identically zero.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^*=r^*=0,\qquad 0\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in R}0,\qquad 0\notin S.

notation.meaning: Original feasible set and convex outer relaxation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal witness that value exactness does not imply recoverability of every relaxed optimizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S=\{-1,1\}\), \(R=[-1,1]\), and use the constant objective \(f(x)=0\). The original and relaxed values both equal zero, so the relaxation is value-exact. Nevertheless, \(x=0\) is a relaxed optimizer and is not original-feasible. Hence value exactness does not imply that every relaxed optimizer recovers an original solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A zero value gap can coexist with relaxed optimizers that are infeasible for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Zero Gap Without Universal Optimizer Recovery
knowledge_statements.title: Zero Gap Without Universal Optimizer Recovery

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl[\forall c\in\mathbb R^n,\ \min_{x\in S}c^\top x=\min_{x\in R}c^\top x\bigr]\iff R=\operatorname{conv}(S).

notation.meaning: Original feasible set and convex outer relaxation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural characterization of compact convex outer relaxations that are exact for every linear objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subset\mathbb R^n\) be nonempty and compact, and let \(R\subset\mathbb R^n\) be compact and convex with \(S\subseteq R\). Then \[\min_{x\in S}c^\top x=\min_{x\in R}c^\top x\quad\text{for every }c\in\mathbb R^n\] if and only if \(R=\operatorname{conv}(S)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact convex outer relaxation preserves every linear-objective optimum exactly if and only if it is the convex hull of the original feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Uniform Linear Exactness Characterizes the Convex Hull
knowledge_statements.title: Uniform Linear Exactness Characterizes the Convex Hull

children.title: Nonzero Relaxation Gap Regime
children.top_down_role: Covers application settings where relaxation quality is limited by a nonzero gap.

assumptions_latex: The original feasible set \(S\) is contained in the relaxation set \(R\).
The original and relaxed optimal values are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A strict inequality \(r^*<p^*\) defines a positive relaxation gap \(\Delta=p^*-r^*>0\) and precludes recovery of an original optimum at relaxed value \(r^*\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Positive additive gap for a finite-valued minimization relaxation.

source_refs.locator: 7 Convex Hulls of Algebraic Sets p. 293
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p^*=\inf_{x\in S}f(x)\) be the finite original minimum value and \(r^*=\inf_{z\in R}\widetilde f(z)\) the finite relaxed value, with \(S\subseteq R\) and matching objectives on \(S\). The additive relaxation gap is \(\Delta=p^*-r^*\ge0\). The nonzero-gap regime is the condition \(r^*<p^*\), equivalently \(\Delta>0\). In this regime no original-feasible point can attain objective value \(r^*\), so a relaxed optimizer at that value cannot itself provide an exact original solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxation has a nonzero gap when its lower optimal value is strictly below the original optimum; then no original-feasible point can attain the relaxed value.
knowledge_statements.title: Nonzero Relaxation Gap Regime

source_witnesses.locator: 7 Convex Hulls of Algebraic Sets p. 293
source_witnesses.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: p^*=\tfrac14,\qquad r^*=0,\qquad \Delta=\tfrac14>0.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimal one-dimensional example separating a discrete problem from its convex relaxation by a positive value gap.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \[p^*=\min_{x\in\{0,1\}}\left(x-\tfrac12\right)^2,\qquad r^*=\min_{x\in[0,1]}\left(x-\tfrac12\right)^2.\] Then \(p^*=\tfrac14\), whereas the relaxed minimizer is \(x=\tfrac12\) and \(r^*=0\). Hence \(\Delta=p^*-r^*=\tfrac14>0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relaxing a binary variable to the unit interval produces a strict gap for the squared-distance objective centered at one half.
knowledge_statements.statement_title: Positive Gap from a Fractional Relaxed Minimizer
knowledge_statements.title: Positive Gap from a Fractional Relaxed Minimizer

children.title: Gap Certification Interface
children.top_down_role: Covers application-facing interpretation of evidence about relaxation quality.

assumptions_latex: Certified bounds satisfy \(L_R\le r^*\le U_R\) and \(L_S\le p^*\le U_S\).
The problem is a minimization relaxation, so \(r^*\le p^*\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The relaxation gap satisfies \(\max\{0,L_S-U_R\}\le p^*-r^*\le U_S-L_R\).

notation.meaning: Certified lower and upper bounds on the relaxed optimum.
Certified lower and upper bounds on the original optimum.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Verifiable interval certificate for the additive gap of a minimization relaxation.

source_refs.locator: 7 Convex Hulls of Algebraic Sets p. 293
source_refs.source_title: Semidefinite Optimization and Convex Algebraic Geometry

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(r^*\) and \(p^*\) denote the relaxed and original minimization values. Given independently verifiable bounds \(L_R\le r^*\le U_R\) and \(L_S\le p^*\le U_S\), the gap \(\Delta=p^*-r^*\) obeys \(\max\{0,L_S-U_R\}\le\Delta\le U_S-L_R\). Thus \(L_S>U_R\) certifies a nonzero gap. Exactness is certified when a common value \(v\) is established with \(L_R=U_S=v\), since \(r^*\le p^*\) then forces \(r^*=p^*=v\). Bounds may arise from feasible points, dual certificates, or valid problem-specific lower bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Certified bounds on both optima enclose the relaxation gap. Separated bounds prove a positive gap, while matching relaxed lower and original upper bounds prove exactness.
knowledge_statements.title: Gap Certification Interface
